title: Around the team becomes a Full-timer destination; My Day becomes a skim dashboard
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

My Day tries to be two pages at once.

The top of it is the Attention Feed: **On you** — the things addressed to you or on people you carry — beside **Around the team**, everything else the team has been doing. Below it sits the bento: Next up, the figures, On the horizon, Your prayers, Your sheep, Your week.

#823 reported the visible symptom — "On you" is honestly empty most days while "Around the team" is long, so a one-line card sat beside a tall column and left a blank rectangle. #853 fixed that by making the feed's shape a function of how much there is to show (ADR 0011): on a busy day the feed splits, and My Day *lends* its personal column upward to fill the space beneath the empty "On you".

That fix treated the problem as a width problem. It isn't. Reading **Around the team** and doing your own work are two different activities, and the split forces them to share a screen: when you are catching up on the team you do not need On the horizon or Your prayers in your peripheral vision, and when you are working through your own list you do not need a wall of other people's activity beside it. Worse, the borrow only relocated the ragged edge — the lent column is uncapped while the team column is capped at five rows, so on a typical day the blank rectangle is now under the *team*, not under "On you".

There is a second, quieter cost. Around the team has never had room. It has always been half a column: five rows, single-file, with its team/teammate filters (#727) squeezed into a chip row above it. It is the richest thing the app knows — every person the team touched, who touched them, and what happened — and it has been living in the narrowest space on the page.

## Solution

**My Day becomes what it looks like it is: a skim dashboard of your own work.** "On you" stops being a full-bleed feed section and becomes a bento card among the others, keeping its five-row cap, its "show more", and its "Nothing's waiting on you." line. Beside it sits a small **pointer card** — a count of team activity you have not looked at, and a door.

**Around the team becomes its own destination**, at its own route, for Full-timers. It keeps everything it has today — the team and teammate filters, the new-only filter, per-stack seen and completed state, and the reach affordance on team rows — and finally gets the width to show them properly, paged by day.

This is the shape #646 already settled for "Questions for the team": the page is where the thing lives, My Day keeps a summary that points at it, and there is exactly one read model. It is applied here to the other half of the same feed.

Because the destination is Full-timer-only, a Trainee's My Day now shows their own work and nothing else. That is intended, and it is the one deliberate reduction in this change.

The two-column feed, the shape rule that chose between three layouts, and the borrowed personal column are all deleted. ADR 0011 is superseded: the question it answered — how wide should these two things be — was the wrong question.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer, I want My Day to show only my own work, so that opening it does not immediately hand me everyone else's.
2. As a Full-timer, I want "On you" to sit in the bento as a card like Your sheep and Your week, so that a page I skim has one kind of furniture instead of two.
3. As a Full-timer, I want "On you" to keep saying "Nothing's waiting on you." when it is empty, so that I still get the daily reassurance #823 asked for.
4. As a Full-timer, I want "On you" to keep its five-row cap and "show more", so that a quiet card cannot grow into the wall the bento exists to prevent.
5. As a Full-timer, I want a small card telling me how much team activity I have not looked at, so that I know whether visiting the team page is worth it right now.
6. As a Full-timer, I want that count to be a count of things I have not *seen*, not a count of things that happened, so that it changes when I act and is not the same number every day.
7. As a Full-timer, I want the pointer card to be a door and nothing else, so that I never read team rows in two places with two different behaviours.
8. As a Full-timer, I want "Around the team" to have its own destination in the nav, so that catching up on the team is something I choose to do rather than something that happens to me.
9. As a Full-timer, I want the team page to use the full width, so that a stack that has always been squeezed into half a column can finally show what it knows.
10. As a Full-timer, I want the team/teammate filters carried over intact, so that the work #727 did is not lost in the move.
11. As a Full-timer, I want the new-only filter carried over, so that I can narrow to what I have not opened.
12. As a Full-timer, I want my filter choices written into the URL, so that I can link a teammate the exact view I am looking at.
13. As a Full-timer, I want the URL to drive the filters on load, so that opening a shared link shows what the sender saw.
14. As a Full-timer, I want the back button to undo a filter change, so that the page behaves like a page.
15. As a Full-timer, I want filters *not* remembered between visits, so that a filter I forgot about never makes me think the team has gone quiet.
16. As a Full-timer, I want the page grouped by day, so that "what happened since I last looked" is legible without counting rows.
17. As a Full-timer, I want a day with nothing in it to read as a day with nothing in it, so that quiet is a visible state rather than an absence.
18. As a Full-timer, I want the seen and completed state I already have to carry over, so that rows I have worked through do not come back.
19. As a Full-timer, I want completion to survive the move, so that a team row I acted on — a comment, a question, a follow-up — can still be marked handled.
20. As a Full-timer, I want the reach affordance to survive the move, so that news I can act on is still actionable where I read it.
21. As a Full-timer, I want rows to open the contact the same way they do today, so that the move changes where I read, not what a click does.
22. As a Full-timer, I want the page to say plainly how far back it reaches, so that I do not assume it is an archive and conclude something is missing.
23. As a Full-timer on mobile, I want the same On you card and pointer card as on desktop, so that the two surfaces tell me the same thing about the same day.
24. As a Full-timer on mobile, I want the team page reachable from the pointer card, so that I can get to it without a nav slot that does not exist.
25. As a Full-timer, I want the bottom nav bar left as it is, so that the bar does not shift under me when my role or impersonation changes.
26. As a Trainee, I want My Day to show my own people and my own work, so that the page is about what I am responsible for.
27. As a Trainee, I want no pointer card and no team destination, so that I am not shown a door I cannot open.
28. As a Trainee, I want to keep everything in "On you" — questions to me, mentions, assigned to-dos, my own contacts — so that nothing addressed to me is lost in this change.
29. As a Trainee whose Full-timer mentions me, I want that mention still to land in "On you", so that the direct tie is untouched.
30. As a Trainee, I want "Questions for the team" to keep working as it does, so that this change does not disturb the surface #646 settled.
31. As a screen reader user, I want "On you" to remain a labelled region, so that I can still reach it by landmark.
32. As a screen reader user, I want the pointer card's count announced as part of its link, so that I know what I am navigating to and why.
33. As a screen reader user, I want the team page's day groups to be real headings, so that I can move between days by heading.
34. As any user, I want My Day's layout to be the same every day, so that a page I skim is a page I have memorised.
35. As any user, I want no section of My Day to reflow when I expand another, so that the page never moves under my cursor.
36. As a developer, I want the shape rule and its threshold deleted rather than left unused, so that nobody restores a two-column feed by finding a function that still exists.
37. As a developer, I want the Attention Feed component dissolved rather than given a mode prop, so that the coupling this change removes from the design is also removed from the code.
38. As a developer, I want the partition logic untouched, so that what lands in "On you" versus "Around the team" is not silently redefined by a layout change.
39. As a developer, I want the unseen count exported as a pure function, so that the number on the card is testable without rendering a page.
40. As a developer, I want the route's role floor expressed in the destination list, so that the gate is tested where every other gate is tested.
41. As a developer, I want a Full-timer hitting the route directly and a Trainee hitting it directly to be covered, so that the gate is proven and not assumed.
42. As a maintainer, I want an ADR that supersedes 0011, so that a future reader who finds a deleted shape rule with deleted tests understands it was answered by a page split, not abandoned.
43. As a maintainer, I want the glossary to stop describing a two-part Attention Feed, so that the vocabulary matches what is on screen.

## Implementation Decisions

**The destination.** "Around the team" becomes a route of its own at `/around`, labelled with the phrase the team already says — the label is not renamed. `/around` rather than `/team`, because "team" already means a *group of trainees* in the #727 filters and overloading it would make the route lie. It joins the destination list in the permissions module with a Full-timer floor, and is guarded by the same role-guard wrapper every other gated route uses. No new guard mechanism.

**My Day is furniture-uniform.** The Attention Feed no longer renders on My Day. "On you" becomes a bento card, retaining the collapsed five-row limit, its "show more"/"show less" affordances, its empty copy, and its labelled region. The pointer card is a sibling cell in the same grid, present only for Full-timers; for a Trainee it is absent and the grid closes up around it.

**The pointer's number is a pure function.** A new export in the attention library takes the partitioned team stacks and a seen-predicate and returns the count of unseen ones. It introduces no new persisted state: the existing per-stack seen set already answers the question. The horizon is whatever the existing feed subscription covers — no "since last visit" timestamp is stored, because a stored timestamp would disagree with the dots on the page the first time someone opens it on a second device.

**The shape rule is deleted.** `attentionLayout`, `ATTENTION_LAYOUT_THRESHOLD`, the three layout modes, the personal-column slot prop, My Day's "is the column lent" derivation, the Your sheep / Your week re-pairing, and the multi-up card grid all go, together with their tests. ADR 0011 is superseded by a new ADR.

**The component is dissolved, not parameterised.** The Attention Feed component is split into the On you bento card and the Around the team page. Both are built on the existing worklist card and the existing attention library. No shared component keeps a notion of "two sections" alive — not via a mode prop, not via team-only data passed to the old component.

**The partition is untouched.** What lands in "On you" versus "Around the team", the new-people-first grouping, the Full-timer-only visibility of team-scope threads, and the reach rules are all unchanged. This change moves surfaces; it does not redefine categories.

**Filters become URL state.** Team, teammate, and new-only are read from and written to the query string on the page. They are not persisted per user. The teammate options keep their current source — the roster, so a teammate who has done nothing is still offerable — and the existing "nothing from them" empty state is preserved.

**The page pages by day.** Rows group under day headings, newest first. A day the filters empty out reads as an empty day rather than vanishing.

**The reach is the existing subscription.** The page uses the same live query the feed uses today, with the same document limit. The page is "recent team activity", and the spec says so rather than leaving it to be discovered; a real archive is separate work.

**Mobile follows exactly.** Mobile My Day gets the same On you card and pointer card and loses its inline team section. The bottom nav bar is not changed — it is a fixed four slots around a raised search button, and the pointer card is the only door to the page on mobile. This retires the mobile ordering established in #841 (On you → Around the team → On the horizon), which existed to sequence two things that are no longer on the same page.

**Code vocabulary stays.** The attention library keeps its module name and its `attention*` exports. "Attention Feed" retires as a *glossary term for a screen element*; "attention" remains the right name for what the library computes, and renaming every import inside the change that most needs to be readable is not worth it.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts what a person can observe: an accessible region by name, a link and where it goes, a count rendered on screen, a role seeing or not seeing something, a URL after a click. None of these tests should know a class name, a grid span, or a component's internal state. The ADR-0011 tests are the model to *avoid* re-creating — they pinned a layout decision, and the layout decision turned out to be the wrong abstraction.

Four seams, three of which already exist:

1. **The attention library** (existing unit seam). The new unseen-count function is tested directly over arrays and a stub predicate: none unseen, some unseen, all unseen, and an empty team stack. The existing partition tests stay as they are — they are the guard that this change did not silently redefine the categories. The `attentionLayout` tests are deleted with the function.

2. **The permissions module** (existing seam). One row added to the destination list; the route-access helper is tested for a Full-timer allowed and a Trainee refused. No component renders to prove a role gate.

3. **My Day, desktop and mobile** (existing seams). By accessible role and name: a Full-timer sees the On you card and the pointer card with its count; a Trainee sees the On you card and no pointer; neither sees an "Around the team" region on My Day. The same files hold the demolition guard — On the horizon and Your prayers render exactly once, in the bento, on every day and every count, which is the assertion that the borrow is really gone.

4. **The Around the team page** (the one new seam, proposed at the top: render the page, never its internals). The existing Attention Feed filter tests and reach tests move here largely intact — both behaviours survive the move and should not be re-derived. New coverage: filters read from the URL on load, filters written to the URL on change, day grouping as headings, a filtered-empty day reading as empty, seen and completed surviving a filter change. Prior art for the whole shape is the Questions page's tests — the same stack-becomes-a-page move from #646, rendered under a memory router with the data layer stubbed.

The two-section Attention Feed test file is deleted rather than adapted: it exists to test a component that will not exist.

Coverage thresholds are enforced in CI and must still pass after a net deletion of tests.

## Out of Scope

- **The teammate strip.** A per-teammate row on the page — who has been active, who has been quiet — was considered and deliberately deferred. The data is already available (the roster, and the actors in the stacks), so it is cheap later; landing it here would merge "did the split work?" with "is this summary right?" into one unreviewable change. Worth its own issue once the page exists.
- **Any per-person counts.** If a teammate summary is built later, showing how many people each teammate touched turns a pastoral page into a ranking of Trainees by output. Recency, not volume, and that decision belongs to that issue.
- **Team tallies and "new people this week" figures.** Figures belong on the dashboard My Day now is.
- **An archive.** The page reaches exactly as far as the existing subscription. Dated queries, indexes, and paging beyond that window are separate work, the same shape as #645.
- **Trainee-facing team awareness.** A Trainee losing sight of team activity is an accepted consequence of the Full-timer-only destination, not an oversight. If it proves to be a real loss, the fix is a separate decision about what Trainees should see, not a re-opening of this layout.
- **Renaming the attention library or its exports.**
- **Changes to the partition, the grouping order, the reach rules, or thread-scope visibility.**
- **"Questions for the team" and its My Day stack**, which keep the shape #646 gave them.
- **A design canvas.** Judged unnecessary: with new derivations out of scope, every element on the page already has a rendered form. If the layout section of implementation turns out not to write itself, open a canvas *before* implementing rather than after.

## Further Notes

- Supersedes **ADR 0011** (the Attention Feed's shape as a pure function of two counts). The new ADR should record the trade-off plainly: a shape rule computed from data was a reasonable answer to the wrong question, and the fixed side-by-side pairing that 0011 deliberately gave up is not being restored — it is being dissolved, because the two things are no longer on the same page.
- Directly follows the precedent set in **#646**: when a team-wide surface earns its own destination, My Day keeps a pointer summary and the doing happens in exactly one place, with one read model.
- Related: **#823** and **#853** (the shape rule being superseded), **#727** (the team/teammate filters that move with the page), **#841** (the mobile ordering this retires), **#645** (the archive-shaped follow-up).
- `CONTEXT.md` changes belong in the implementation PR, not before it: **Attention Feed** retires as a term, **On you** is re-cut as a My Day card, and **Around the team** is re-cut as a Full-timer surface. Writing them earlier would make the glossary describe a page that does not exist yet.

title: Opening a person from "Around the team" clears them from the box — only Reviewed should
label: CLOSED
body:
## Symptom

Opening a contact's detail from the **Around the team** box removes that person from the box. The box should behave as an inbox: opening marks the person viewed (dims them, clears the accent dot) but keeps them listed; only pressing **Reviewed** (or the card's fitting verb) should clear them.

## Repro

1. My Day → What's new, with a teammate's person in **Around the team**.
2. Switch the state filter to **New**.
3. Open the person (name or chevron) → the detail opens.
4. Return to My Day → the person is gone from the box ("No recent team touches") — they were merely marked seen, never reviewed.

## Cause

The worklist keeps `seen` and `completed` as separate axes everywhere, but the New view filter drops any row the moment it becomes seen. Opening the person calls `markSeen`, so the act of opening removes the row from the New view — collapsing the two axes back into one gesture, which is exactly what the feed's own design record forbids ("opening something must never make the number go down"; "opened, not finished" is a real state).

## Expected

- Opening the person dims the card (dot gone, "opened, not finished") but never removes them from the box in any view.
- Only the completion verb (Reviewed / Answered / I followed up / Got it) clears a person.
- The New view still narrows to what earlier visits left unopened — it just must not hide a row the reader opened *this visit* (mirror of how completed-this-visit rows are already kept visible for the Undo).

title: Bible study: leaving Present mode returns to the week it was launched from, not the Weeks index
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

A Full-timer opens a week's editor, taps "Show QR", and holds the phone up in the room in Present mode. When the gathering is over they tap the back chevron to pick the phone back up — and land on the Weeks index, the flat list of every week, instead of the week they were just working on. They have to re-find and reopen their week to continue editing. Present mode's only exit is a hardcoded link to the Weeks index that remembers nothing about where it was entered from.

## Solution

Leaving Present mode returns to whoever showed the code. When Present mode was launched from a week's editor, the back chevron returns to that week's editor. When it was launched from the Weeks index, or entered directly (a pasted link, a refresh, an app relaunch), it returns to the Weeks index — never the home page. The QR itself is untouched and still encodes the Entry point's durable URL.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer editing a week, I want to tap "Show QR" in that week's editor, present the code, and then leave Present mode straight back to that same week's editor, so that I can continue working where I left off instead of hunting my week down again on the Weeks index.
2. As a Full-timer on the Weeks index, I want to tap "Show QR" from the Entry point panel, present the code, and leave back to the Weeks index, so that my exit lands on the same screen I launched from.
3. As a Full-timer or viewer who opened Present mode directly (pasted link, page refresh, app relaunch with the mode still open), I want leaving to land on the Weeks index, so that I am never dumped somewhere outside the app or on the home page.
4. As a Full-timer who just created a brand-new week and tapped "Show QR" before publishing anything, I want leaving Present mode to return to that new week's editor, so that creating a week and showing its code is one continuous flow.
5. As a Full-timer whose week was deleted while Present mode was open, I want leaving to land somewhere safe that explains the week is gone and offers the week list, so that a stale target never dead-ends me.
6. As a Full-timer holding the phone in the room, I want the QR shown in Present mode to be identical whether I launched the mode from the index or from a week's editor, so that what students scan never depends on my navigation path.
7. As a viewer holding the phone (the person showing the code is often not a Full-timer), I want Present mode to keep working and leaving to behave predictably, so that handing the phone over is safe.
8. As an authenticated user of the app, I want the Present mode URL's query string to be unable to steer me to arbitrary places in the app or outside it, so that a crafted link can never abuse my session.
9. As a Full-timer who refreshes or reopens Present mode while the code is on screen, I want the return destination to survive the reload, so that my exit is still correct after the page comes back.
10. As a Full-timer switching between several weeks in an evening, I want each Present-mode visit to remember its own week, so that I never end up on the wrong week's editor after presenting two different codes.
11. As a developer reading the docs, I want the glossary's Present mode entry to describe the real exit behavior, so that the documented contract and the shipped behavior never disagree.
12. As a Spanish-language user of the app, I want no new untranslated strings introduced by this change, so that localization is untouched.

## Implementation Decisions

- Present mode's back control is no longer a hardcoded Weeks-index destination. It returns to the week's editor when the Present mode URL carries a return target naming that week; otherwise it falls back to the Weeks index.
- Only the week editor's "Show QR" launcher gains the return target. The Weeks index's "Show QR" launcher is unchanged: its natural return is the index, which is exactly what the fallback already produces — carrying a redundant target would add plumbing with no behavioral difference.
- The return target is validated before use. Meeting ids are slug-shaped (`<study>-<term>-<date>`, letters, digits and hyphens only); the query value is accepted only when it matches that shape, and any other value (including an absolute URL) falls back to the Weeks index. A query string therefore cannot navigate an authenticated holder to arbitrary routes or outside the app.
- The documented invariant survives in both branches: leaving Present mode never lands on the home page. The glossary's Present mode entry is amended to the sender-aware wording ("leaving returns to whoever showed the code").
- New weeks exist as persisted documents before their editor opens, so returning to a just-created week always resolves. A week deleted mid-presentation resolves to the editor's existing "this week doesn't exist" state, which already offers the week list.
- Roles are unchanged: the editor and the Weeks index are Full-timer-only, while Present mode admits viewers (the holder is often not a Full-timer). A viewer can only ever reach Present mode directly, so they always get the index fallback — pre-existing behavior, preserved.
- Direct entry (no return target, or no Entry point parameter) is unchanged from today in every case except one: when the target is present and valid, it wins.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test asserts external navigation behavior only: render the real Present mode view, click the "Leave present mode" control, and assert where the router actually lands. It must not assert on internal plumbing — how the target is built, parameter forwarding, or mocked echoes.
- One seam covers the feature: the route-level component suite of the Present mode view, which renders the view under a router with stubbed sibling routes (the Weeks index, a week editor, and the home page) and clicks the real control.
- The suite must cover three behaviors: direct entry leaves to the Weeks index (existing contract, retained); entry launched from a week's editor leaves to that week's editor and not the index; and a return target that is not a plain meeting id (e.g. an encoded external URL) falls back to the Weeks index.
- Prior art: the same MemoryRouter-plus-stubbed-routes pattern already exists in the sibling suites for the Weeks index and the week editor, and in this suite's long-standing "leaves back to the weeks index, not the home page" test.
- No E2E coverage: existing browser suites do not exercise this path, and the navigation contract is fully asserted at this seam. A browser test would repeat the same assertion more expensively.

## Out of Scope

- Any change to what a QR encodes: it remains the Entry point's durable URL (`/s/<slug>`), never a Meeting, a Study, or the Present mode URL itself.
- Viewer-role landing behavior beyond what exists: a viewer who enters Present mode directly still falls back to the Weeks index, which is a Full-timer-only page — noted, not changed.
- New copy or translation strings: the "Leave present mode" accessible label is unchanged, so no locale work is needed.
- Revisiting the "never the home page" invariant.
- New launchers for Present mode, or per-week "Show QR" entries on the Weeks index itself.
- Multiple Entry points (split-week rooms) beyond what the single Entry point per Study already supports.

## Further Notes

- The glossary (`CONTEXT.md`) Present mode entry is amended to the sender-aware wording as part of this work; the two are a single change.
- The request's "the particular bible study" maps, in domain terms, to the week's editor — the only launcher with a particular-week context. "The index" is the Weeks index.
- Canonical naming: this screen is Present mode; "QR screen" is retired vocabulary.
- Related, closed work: weeks index/editor/Present mode (#856, #857 for #822) and the real scannable QR in Present mode (#861).
- Implementation and tests already exist in the working tree behind this spec; this issue records the decision on the tracker.

title: Bible study: the editor preview themes independently and fills its pane's width
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

After #909/#916 shipped, the editor's Live Preview phone has two failures for a Full-timer writing a week.

**Light mode is not working.** The preview's Dark/Light toggle swaps an attribute and the wrapper's background colour, but the reader inside the phone resolves its palette from the app's own theme scope on the document root — and the only reader rule keyed to the preview's attribute is the dark one. In a dark app the "Light" phone still renders the dark ground and cards, so flipping the toggle appears to do nothing; in a light app the Dark default fails the same way in reverse. The closed-issue promise that the toggle "themes the frame independently of the app's own theme" was never actually implemented — only the DOM attribute flips.

**The phone is smaller than it should be.** The scale takes the smaller of the pane's width and height ratios so the phone is always whole, which on a short laptop window leaves the phone at roughly 0.6 scale in a fixed-width pane with wide empty gutters on either side — type too small to proofread, which is the preview's entire job.

The author wants the phone to fill the pane's width instead, keeping the phone's ratio, accepting that the phone will then be taller than the pane on short windows and that the preview will scroll.

## Solution

- Preview Light and Dark both truly re-theme the reader interior, independently of the app's own theme, by making the phone a scoped theme host: the host carries the same light/dark class and theme attribute the app puts on the document root, the light palette applies to a nested light scope, and the reader's card-on-ground pair swap gains a scoped light mirror. No new colour tokens; the two shipped themes stay the single source of values.
- The phone fills the pane's width at its ratio (capped at true phone size). On windows where the phone is then taller than the pane, the preview column scrolls — the phone and the Present-mode handoff row scroll together beneath a pinned "Live Preview" caption and Dark/Light toggle; when the phone fits, the Present row sits at the bottom of the pane as today.
- ADR 0014 §11 is amended to record the width-fill scroll model, the independent-theming mechanism, and the rejected branches.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer writing a week, I want the preview's Light toggle to render a genuinely light phone, so that I can check the theme a student in a bright room gets.
2. As a Full-timer writing in a dark app window, I want the Light preview to look different from the Dark preview, so that the toggle is not a lie.
3. As a Full-timer writing in a light app window, I want the Dark preview to render a genuinely dark phone, so that the default state is truthful too.
4. As a Full-timer, I want the light preview's card to sit on its ground exactly as it does on a real light phone (ground takes the panel tone, card the background tone, layered shadow), so that what I approve is what the room gets.
5. As a Full-timer, I want the phone to fill the width of the preview pane at its natural ratio, so that the type is large enough to proofread.
6. As a Full-timer on a short laptop window, I want the width-filling phone to scroll within the preview when it is taller than the pane, so that I read at near-true size instead of a shrunken still.
7. As a Full-timer, I want the "Live Preview" caption and the Dark/Light toggle to stay pinned while the phone scrolls, so that I can flip themes without scrolling back to the top.
8. As a Full-timer, I want the Present-mode handoff row to stay reachable, so that grabbing the entry-point URL is not a hunt.
9. As a Full-timer on a tall window, I want the whole phone visible with no scroll, so that I can still judge a Section at a glance.
10. As a Full-timer, I want the phone never blown up past true size, so that I am judging real dimensions.
11. As a Full-timer, I want moving my caret into a Section to bring that Section into the preview exactly as it does today, so that the width-fill and theming changes do not disturb proofreading.
12. As a Full-timer, I want a Blank revealed in the preview to stay revealed while I keep writing, so that reader state survives these changes.
13. As a Full-timer, I want scrolling the preview never to move my cursor, so that inspecting the end of the week does not interrupt a sentence.
14. As a Full-timer, I want the preview to keep reflecting markdown typed but not saved, so that the one rendering path (ADR 0013 §3) is unchanged.
15. As a future maintainer, I want the record to say why the preview scrolls again on short windows and why the frame themes itself through a scoped host, so that the reversal reads as a decision rather than a regression.

## Implementation Decisions

Decisions from the grilling session; all recommended branches accepted.

- **Scoped theme host (the Light fix).** The reader's palette resolves the app's CSS custom properties from the document root, so an attribute alone cannot re-theme it. The preview host becomes a theme island: it carries the light/dark class and the theme data attribute exactly as the app's theme provider applies them to the document. The light palette's root rule also matches a nested `.light` element, so the host takes the light values inside a dark app (dark already applies by class). The reader's card-on-ground pair swap gains a light-scoped mirror of the dark rule — the same two pair-swap values as the shipped light block, no new colour tokens, ADR 0014 §5 physics untouched — ordered so it wins inside a light island inside a dark app. This also fixes the symmetric failure: the Dark default inside a light app.
- **Attribute-only theming is recorded as the rejected branch** — it is what shipped, and it renders the preview in the app's own theme, which is the reported bug.
- **Width-fill scale.** The phone's scale follows the pane's width: the smaller of 1 and width ÷ 390, with the existing legibility floor retained. The height ratio no longer binds; a phone taller than the pane is expected and handled by scrolling. The phone is never blown up past true size.
- **One scroller, pinned caption.** The preview column keeps a fixed caption row ("Live Preview" + the Dark/Light toggle). Beneath it, a single scroll region holds the phone and the Present-mode handoff row: the phone sits top-aligned (centred when it fits) and the Present row carries the bottom margin that pins it to the region's bottom when the phone is short and lets it follow the phone when the phone overflows. Exactly one new scroller; the reader's own deck remains the only scroller inside the phone.
- **Reversal recorded.** #909/#916's "the phone is always whole" and "the pane never scrolls" acceptance rules are rejected for short windows: proofreading type at near-true size beats seeing the whole phone at once, and the re-admitted pane scroll — the reader's sticky chrome can leave view while the phone's lower Sections are inspected — is the accepted cost. Amends ADR 0014 §11.
- **Column width unchanged.** The preview column stays at its fixed width (~0.89 scale typical). Widening it so the phone can reach true size inside it is rejected: it squeezes the writing pane on small laptops for a few percent of scale.
- **Defaults and behaviour unchanged.** The preview still opens on Dark. Preview state (scroll position, revealed Blanks, caret following) and one-way tracking are untouched. No Meeting/schema change — `md` remains the single source of truth (ADR 0012, ADR 0013 §5). The editor stays desktop-only and the preview stays hidden below the desktop breakpoint.

## Testing Decisions

A good test asserts what a Full-timer observes — that the Light preview actually selects the light theme, that the frame's box follows the width-fill scale, that toggling does not remount the reader. Pixel geometry is not assertable in jsdom, which has no layout; a test that asserted a scale factor or a computed size would be asserting the implementation (the #909 note). Class-name and render-count assertions are not behaviour.

- **Seam 1 — the pure scale helper (existing bible-study unit seam).** Width-fill is a pure function. Tests replace the current whole-phone suite: the width binds and the height no longer does; the scale caps at 1; the legibility floor holds. Prior art: the existing previewScale unit suite.
- **Seam 2 — the BibleStudyEditor view seam (existing).** Choosing Light puts the light scope on the preview host (observable theme state, not paint); the frame's box is sized by the width-fill scale; the reader is not remounted by a theme change. The existing caret-following, revealed-Blank-persistence, one-way-tracking and unsaved-markdown cases stay green as the guard that nothing else moved. Prior art: the editor preview suites from #909/#920.
- **Seam 3 — the reader card-on-ground guardrail (existing CSS-text guardrail, #922/#934 precedent).** Extended to pin the light-scoped mirror of the pair swap and the palette's nested-light membership, and to keep asserting that no new colour tokens appear.
- **Not covered by any automated seam.** The scroll model, the pinned caption and the phone's fit are layout facts; jsdom has no layout. Verification is browser inspection of the editor at a laptop-sized window and a tall one, across both app themes × both preview themes — the #916 precedent.

## Out of Scope

- Widening the preview column (rejected above).
- Any change to the reader itself — the deck, panels, peek, Blanks, the type-size control, or the card physics beyond the scoped mirror.
- Present mode, the QR and the entry-point flow.
- Editing a Meeting on a phone; the preview stays hidden below the desktop breakpoint.
- The toolbar caret-jump feedback, specified separately.
- Updating the `docs/design/bible-study` artboards, already a recorded follow-up from #890.
- Any Meeting schema or `md` format change.

## Further Notes

- The bug shipped because #909 said the toggle "themes the frame independently of the app's own theme" and the implementation only swapped an attribute and inline colours while the reader's palette is scoped to the app's document root — so nothing inside responded. The same root cause fails the Dark default in a light app.
- The ADR 0014 §11 amendment ships with the change. CONTEXT.md needs no new terms: Entry point, Study, Meeting, Section, Passage, Prompt and Blank keep their meanings.

title: Bible study: the student sets the type size
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#912

## What to build

Body text is set larger by default, and a student can change it.

The type is genuinely small — and the editor preview has been hiding that, rendering a step larger on desktop than on a phone, so a Full-timer approving a week has been judging the generous version of it. A student in the back row of a gathering, holding a phone, gets the smaller one and has no way to ask for anything bigger.

Raise the default, and put a control in the reader's chrome offering a small range of sizes, persisted in that student's browser storage. Prompt and title sizes derive from the body size so the page stays in proportion at any setting.

Deliberately **not** a field on the Meeting. `md` is the single source of truth and holds the week's text, not its presentation (ADR 0012, ADR 0013 §5), and an author cannot know a reader's eyesight or phone in any case. The person who cannot read it is the person who can fix it, with no author involvement and nothing stored on the document.

The card's internal inset stays constant across sizes. Scaling it down at larger type — the card's side padding costs reading width exactly when type is largest — was considered and is deliberately deferred, not shipped. Revisit if the measure proves uncomfortable at the top of the range.

Expect overflow to become substantially more common: Sections that fit today will not fit at the new default, and more still will overflow for a student who increases the size. That is expected, and is why the overflow treatment was settled before the default was raised.

A stored size that cannot be read falls back to the default rather than erroring, following the precedent set by the reader's Blank state and the editor's dismissed-card persistence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Body text renders at the raised default with no stored preference
- [ ] A text-size control is present in the reader and offers the agreed range
- [ ] Choosing a size records it in that browser's storage and applies it immediately
- [ ] A reader returning with a stored size applies it on mount
- [ ] A stored size that cannot be read falls back to the default without erroring
- [ ] One student's choice does not change what any other student sees
- [ ] Prompts, passages and Section titles scale in proportion with the body size
- [ ] Every Section still renders all its blocks at every size in the range
- [ ] A Section that no longer fits at a larger size scrolls normally, keeping its card
- [ ] Nothing is written to the Meeting; no schema change
- [ ] The card's internal inset is unchanged across sizes
- [ ] Covered at the existing `StudyReaderView` seam for the control, persistence and fallback — the layout consequences are browser-verified
- [ ] No new test seam is introduced

## Blocked by

- Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#915 — the viewport-keyed size pairs must be collapsed before a single scale can drive the type.
- Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#922 — raising the default makes overflow common, so the overflow treatment must exist first.

title: Bible study: a Section reads as a card on ground, in both themes
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#912

## What to build

A short Section stops reading as a small thing marooned on a large screen.

Most Sections in a real week are short — a point, a Passage, a Prompt — and each one currently clings to the top of the panel with an empty band beneath it. ADR 0014 §5 removed vertical centring to fix exactly this, and did not: it correctly identified dead space as the problem but treated centring as the cause, so top-aligning only relocated the emptiness from above-and-below to entirely below.

Put the Section's content on a raised card and let the panel around it become ground, so the same emptiness reads as margin around an object rather than a void. While the content fits, it settles optically in the panel, framed above by air and below by the peek — which stays outside the card, so the trailing space is bounded at both ends. The settling is continuous: as content grows the offset shrinks to zero, so nothing jumps at the threshold.

When a Section overflows, **the card grows** — one continuous surface running past the fold and closing below the last block. Dropping the card on overflow was considered and rejected: it is discontinuous, so a Section a line either side of the threshold looks entirely different and can flip on a rotation; and combined with the reader-side type control it would hand the plainest treatment to the readers who chose the largest type. The cost is accepted and stated — mid-scroll through a long card no edges are visible, so the object reading weakens exactly when a Section is long.

The two themes elevate by different physics. The app's light theme fills cards with the panel tone on a white ground and sets no card shadow, which would render this card *darker* than its ground — a recess, not an object. For the reader, swap the pair: the panel ground takes the panel tone, the card takes the background tone, and light elevation comes from a layered shadow, while dark keeps elevating through lightness plus an edge, because shadow is invisible on near-black. No new colours; both themes use tokens the app already ships.

This is a deliberate local departure from the app's flat light-mode cards, and it changes the reader's light background from white to the panel tone. It is scoped to the reader: every other light-mode card in the app stays flat and the app-wide card shadow token is not touched. The justification is that the reader is its own surface — most people who see it arrive by scanning an Entry point QR at a gathering and never open the tracker.

Amend ADR 0014 §5, saying plainly that the dead space was the problem and centring was not the cause, with top-align recorded as the rejected branch. Otherwise the next reader of §5 and the shipped code will assume one of them is a mistake.

The card treatment and its alternatives were chosen from a live comparison at true phone dimensions in both themes; the rejected branches were plain top-align, settle without a card, and card without settling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Section's content sits on a card with radius, internal padding and elevation; the panel is ground
- [ ] Content that fits settles optically in the panel rather than clinging to the top
- [ ] The peek sits outside the card at the bottom of the panel
- [ ] A Section that overflows keeps its card, which grows and closes below its last block
- [ ] The settling offset shrinks continuously to zero as content grows — no jump at the threshold
- [ ] In light, the card is lighter than its ground and carries a layered shadow
- [ ] In dark, the card stays lighter than its ground with an edge
- [ ] Prompt surfaces read as insets within the card, not as further raised objects
- [ ] No new colour tokens are introduced, and the app-wide card shadow token is unchanged
- [ ] Every other light-mode card in the app is visually unchanged
- [ ] ADR 0014 §5 is amended, with top-align recorded as the rejected branch and the reasoning stated
- [ ] Verified in the browser at emulated phone sizes in both themes and on a real iPhone — covering a short Section, one that overflows only at the largest type, and one that overflows at every size

## Blocked by

- Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#913 — settling is measured against the panel, so the panel must be sized correctly first.

title: Bible study: Passage inserts bare, and block inserters land in the caret's Section
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#911

## What to build

The toolbar stops inserting text the author has to delete, and puts blocks where the author is actually writing.

Two changes to the insertion path.

**Passage inserts a bare quote.** The button currently writes a two-line template with a placeholder reference the author usually deletes, even though a Passage with no citation is valid and already renders correctly — the parser treats a single-line blockquote as a Passage without one. This is editor-side only, and it brings Passage in line with the principle ADR 0014 §9 already settled for "+ Add section": an inserted thing carries no starter text the author must remove. A citation is added by typing one.

**Block inserters append to the end of the caret's Section**, separated from what came before by exactly one blank line, whatever the document was terminated with. Today they write at the caret, splitting whatever line the author is mid-way through and leaving inconsistent whitespace.

Note this deliberately departs from the literal request, which was the end of the *document*. A Prompt, a Passage and a Verse all live inside a Section, so appending to the document end would file them under the last Section while the author writes the second — the same class of silent misplacement ADR 0014 §9 fixed for Sections one level up. The end of the caret's Section delivers everything the request was after: no cursor guesswork, no split lines, a visible result. With the caret outside any Section, fall back to the end of the document. Scroll to the insertion and leave the caret ready to type, as "+ Add section" does.

Inline inserters — bold, italic, Blank — are unchanged and keep wrapping at the caret. Only block-level items move.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Passage inserts a quote with no reference line
- [ ] A Passage with no citation still parses and renders correctly
- [ ] Clicking a block inserter with the caret in an early Section appends to the end of *that* Section, not the document
- [ ] Exactly one blank line separates the inserted block from the preceding content, regardless of how the document was terminated
- [ ] A block insertion never splits the line the caret is in
- [ ] With the caret outside any Section, the block lands at the end of the document
- [ ] The editor scrolls to the insertion and leaves the caret ready to type
- [ ] Inline inserters still wrap at the caret
- [ ] The helper reporting where a block insertion belongs is covered at the pure mirror seam
- [ ] No new test seam is introduced

## Blocked by

- Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#917 — both rewrite the insertion path, and this is cleaner applied on top of the fixed focus and scroll handling.

title: Bible study: the preview follows the caret instead of restarting
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#909

## What to build

The preview follows the author's caret instead of restarting.

#897 asked for the preview to scroll to the Section being written. What ships does something else: the preview is keyed on the caret's Section index, so React discards and rebuilds the reader on every change — a fresh reducer starting at the first Section, a fresh scroll container at the top, an empty Blank map. So every caret move resets the preview to Section 1 rather than moving it to the caret's Section, and any Blank the author had tapped open is wiped. Proofreading the Section you are writing means scrolling the preview back down after every keystroke that crosses a boundary.

Remove the key. Have the reader accept the Section the preview should be showing and scroll to that panel when it changes, reusing the same scroll-to path the Section index already uses. Reader state — scroll position, revealed Blanks — persists across edits.

Tracking stays strictly one-way. Nothing in the reader writes back to the editor's selection: a scroll that yanked the cursor mid-sentence would be hostile.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Moving the caret into a Section scrolls the preview to that Section, not to the first one
- [ ] The reader is not remounted on a caret move — a Blank revealed in the preview stays revealed after an edit elsewhere in the document
- [ ] The preview's scroll position survives an edit
- [ ] Scrolling the preview does not change the textarea's selection
- [ ] The preview still reflects markdown typed but not saved
- [ ] Asserted through observable state at the existing `BibleStudyEditor` seam, not render counts
- [ ] No new test seam is introduced

## Blocked by

- Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#914 — the scroll-to path this uses is dead until the panel refs are wired.

title: Bible study: Apply becomes a fourth kind of Prompt
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#911

## What to build

A Full-timer can mark an Apply prompt — the part of a study where the room names what they will actually do.

Prompts come in three kinds today: Question, Discuss and Activity. The move a study makes at the end has no marker, so it is written as plain prose and reads as plain prose. Reported from the field as "need an apply in bible study editor" (#905).

Apply joins the prompt-kind union, the prompt line grammar and the renderer's colour mapping, in both parser mirrors and the parity corpus per ADR 0013 §5. It takes the ochre tone from the existing palette, which reads warm against the sage, clay and slate already in use without colliding with any of them.

`CONTEXT.md`'s **Prompt** entry currently says "one of three kinds" and lists "application" among the words to avoid. It becomes four kinds, and "application" is struck — the model said "application" was a wrong word for Prompt, and it turned out to be a real distinction the model had not yet made.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Apply:` parses to a Prompt of that kind, case-insensitively, alongside the existing three
- [ ] An Apply prompt renders as a prompt with its own label and the ochre tone
- [ ] The toolbar offers Apply alongside Question, Discuss and Activity
- [ ] The kind is implemented in both parser mirrors, and corpus fixtures containing Apply prompts produce deep-equal results from both
- [ ] `CONTEXT.md`'s Prompt entry says four kinds and no longer lists "application" as a word to avoid
- [ ] No new test seam is introduced
- [ ] Closes #905

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Bible study: Verse becomes its own block, with the reference leading
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#911

## What to build

A Full-timer can write a Verse: scripture where the reference leads and the words follow at body size, sitting in the flow of the Section rather than pulling out of it.

Today there is one way to put scripture on a page. A Passage sets the words large with the citation trailing underneath, which is right for a text the room dwells on and wrong for a proof-text glanced at mid-thought — "Rom. 5:6 — while we were still weak…", where the reference leads because the reference is the point. Authors writing those get a pulled-out quotation whether they want one or not.

Verse is its own block kind, not a display flag on Passage. The stored data is the same shape either way, so this was a real choice: it goes to two blocks because the *reading* is genuinely different, and collapsing them would put a rendering decision inside a document model whose discipline is that a Section reads as the author wrote it.

Verse takes its own unambiguous prefix. A leading-reference line inside a blockquote is not distinguishable from a two-line Passage, and detecting "looks like a book, chapter and verse" is explicitly rejected — it is fragile, and it would silently reclassify existing Passages whose first line happens to match.

The grammar lands in both parser mirrors and joins the parity corpus, per ADR 0013 §5.

`CONTEXT.md` gains a **Verse** entry. **Passage** currently lists "Verse" among the words to avoid, on the understanding that it was a wrong word for Passage; amend that, and sharpen Passage's definition to say the citation is subordinate and trailing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Verse line parses to a Verse block with its reference and text separated
- [ ] A blockquote still parses to a Passage — last line as citation when multi-line, no citation when single-line
- [ ] A line that merely looks like a scripture reference is not reclassified as a Verse
- [ ] A Verse renders with its reference leading, at body size, in the flow — visibly distinct from a Passage
- [ ] Inline emphasis and Blanks work inside a Verse
- [ ] The toolbar offers Verse alongside Passage
- [ ] The grammar is implemented in both parser mirrors, and corpus fixtures containing Verses produce deep-equal results from both

title: Bible study: a toolbar click stops throwing the author back to the top
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#910

## What to build

Clicking a toolbar button stops throwing the author back to the top of the document.

A Full-timer writing partway down a long week clicks Passage — or Blank, or bold, or a Prompt — and the textarea scrolls to the beginning. The insertion lands correctly, but the author has lost their place. It happens on every block-inserting button, every time, which makes the toolbar unpleasant on exactly the weeks long enough to need it.

**Diagnose in the browser before fixing.** Two mechanisms are plausible and they call for different fixes: either the button takes focus on mousedown so the textarea is blurred when its value is replaced — a programmatic value assignment on an unfocused textarea resets scroll, and the later refocus restores the caret but not the scroll — or the deferred refocus races the controlled re-render and applies the selection against a stale value. Reproduce first, at the reported 1107x662 viewport, on a week long enough to scroll; a large monitor may not show the symptom at all.

Then fix it two ways, both cheap and compatible: suppress the mousedown focus shift so the field never blurs, the standard arrangement for a formatting toolbar over a text field; and capture the scroll offset before the value changes and restore it after the selection is set, so the fix does not depend on browsers agreeing about when a value assignment resets scroll. Where the insertion is off screen, scroll to the caret rather than leaving it invisible — the author must see that the click did something.

Both edit paths must be covered. The editor writes through one path that routes through the replicated document when live collaboration is connected and local state otherwise; the handling belongs on that shared path so behaviour is identical with or without a second Full-timer in the document.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The symptom is reproduced in a browser before any fix, and the cause recorded on the issue
- [ ] Clicking any toolbar button leaves the document scroll position unchanged
- [ ] The textarea retains focus across a toolbar click
- [ ] An insertion outside the visible range scrolls to the caret rather than the top
- [ ] A previously selected run stays selected between wrapping markers; a collapsed caret lands between them
- [ ] Behaviour is identical whether or not live collaboration is connected
- [ ] The outline still highlights the caret's Section after an insertion, and autosave is still scheduled
- [ ] Verified in the browser at 1107x662 on a week long enough to scroll — jsdom reports a scroll offset of zero, so no automated test can prove this
- [ ] Closes #906

title: Bible study: the editor preview becomes a phone that fits its pane
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#909

## What to build

The editor preview becomes a phone that fits its pane.

Three symptoms, one cause: a CSS transform is paint-only, so scaling a full-size phone inside a wrapper sized to the *unscaled* phone leaves the layout box full size while the picture shrinks. That is the empty band along the bottom inside the bezel, the empty slivers down both sides, and the frame overflowing a pane narrower than it — all from the same mistake. The bezel is drawn around a phone that is not where the picture is.

Size the outer box to the scaled dimensions and keep the inner box at true phone dimensions scaled from its top-left corner, so layout and paint agree, and move the bezel, border and shadow onto the box that matches the picture. Drive the scale from a `ResizeObserver` on the pane rather than the current fixed constant, which fits no pane correctly including the one it was picked for; take the smaller of the width and height ratios so the phone is always whole, with a lower bound so it stays legible.

Then stop the pane scrolling: the phone takes the height genuinely available and the Present mode panel sits beneath it as a row. The only scroller in the preview should be the reader's own deck — the thing under test. Today the pane scrolls instead, which pushes the reader's sticky header and progress rail out of sight, the two pieces of chrome the preview exists to let you check.

Leave a brief comment at the frame recording why the outer box is pre-multiplied; the arrangement looks redundant to anyone who does not know that transforms do not affect layout, and simplifying it back to one box reintroduces this bug exactly.

ADR 0014 §11 needs no amendment. This is what "CSS-scaled into the pane" always meant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The frame's layout box matches its painted size — no dead band inside the bezel, no slivers at the sides
- [ ] The bezel, border and shadow hug the screen they frame
- [ ] Neither axis of the preview pane scrolls, and no horizontal scrollbar appears
- [ ] The scale is measured from the pane and updates on resize, keeping the phone whole
- [ ] The reader's sticky header and progress rail are visible without scrolling the pane
- [ ] The Present mode panel sits beneath the phone and is reachable without a long scroll
- [ ] Scrolling inside the frame scrolls the reader
- [ ] The dark/light preview toggle still works
- [ ] A comment at the frame records why the outer box is pre-scaled
- [ ] Verified in the browser at a laptop-sized window and a large one — jsdom has no layout, so no automated test can prove this

## Blocked by

title: Bible study: the preview stops rendering type a step larger than the phone

## What to build

The editor preview stops showing type one step larger than a phone does.

Reader components set two sizes per element and choose between them with a viewport-width breakpoint. Inside the editor preview that breakpoint reads the desktop window rather than the 390px frame, so the preview always renders the larger of each pair — body text, prompts and Section titles alike. A Full-timer approving a week has been judging a more generous version of it than the room gets.

Replace the breakpoint-selected pairs with a single size per element, driven by the reader's own type scale. This is a prerequisite for the reader-side type control, and it is a general hazard worth removing: any responsive rule inside the preview's scaled frame reads the desktop window and has the same bug latent in it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Body text, prompt text and Section titles render at one size, not a viewport-selected pair
- [ ] The editor preview and a real 390px phone render the same sizes

title: Bible study: the scroll drives the counter, the rail and the Section index
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#908

## What to build

The counter, the progress rail, the Section index and the peek all start working.

All four are inert today, from one cause: the reader keeps an array of panel elements to observe and to scroll to, and that array is never populated — the panel is rendered by a component that accepts no ref and is given none. So the `IntersectionObserver` is never constructed (the observe loop finds nothing to observe) and `jump`'s `scrollIntoView` is called on nothing. The result is a counter frozen at `01`, a rail that never fills, an index whose rows do nothing, and a peek that does nothing.

Wire the refs, then fix the guard sitting behind them: the observer callback compares against the Section index captured when the observer was built, and because the observer is rebuilt only when the Section count changes, that value stays at its initial value for the life of the Meeting — so scrolling back to the first Section can never re-register. Read current state rather than a closed-over copy, while keeping the observer's subscription lifecycle keyed to the Section count so it is not torn down and rebuilt on every scroll tick.

Both halves ship together deliberately: wiring the refs alone gives a counter that climbs and never comes back down, which is half a behaviour rather than a shippable one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The panel component accepts a ref and the call site supplies one
- [ ] The counter names the Section currently on screen, and decreases when scrolling back up
- [ ] The progress rail fills as the reader advances and unfills on the way back
- [ ] Tapping a row in the Section index scrolls the deck to that Section
- [ ] Tapping the peek scrolls the deck to the following Section
- [ ] The Section index highlights the Section currently on screen
- [ ] The observer is not rebuilt on every scroll tick
- [ ] Covered at the existing `StudyReaderView` seam by asserting the correct panel was asked to scroll into view — jsdom stubs `scrollIntoView` and has no layout, so the assertion is about which panel was asked, not that the browser moved
- [ ] No new test seam is introduced

title: Bible study: a Section comes to rest — size a panel to the deck, not the viewport
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#908

## What to build

A Section comes to rest when a student scrolls to it.

Today no Section can settle. Panels are sized against the browser viewport, but the box they snap inside is the scroll container — which is shorter than the viewport by the height of the sticky header and the sticky progress rail. Every panel is therefore taller than the box it snaps in, so no `start` snap position is reachable, and the deck parks wherever the finger left it: scroll a little past the header and the Section title is cut in half and stays that way.

Size a panel to the scroll container instead. Keep `min-height` semantics so a Section longer than the deck still overflows and scrolls normally, and keep proximity snapping for the reason ADR 0014 §1 gives — mandatory snapping can skip or trap on a Section taller than the viewport.

Amend ADR 0014 §1 for the panel height. The decision it records is unchanged and correct; only the stated measurement was wrong, and it was wrong in a way that stopped the decision from ever taking effect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Section panel is sized to the reader's scroll container, not to the browser viewport
- [ ] Scrolling a short distance into a Section settles on that Section with its title fully visible
- [ ] A Section longer than the deck still scrolls normally and snaps only at its boundary
- [ ] Proximity snapping is retained; snapping is not made mandatory
- [ ] The empty-Meeting placeholder is sized the same way as a panel
