title: Bible study: record the reader and editor decisions (ADR 0014, amend 0012 and 0013)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker#890

## What to build

The records for the Bible study reader and editor rework, so that a future maintainer finds decisions rather than oversights. No code changes.

ADR 0014 covers two decisions made together: the reader's navigation model (a scroll-snap deck, scroll owning position) and the editor's shape (one document with a navigating outline, Sections still derived from `md`). Its rejected alternatives are on record: for the reader, a deck with swipe gestures and a plain continuous document; for the editor, Sections as stored documents and a section-stack pane showing one Section at a time. It also records two deliberate omissions with their costs — reorder and delete have no UI (cut-and-paste is the mechanism), and distraction-free mode is deleted rather than kept idle.

ADR 0012 is amended in place: `md` remains one string and the single source of truth, so §3's `Y.Text`-to-textarea binding target is the whole-document textarea; the desktop-only scope is reaffirmed. The autosave and collaboration work itself is unaffected and remains unbuilt.

ADR 0013 gains a note that the preview and the reader are now literally one component, making its §3 requirement structural rather than a convention.

`CONTEXT.md` is deliberately untouched — Entry point, Study, Meeting, Section, Passage, Prompt and Blank all still mean what they meant, which is the evidence the domain model held under this change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ADR 0014 exists, follows the repo's ADR format, and is Accepted
- [ ] ADR 0014 records the reader navigation decision with deck-with-swipe and continuous-document as rejected alternatives, and the reasons
- [ ] ADR 0014 records the editor decision with stored-Sections and section-stack as rejected alternatives, and the reasons
- [ ] ADR 0014 states the reorder/delete omission and what would justify revisiting it
- [ ] ADR 0012 is amended in place with the binding target and desktop-only scope, without changing its Status
- [ ] ADR 0013 carries the note about one rendering path
- [ ] `CONTEXT.md` is unchanged, and ADR 0014 says why

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Bible study: reader becomes a scrolling deck, editor becomes a document with a navigating index
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

A student scans the Entry point QR at a gathering and lands on a reader that fights them. Each Section fills the screen but its content floats in the vertical middle, so a short Section — a point, a Passage, maybe a Prompt — sits in a band of empty background with dead space above and below. Tapping anywhere advances, which is the only way forward, and going back means finding a 36px chevron in the corner. There is no scrolling model at all: a reader who wants the previous Section, or who overshoots, is stuck. The card is sized in `vh`, so on iOS Safari the bottom chrome (progress rail, hint line) hides under the browser toolbar.

A Full-timer writing the week hits a different set. The editor is one markdown textarea with a left pane listing the `##` headings, and that pane is inert — it cannot be clicked, so a long week has no navigation. "+ Add section" inserts at the textarea's cursor, which is offset 0 if the textarea has never been focused, so the new heading lands silently at the *top* of the document, the pane does not scroll to it, and the selected Section does not change: the author clicks a button, the document looks unchanged, and they conclude nothing happened. The toolbar's "Section" button does the same thing from a second place, with no visible result either.

The right-hand live preview is supposed to show what a student sees, and does not. It is a hand-built 320×520 frame with `overflow-hidden` and no scroll, while `SectionBody` renders type at fixed 16–19px sized for a 390×844 phone. The result is oversized and cropped — it shows *less* than the real phone shows, which is the opposite of a preview's job. Its Blanks are stubbed inert.

## Solution

**The reader becomes a scrolling deck.** Sections stack vertically as scroll-snap panels, each at least the height of the viewport. Scrolling is the whole navigation model: forward, back, and overshoot-recovery all come free from the browser. A Section taller than the screen scrolls normally and snaps only at its boundary. Content top-aligns so the eye has one landing spot on every panel, and the space that used to be dead becomes a **peek** — a dimmed sliver of the next Section's title, which doubles as the scroll affordance. Tap-to-advance is removed; the Blanks keep their taps and stop competing with navigation. A slim sticky header carries the Meeting title, the counter, and — when the reader has fallen back to an older week — a date chip that never scrolls away.

**The editor becomes a document with an index that navigates.** The right pane stays one continuous markdown textarea for the whole week; Sections remain derived from `md`, not stored. The left pane stays the live `##` outline but becomes clickable: selecting a row scrolls the textarea to that heading and puts the caret there, and the row containing the caret is highlighted. One mutation lives on it — "+ Add section" appends a new heading at the **end** of the document, scrolls there, and leaves the caret after the hashes so the author immediately types the name and watches the row appear. The toolbar's Section button is removed; the toolbar becomes only things that go *inside* a Section.

**The preview becomes the reader.** The reader's presentational half is extracted into a component that both the public route and the editor preview render — the route feeding it a resolved published Meeting, the preview feeding it the author's unsaved markdown. It renders at true phone dimensions and is CSS-scaled to fit the pane, follows the caret's Section, scrolls freely, and reveals Blanks for real.

## User Stories

1. As a student who has scanned the Entry point QR, I want to scroll back to the previous Section, so that I can re-read a Passage the group is still discussing.
2. As a student, I want scrolling to be the way I move through a Meeting, so that I do not have to learn a tap gesture while a leader is talking.
3. As a student, I want each Section to come to rest filling the screen, so that I am reading one movement at a time rather than a wall of text.
4. As a student, I want a Section longer than my screen to scroll normally, so that I can read all of it without the page fighting me at every boundary.
5. As a student, I want to see a sliver of the next Section's title below the one I am reading, so that I know more exists and know what is coming.
6. As a student, I want a Section's content to start at the same place on every panel, so that my eyes are not hunting for where the text begins each time.
7. As a student, I want the whole page to fit inside the visible area of mobile Safari, so that the progress rail is not hidden behind the browser toolbar.
8. As a student on a notched phone, I want the header and footer clear of the safe area, so that nothing is under the notch or the home indicator.
9. As a student, I want to tap a Blank to reveal its word without also advancing the page, so that revealing an answer does not lose my place.
10. As a student, I want a revealed Blank to stay revealed when I scroll away and back, so that I do not lose what the group already worked out.
11. As a student who is reading a week that is not the current one, I want the older-week date to stay visible wherever I scroll, so that I never mistake an old Meeting for this week's.
12. As a student, I want to open the Section index and jump to a named Section, so that I can catch up when I arrive late.
13. As a student, I want the progress rail to reflect where I actually am after scrolling, so that the position indicator is not lying about my place.
14. As a student, I want to know when I have reached the last Section, so that I stop scrolling for content that is not there.
15. As a leader holding the phone in Present mode, I want the QR and its screen-awake behaviour unchanged, so that this work does not disturb what already works in the room.
16. As a Full-timer writing a week, I want the left pane to list every `##` heading in my document, so that I can see the week's structure while I write.
17. As a Full-timer, I want to click a heading in that list and land in the textarea at that heading, so that navigating a long week does not mean scrolling and squinting.
18. As a Full-timer, I want the list to highlight the Section my caret is in, so that I always know where I am in the document.
19. As a Full-timer, I want "+ Add section" to append at the end of the document, so that a new Section never appears silently in the middle of what I have already written.
20. As a Full-timer, I want the editor to scroll to the newly added heading and leave my caret ready to type its name, so that I can see that the click did something.
21. As a Full-timer, I want the new heading's row to appear in the outline as I type its title, so that the connection between `##` and "a Section" is visible rather than something I have to know.
22. As a Full-timer, I want only one place to add a Section, so that I am not guessing which of two buttons does what.
23. As a Full-timer, I want the toolbar to hold only what goes inside a Section — Passage, Blank, bold, italic, Question, Discuss, Activity — so that its contents mean one consistent thing.
24. As a Full-timer, I want typing a `##` mid-document to split that Section for real and update the outline immediately, so that the structure I see is the structure that exists.
25. As a Full-timer, I want the live preview to be the actual reader, so that what I approve is what the room gets.
26. As a Full-timer, I want the preview at real phone dimensions, so that a Passage that overflows on a student's phone overflows in my preview too.
27. As a Full-timer, I want the preview to scroll to the Section my caret is in, so that I am proofreading the thing I am writing without hunting for it.
28. As a Full-timer, I want to scroll the preview without my caret moving, so that inspecting a later Section does not move my cursor mid-sentence.
29. As a Full-timer, I want to tap a Blank in the preview and see it reveal, so that I can confirm `[[grace]]` became a tap target rather than literal brackets.
30. As a Full-timer, I want the preview to render my unsaved markdown, so that I can see a change before deciding to publish it.
31. As a Full-timer, I want the preview to show the peek, the sticky header and the snap behaviour, so that I am judging the real reading experience and not a still frame.
32. As a Full-timer, I want to move a Section by cutting and pasting its markdown, so that reordering remains possible even though no button offers it.
33. As a Full-timer, I want the Weeks index, publishing and Present mode to behave exactly as they do now, so that this change is confined to reading and writing a Meeting.
34. As a Full-timer, I want the same Meeting markdown to parse identically in the web app and in `@cisa/core`, so that what I write renders the same wherever it is read.
35. As a future maintainer, I want to find a record explaining why `readerReducer` has no `advance` or `back`, so that the deletion reads as a decision rather than an oversight.
36. As a future maintainer, I want the reason reorder and delete have no UI written down, so that I know it was chosen and what would justify revisiting it.

## Implementation Decisions

**Reader navigation model (replaces the tap-deck).**
- Sections render as a vertical stack of snap panels: each panel `min-height: 100dvh` with `scroll-snap-align: start`; the scroll container uses `scroll-snap-type: y proximity`. Proximity, not mandatory — mandatory can skip or trap on a Section taller than the viewport, which is the failure being fixed.
- Scroll position is the single owner of "which Section am I on". An IntersectionObserver mirrors the visible panel into component state as a **read model** only, consumed by the progress rail, the counter, and the index highlight.
- `advance` and `back` are deleted from `readerReducer` in **both** mirrors (`src/lib/bibleStudy.ts` and `packages/core/src/bibleStudy.ts`, which are kept in step). `jump` remains as the action the Section index dispatches, but its effect is a `scrollIntoView` rather than a state-owned index. `setTotalSections`, `revealBlank`, `openIndex`, `closeIndex` are unchanged.
- Whole-surface tap-to-advance is removed. `SectionBody`'s Blank handlers no longer need `stopPropagation` to survive, and the "Tap anywhere to go on" line is deleted.
- The `unadorned` field, `toggleUnadorned` action, and the distraction-free toggle are deleted. The chrome they hid is no longer busy enough to warrant them.

**Reader composition.**
- Section content top-aligns within its panel; the previous `my-auto` vertical centring is removed, so the title lands at the same height on every panel.
- The trailing space of each panel carries a **peek**: the next Section's title, dimmed, acting as both the "more below" affordance and a preview of what is coming. The last panel shows an end-of-Meeting treatment instead.
- Chrome is a slim sticky header (Meeting title, `NN / NN` counter) plus a sticky progress rail. The back chevron is removed with tap-to-advance.
- The stale-week notice condenses into a date chip inside the sticky header, so it is visible from any panel. Falling back is correct; falling back silently is not (ADR 0011 §3), and a student who lands on panel 4 must still be able to see the week is old.
- All viewport sizing moves from `vh` to `dvh`, and header/footer respect safe-area insets.

**Editor: document with an operating index.**
- The centre pane remains one textarea holding the whole Meeting's markdown. Sections stay **derived** from `md`; no per-Section storage, no Draft, no schema change. `md` remains the single source of truth (ADR 0013 §5).
- The left pane lists parsed Section headings and becomes interactive: clicking a row focuses the textarea, sets the selection to that heading's offset, and scrolls it into view. This is navigation, never mutation.
- The row containing the caret is highlighted; the caret's Section is also what the preview follows.
- "+ Add section" is the single mutation: it appends `\n\n## ` at the **end** of the document (never at the current cursor), scrolls there, and places the caret after the hashes. A new Section carries no starter body — the textarea's placeholder teaches the three moves (a point, `> a passage`, `Discuss:`) without inserting text the author must delete.
- The toolbar's "Section" button is removed. The toolbar retains only intra-Section inserters: Passage, Blank, bold, italic, Question, Discuss, Activity.
- No separate title input. Headings are edited inline in the document; the live outline is what makes their effect visible.
- No reorder and no delete controls. Moving a Section is cutting and pasting its markdown. Recorded as a deliberate omission with its cost stated.
- A `##` typed inside a Section body splits it for real. The outline updates live and the editor surfaces the split quietly rather than letting it happen silently.
- Editor remains desktop-only; the panes stay hidden below the `lg` breakpoint, now stated rather than incidental.

**New pure functions (both mirrors, kept in step):**
- `appendSection(md)` → the new markdown plus the caret offset the editor should land on.
- `sectionOffsets(md)` → the character offset of each Section heading, for click-to-jump.
- `sectionIndexAtOffset(md, offset)` → which Section the caret sits in, for the outline highlight and preview tracking.

**Preview: one rendering path.**
- The reader's presentational half is extracted into a shared component taking a Meeting as a prop. `PublicStudyReader` keeps the Entry point → Study → newest published Meeting resolution (`resolveScan`) and the empty states, then renders the shared component; the editor preview renders the same component over a Meeting built from the author's unsaved markdown. This makes literal ADR 0013 §3's requirement that the preview and the reader be one rendering path.
- The preview renders at true phone dimensions (390×844) and is CSS-transform-scaled to fit the pane, replacing the hand-built 320×520 frame. The dark/light toggle is retained.
- The preview is interactive: it scrolls, and Blanks reveal on tap (today they are stubbed with an empty `openBlanks` map and a no-op reveal). Scrolling the preview never moves the caret — tracking is one-way, editor to preview.

**Records.**
- New **ADR 0014** covering the reader's navigation model and the editor's document-with-index shape, with the rejected alternatives on record: deck-with-swipe and continuous-document for the reader; Section-as-stored-document and section-stack editing for the editor.
- **ADR 0012** amended: `md` remains one string and the single source of truth, so §3's `Y.Text`↔textarea binding target is the whole-document textarea, and its desktop-only scope is reaffirmed. The autosave/collaboration work itself is unaffected and unbuilt.
- **ADR 0013** gains a note that the preview and reader are now literally one component.
- `CONTEXT.md` needs no new terms — Entry point, Study, Meeting, Section, Passage, Prompt and Blank all still mean exactly what they meant, which is the signal the model held under this change.

**Sequencing — three PRs, in order:**
1. Reader: snap panels, `dvh`, top-align, peek, sticky chrome, tap-to-advance and distraction-free removal, reducer changes in both mirrors.
2. Editor: clickable outline, caret tracking, end-appending "+ Add section", toolbar Section button removal, the three new pure helpers.
3. Shared reader component extraction and the scaled, interactive preview — last, because it can only honestly mirror a reader whose shape is final.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts what a student or a Full-timer can observe, not how it was built: that a Section's panel is present and reachable, that clicking an outline row lands the caret in that Section, that the preview shows unsaved text. Tests that assert a class name, a reducer's internal shape, or a component's render count are not that. The seams below are the existing ones; **no new test seam is introduced** — the shared reader component is extracted for production reasons and is exercised through the two view seams that already exist.

**Seam 1 — the pure mirror pair** (`src/lib/bibleStudy.ts` and `packages/core/src/bibleStudy.ts`), the highest seam and where all new load-bearing logic goes. Covered by the existing `src/test/bibleStudy.test.ts` and `packages/core/test/bibleStudy.test.ts`. Cases: `appendSection` appends at the end regardless of any cursor and reports a caret offset inside the new heading; `sectionOffsets` returns an offset per heading and an empty result for a headingless document; `sectionIndexAtOffset` maps offsets to Sections including the boundary cases (offset 0 in a document that opens with prose, an offset exactly on a heading, an offset past the last heading); `readerReducer` no longer answers to `advance` or `back` and still handles `jump`, `revealBlank`, `openIndex`, `closeIndex`, `setTotalSections`.

**Seam 1b — mirror parity.** `src/test/bibleStudyMirrorParity.test.ts` asserts both parsers agree across a shared corpus. The three new helpers join it: every corpus fixture must produce deep-equal results from both modules, on the same grounds the parser does — a Full-timer's week must not behave differently depending on which module read it.

**Seam 2 — `PublicStudyReader`** (`src/test/PublicStudyReader.test.tsx`), the existing view seam with `src/lib/data/bibleStudy` already `vi.mock`ed and fixture Entry points, Studies and Meetings supplied as plain data. Cases: one panel per Section is rendered (all Sections in the document, not just the current one — the structural change from the old single-panel deck); clicking the body does not change the visible Section; the Section index jumps; the stale-week date chip is present and inside the sticky header; the end-of-Meeting treatment appears on the last panel; no distraction-free control exists. The existing resolution-state tests (never published, no active Study, permalink fallback) are unchanged and must keep passing.

**Seam 3 — `BibleStudyEditor`** (`src/test/BibleStudyEditor.test.tsx`), the existing view seam with the data layer and `AuthProvider` mocked. Cases: the outline lists every `##` heading; clicking a row moves the textarea's selection to that heading's offset; "+ Add section" appends at the end even when the textarea has never been focused (the exact reported bug) and leaves the caret in the new heading; the toolbar no longer offers a Section button; the preview renders text typed into the textarea but never saved. Note that these tests currently run against `BrowserRouter` because of the unsaved-changes guard; that stays until ADR 0012's autosave work removes the guard.

**Seam 4 — `SectionBody`** (`src/test/SectionBody.test.tsx`) is unchanged. Block rendering, Blank extraction and markdown escaping are not touched by this work, and the suite standing green is the evidence.

**Test-environment prior art.** jsdom implements neither `IntersectionObserver` nor `Element.prototype.scrollIntoView`. Both get stubs in `src/test/setup.ts`, alongside the `matchMedia` stub already defined there, which is the precedent for this kind of global.

**Not covered by any automated seam.** `dvh` versus `vh`, safe-area insets, and real scroll-snap physics only tell the truth on a device — jsdom has no layout and browser emulation renders both `vh` and `dvh` as correct. Verification is browser-preview inspection at emulated phone sizes plus a manual pass on a real iPhone against the QA deploy before merge.

## Out of Scope

- **ADR 0012's autosave and Yjs collaboration.** Accepted but unbuilt; the editor keeps Save draft and `useUnsavedGuard` through this work. Only the binding-target clarification is recorded.
- **Section reorder and delete controls.** Deliberately omitted; cut-and-paste is the mechanism. Revisit if reordering proves frequent.
- **A section-stack editor** (one Section at a time in the right pane) and **Sections as stored documents.** Both considered and rejected; recorded as alternatives in ADR 0014.
- **A whole-document bulk-paste workflow** from Google Docs. ADR 0013 anticipated it; not needed in the near term.
- **Editing a Meeting on a phone.** The editor stays desktop-only.
- **A separate Section title input.** Headings are edited inline.
- **Present mode, the QR, the Weeks index, Entry point setup, publishing and the Firestore rules.** Untouched.
- **Updating `docs/design/bible-study/` artboards** (`Main.dc.html`, `Editor.dc.html`, `DirectionA/B.dc.html`), which this work makes stale. Follow-up after the three PRs land, against what actually shipped.
- **Drag-to-reorder the outline**, and any change to `SectionBody`'s block rendering or markdown scope.

## Further Notes

- The `Section.long` flag exists in the type and has no behaviour. Under proximity snapping a long Section needs no special handling, so the flag should be checked for consumers and removed if it has none — same class of dead declaration ADR 0011 §4 cleaned up with `siblingId`.
- `docs/design/bible-study/README.md`'s Settled table survives this change: the Structure row ("Sections, one per screen; order as written") still holds — a snap panel is still one Section per screen. The Desktop row is already marked reversed by ADR 0011.
- The reported editor bug has a precise cause worth keeping in the record: "+ Add section" called an insert-at-cursor helper, and a textarea that has never been focused reports `selectionStart` 0, so the heading was written to the top of the document while the author watched the bottom.
- The preview's cropping has an equally precise cause: `SectionBody` sets type in fixed pixels sized for a 390-wide phone, and the mimic frame was 320×520 with `overflow-hidden`. Same type, smaller box, no scroll.
- This work originated in a grilling session on 2026-09-07 covering thirty decisions across the reader, the editor and the preview; ADR 0014 is where the rejected branches are recorded.

title: Bible study: indented sub-points nest instead of flattening (ADR 0013 promised nesting)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Gap

ADR 0013 (§2, Consequences) says: "Nested lists deliver most of the deferred outline-style want (I / A / 1 nesting) with no grammar work." The code does not deliver it.

`parseSectionBody` (src/lib/bibleStudy.ts:249 / packages/core/src/bibleStudy.ts:245) pushes `rawLine.trim()` for bullet points, so an indented sub-point becomes a sibling `<li>`:

```md
- Main point
  - Sub point A
  - Sub point B
```

parses to three flat points. The grammar doc comment claims "indentation preserved" — it is not. `packages/core/test/bibleStudy.test.ts:182` pins the flat behavior.

## Why it slipped

The marker restoration change (list-disc/list-decimal in `SectionBody.renderList`) kept nesting out of scope on purpose: changing point shape means renderer nesting, Blank reveal keying, and both parser mirrors move together.

## Fix shape

1. `ListBlock.points` gains nesting (either a depth per point, or child arrays).
2. `renderList` renders nested `<ul>`/`<ol>` inside the parent `<li>`.
3. Blank reveal keys extend the existing `${sectionIndex}:${label}${pIdx}` scheme.
4. Both parser mirrors change in step (repo "keep in step" rule); the flat-pinning core test flips to nesting.

Decision from the 2026-09-07 grilling session: deferred, user asked for flat `1 2 3 4` markers first.

label: CLOSED

body:
## Problem Statement

Writing a week's Meeting means trusting a Save button and an interception dialog: every internal link, browser back, and tab close while dirty triggers a "leave without saving?" prompt, and one wrong click — or a crash — loses the week's outline. Two Full-timers preparing the same Meeting can't work together: the editor freezes its copy at load, ignores the other's edits, and whoever saves last silently overwrites the first.

## Solution

The desktop Meeting editor saves by itself: a short debounce after typing stops persists the document, with honest states — "Saving…", "Saved · just now", and "Couldn't save" with automatic retry when a write fails. Two Full-timers opening the same Meeting see each other's edits live and a name chip saying who else is in, using the same Yjs-over-RTDB collaboration The Board's pages already run. Where the realtime backend is absent or degraded, the editor falls back to single-user autosave — saving never depends on the collaboration transport. Publishing remains a deliberate toggle; there is no Draft (ADR 0012).

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer, I want the Meeting editor to save my writing by itself as I type, so that a crash or closed tab never costs me a week's outline.
2. As a Full-timer, I want to see "Saving…" and "Saved · just now" in the editor, so that I trust my work is durable without hunting for a Save button.
3. As a Full-timer, I want a visible "Couldn't save" state that retries automatically, so that a dropped connection can't silently swallow my edits.
4. As a Full-timer, I want the Meeting title and date to save themselves too, so that no field in the editor needs a manual save.
5. As a Full-timer, I want Publish to stay a deliberate toggle that autosave never flips, so that half-written text never reaches students by accident.
6. As a Full-timer, I want to leave the editor at any time without a "leave without saving?" dialog, so that navigation is never interrupted.
7. As a Full-timer, I want a second Full-timer editing the same Meeting to show up as a name chip, so that I know someone else is in the document before I type.
8. As a Full-timer, I want my co-editor's words to appear on my screen as they type, so that we can prepare a week together instead of overwriting each other.
9. As a Full-timer, I want concurrent edits to merge rather than last-write-wins, so that neither of us silently loses work.
10. As a Full-timer, I want my Section, Prompt, Blank, and Passage insert buttons to behave exactly as before, so that collaboration changes nothing about how I write.
11. As a Full-timer whose project hasn't enabled the realtime backend, I want autosave to work anyway, so that saving never depends on collaboration infrastructure.
12. As a Full-timer whose realtime connection drops mid-session, I want the editor to fall back to single-user autosave, so that I keep writing instead of losing the pane.
13. As a Full-timer, I want the document seeded correctly the first time it is opened for collaboration, so that opening a week twice never duplicates or clobbers its content.
14. As a student reading a published Meeting in the room, I want a leader's corrections to reach my page without anyone pressing save, so that the text I follow is current.
15. As a maintainer, I want the meetings realtime path readable and writable only by signed-in users, so that the collaboration log isn't a public door.
16. As a Full-timer, I want autosave on the desktop editor only, so that nothing changes on mobile, where no Meeting editor exists.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Autosave writes the student-facing document in place; there is no Draft.** Publishing stays a manual toggle on the same document, never flipped by autosave. Accepted cost (ADR 0012): re-editing a published Meeting streams changes to readers at the debounce rate.
- **Concurrency is real-time collaboration, not last-writer-wins.** Edits flow through a Yjs document replicated over RTDB under a meetings-specific path; a debounced projection persists the merged state (markdown plus derived Sections) to the Meeting document. This replaces the editor's freeze-at-load behavior.
- **The realtime provider's hardcoded pages base path is parameterized**, and first open seeds the Yjs document from the stored markdown behind the existing seed-claim guard, so double-opening never double-seeds.
- **The editing surface stays a markdown textarea** with a purpose-built Y.Text binding — no rich-text migration; the Section/Prompt/Blank/Passage insert helpers keep working on the selection.
- **Tier 0 fallback mirrors The Board**: realtime transport absent or degraded → single-user debounced autosave, no error noise. Autosave never depends on RTDB being enabled.
- **Cadence mirrors CoordinationNotes: ~1200ms** body markdown, **~800ms** title and date. One cadence for published and unpublished Meetings alike.
- **Honest save states with auto-retry** on the next edit or reconnect. Optimistic silent saving was rejected: the app has no Firestore offline persistence, so a failed write is a real failure, and an indicator that says "Saved" during one is the exact data loss this feature prevents.
- **Presence is name chips only** from the existing awareness plumbing; remote cursors are out.
- **The meeting data module gains narrow update functions** (body projection; title/date meta) instead of autosave reusing the full-document create-style write. Publish keeps its dedicated toggle path.
- **The unsaved-changes guard is deleted with its tests** once the editor stops using it; the promise it carried ("a Full-timer can't lose a week's writing") moves to autosave.
- **Scope is the desktop web editor only** — no mobile Meeting editor exists, so nothing else changes.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests assert external behavior at the highest seam: the rendered editor component — debounce-driven saves under fake timers, visible save states, the publish toggle, presence chips, insert helpers, and the Tier 0 fallback. A good test observes what a Full-timer sees, never internal wiring.
- Prior art: the existing editor component tests, and the Board editor tests that mock the realtime provider the same way.
- The realtime rules are tested as rules, in the style of the existing Firestore rules tests.
- **No isolated unit tests for the Y.Text binding**: merge behavior is asserted through the component, where a regression would actually bite. The ideal seam count is the two above; the binding is deliberately not a third.

## Out of Scope

- Mobile — no Meeting editor exists there.
- A Draft/publish-promotion model — rejected in ADR 0012; the recorded escape hatch if re-editing published weeks while the room reads becomes a real workflow.
- Remote cursors, offline write queueing, stale-edit warnings, and any rich-text editor migration.
- The index and Entry point screens — no unsaved prose lives there.
- Provisioning or enabling RTDB on the Firebase project — rules land in the repo; activation follows the existing env-based opt-in.

## Further Notes

- The full decision record is ADR 0012; the public scan path (Entry point → active Study → newest published Meeting) is ADR 0011 and is unchanged.
- The tracker already carries two 0011 ADR files — pre-existing duplication, left alone.

title: Spec: Bible study Meetings render rich markdown and read as written (ADR 0012)
label: CLOSED
body:
# Spec: Bible study Meetings render rich markdown and read as written

Operationalizes [ADR 0012](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/blob/main/docs/adr/0012-bible-study-rich-markdown-as-written.md). Glossary: Entry point, Study, Meeting, Section, Passage, Prompt, Blank (root `CONTEXT.md`).

## Problem Statement

I lead a Bible study and my material already exists — written on the Google Site / in Google Docs as plain text with some bold, some italics, and underline. When I bring a study into the app, two things go wrong. Pasting into the editor strips all formatting to plain text. Then the reader silently drops anything outside a narrow dialect: a plain paragraph, a numbered list, an indented sub-point all vanish between editor and reader, and my bold/italics show up as literal asterisks. Worse, whatever does survive gets re-ordered — every section renders points, then scripture, then the prompt, no matter how I actually wrote the document. My studies read like a slide deck rebuilt from fragments, not like the documents I wrote.

## Solution

A Meeting's Sections become what they were always designed to be: ordered flows that read as written. I paste my document's plain text, put headings where Sections belong, and re-apply the sparse emphasis with toolbar buttons. Everything I wrote survives — prose, numbered lists, indented sub-points, scripture blockquotes wherever I put them, prompts wherever they fall, blanks wherever they help. The reader shows bold, italics, and links as formatting; the live preview shows exactly what students will see; and my already-published weeks keep reading as they do today.

## User Stories

**Authoring (Full-timer)**

1. As a Full-timer, I want to paste the plain text of an existing study from Google Docs into the meeting editor, so that I can bring in material I already wrote instead of retyping it.
2. As a Full-timer, I want every line I paste to survive to the reader, so that bringing a document in never silently loses prose, numbered lists, or indented points.
3. As a Full-timer, I want document headings to start new Sections, so that my document's structure becomes the reader's navigation.
4. As a Full-timer, I want the reader to show my content in the order I wrote it, so that a study that interleaves prose, outline points, scripture, and prompts reads the way I composed it.
5. As a Full-timer, I want bold and italic inserters in the toolbar beside the existing ones, so that I can restore emphasis after pasting plain text.
6. As a Full-timer, I want links in section text, so that I can point readers at recordings, reading plans, or websites.
7. As a Full-timer, I want nested (indented) lists in my content, so that I can put sub-points under main points without a separate outline feature.
8. As a Full-timer, I want numbered lists to survive, so that ordered sequences like reading steps keep their numbers.
9. As a Full-timer, I want a blockquote anywhere in a section to render as the Passage, with the last line of the blockquote as its citation, so that the scripture convention survives the richer format.
10. As a Full-timer, I want Question:, Discuss:, and Activity: lines to work anywhere in a section, so that a Prompt isn't forced to sit at a fixed spot.
11. As a Full-timer, I want Blanks (`[[word]]`) to work in prose as well as outline points and the Passage, so that fill-in-the-blank can interrupt reading wherever it makes sense.
12. As a Full-timer, I want Blanks to behave predictably when combined with bold or italic, so that tap-to-reveal never breaks or swallows formatting.
13. As a Full-timer, I want the live preview to render exactly what the public reader will, so that what I check while editing is what students get.
14. As a Full-timer, I want my already-published weeks to keep rendering as they do today, so that the format upgrade never rewrites the back catalog.
15. As a Full-timer, I want the markdown textarea to remain the source of truth I can read and edit as plain text, so that documents stay portable and diffable.
16. As a Full-timer, I want the sections gutter to keep tracking my document live while I type, so that navigation always reflects the Sections my headings actually create.
17. As a Full-timer, I want the unsaved-changes guard to keep protecting long paste-and-edit sessions, so that an accidental navigation never loses a big edit.
18. As a Full-timer, I want "underline is not carried" to be a stated convention, so that I know to express emphasis with bold or italic instead of losing it at paste time.

**Reading (students and visitors)**

19. As a student scanning the Entry point QR, I want the week to read as a flowing document — prose where the author wrote prose — so that it reads like a written study, not a slide deck.
20. As a student, I want bold, italics, and links rendered as real formatting, so that emphasis and references communicate instead of showing literal asterisks and bare URLs.
21. As a student, I want nested lists shown as sub-points under their parents, so that the study's structure is visible on the page.
22. As a student, I want to tap a Blank word to reveal it wherever the author placed it, so that reading stays active.
23. As a student, I want the Passage quoted with its citation wherever the author put it, so that scripture reads in place rather than being pushed to a fixed slot.
24. As a student, I want Prompts rendered as distinct Question / Discuss / Activity blocks wherever they fall, so that what the room works through stands out.
25. As a student, I want one Section per screen with the edge scrubber and progress dots unchanged, so that navigation feels the same while the content gets richer.
26. As a student, I want the page to never execute raw HTML from the document, so that scanning a QR never exposes my device to injected markup.
27. As a trainee, I want the unlisted staff permalink to render a Meeting exactly like the QR page, so that what I text a student reads identically for both of us.
28. As a Full-timer, I want the reader and the editor preview built on one rendering path, so that I can trust the preview while editing.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Section = ordered flow of blocks.** Heading lines start Sections. Within a Section, blockquote runs are Passages (last line of a run = citation), `Question:`/`Discuss:`/`Activity:` lines are Prompts, `[[word]]` tokens are Blanks, and everything else — paragraphs, bullets, numbered lists, nested lists — is body content rendered in authored order. No canonical reordering of points/passage/prompt. This restores the design README's Structure row ("all optional, order as written") and its governing principle ("the author decides, the page obeys"); the shipped parser diverged from both.
- **Markdown scope (v1):** inline bold, italic, links, ordered and nested lists. Rendered with ReactMarkdown + remark-gfm — the exact stack coordination notes already ship — with a component map tuned to the reader's type scale.
- **Security posture:** no rehype-raw; react-markdown's default HTML escaping is the sanitization for the public, anonymous reader. Raw HTML in a document renders as text, never executes.
- **Blank rule:** `[[…]]` is reserved syntax, extracted before markdown processing. Blank contents are plain text, never markdown; a Blank wins its run — emphasis markers around it are not styled. Blank keying follows the ordered-block shape and preserves the existing invariant that the same word in different Sections never co-reveals.
- **One rendering path.** A single shared Section-body renderer is consumed by both the public reader and the editor's live preview (dark/light preview toggle preserved). The preview cannot drift from the reader.
- **Editor toolbar gains bold/italic inserters** using the same insert-at-cursor mechanism as the existing Section/Passage/Blank/Question/Discuss/Activity buttons. Authoring remains manual paste; Google Docs headings map to Section headings by author convention.
- **Underline is not carried.** On the web underline is the link affordance; markdown has no underline syntax that doesn't collide with bold. Authors express emphasis with bold/italic.
- **Data model:** the stored raw markdown remains the source of truth; the derived Sections are re-derived under the new grammar. The grammar change lands in both mirrors (web and the core package) which must stay in step.
- **Backward compatibility:** every existing published Meeting must re-parse and render with content in the same visual order as today — for dialect-conformant documents, author order and today's fixed order coincide, so nothing visibly changes.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test asserts external, observable behavior — markdown in, what the reader renders out — never internal block arrays, component props, or implementation wiring.
- **Seam 1 — the meeting markdown parser (existing, pure).** Plain-data fixtures cover every grammar decision: as-written ordering across mixed content; dialect constructs recognized anywhere in the flow; prose survival (the silent drop dies); Blanks winning their run; and legacy documents re-parsing to today's visual order. Prior art: the core package's existing plain-data parser suite.
- **Seam 2 — the shared Section-body renderer (new, the one UI seam).** Render and assert visible output: authored order across mixed blocks; bold/italic/links rendered (no literal asterisks); nested list nesting; Blank tap-reveal and per-Section keying; Passage with citation; Prompt styling. Prior art: the coordination notes' read-only ReactMarkdown rendering tests.
- **View-level smoke tests:** the public reader keeps its existing scan-resolution/empty-state tests plus an assertion that it renders through the shared renderer; the editor preview gets a smoke test that it uses the same component. Prior art: the existing mocked-Firestore view tests for the reader and editor.
- **Mirror parity:** both parser mirrors are exercised against the same pinned fixture corpus, so "keep in step" is enforced by tests rather than by a comment.
- Tests are deterministic, isolated, and full-suite-safe; coverage thresholds only ratchet up.
- No Playwright e2e in this spec (explicit decision).

## Out of Scope

- Tables and images — including any Storage upload path.
- Underline support.
- Rich clipboard-HTML→markdown paste. Deferred deliberately; the Board editor already ships a working Google-Docs paste-normalization precedent (turndown with styled-bold/italic rules) to revisit when the manual tax proves heavy.
- Outline auto-numbering (I / II / A / 1) as grammar. Nested lists cover the want incidentally; the dedicated outline feature was explicitly deferred.
- The mobile app's study reader — no surface exists yet; the core package mirror stays ready for it.
- Playwright e2e specs.
- Scan resolution, Entry points, and publish/unpublish semantics — ADR 0011 territory, unchanged.

## Further Notes

- ADR 0012 plus this issue form the handoff package for the implementing agent; the ADR records the why, this spec the what.
- The silent-drop behavior this work removes is a real data-loss edge today: pasting a document leaves only headings, bullets, and blockquotes in the reader. Prose-survival tests should pin that regression permanently.
- Blanks inside prose are a small grammar extension beyond today's parser (which only looks for `[[…]]` inside bullet text and the passage); the shared renderer must handle a Blank as a block-level as well as inline occurrence.
- The reader is public and anonymous at the Entry point URL; the staff permalink renders through the same reader. Treat every rendering decision as public-facing.

title: CI: Deploy Firestore Rules fails at GCP auth on every push to main
label: CLOSED

labels.name: ready-for-human
labels.description: Ready for a human to implement (judgment / external access / design)

body:
## Problem

The **Deploy Firestore Rules** workflow has failed on every push to `main` since at least Sep 2 (recent runs: [34087408431](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/actions/runs/34087408431), [34141594911](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/actions/runs/34141594911), and five more before). The failure is in the **Authenticate to Google Cloud** step, before any deploy happens:

```
google-github-actions/auth failed with: failed to generate Google Cloud federated token for
//iam.googleapis.com/projects/914549253362/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/providers/github:
{"error":"unauthorized_client","error_description":"The given credential is rejected by the attribute condition."}
```

This is a GCP-side workload identity config problem — the OIDC provider's attribute condition is rejecting the GitHub OIDC token for the `github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com` service account. It is not a code problem: the test-suite CI workflow is green on the same commits.

## Impact

- `firestore.rules` and `firestore.indexes.json` changes merged to `main` are **not published** to `prod` / `qa-db` by CI.
- Concretely: #865 landed the Entry point / Study rules (EP1–EP4), the delete-only-while-unpublished Meeting rule, and the two `bible_study_meetings` composite indexes — those exist only in the repo until this deploy path works.

## Suggested fix

Check the workload identity pool provider's **attribute condition** in the GCP console (IAM → Workload Identity Pools → the `github-actions` provider): the condition likely restricts by ref or repository and no longer matches (common after a repo rename, default-branch change, or condition edit). The service account IAM binding and the `attribute.repository` / `attribute.ref` claim mappings are the other usual suspects.

Only a maintainer with GCP access can fix this; nothing in the repo can.

title: Row actions on the weeks index
label: CLOSED

## Parent

#857 (part 2 of #822). See the `Main` artboard in `docs/design/bible-study-index/`.

## What to build

The things a Full-timer needs to do to a week that are not editing it: reuse one, pull one back, send one to a student, throw one away.

The care is in delete. A published **Meeting** may already be on a student's screen, so removing it should take two deliberate steps rather than one click — and when it is refused, the reason should be readable rather than hidden behind a disabled control.

Duplicate carries extra weight now: it is also how a split week gets made, by populating a second **Entry point**.

Design canvas: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/abbe5271-3a17-4539-b720-89062eccde59

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each week in the list offers duplicate, unpublish, copy staff link, and delete
- [ ] Duplicating produces a new week with the source's structure, leaving the source untouched
- [ ] Unpublishing a week is reflected immediately in what the index says a scan opens, falling back to the previous published week
- [ ] Copy staff link yields the unlisted per-week permalink
- [ ] Delete is offered for an unpublished week and refused for a published one
- [ ] The reason delete is unavailable is written where it can be read, not left as an unexplained disabled control
- [ ] The refusal is enforced by the security rules as well as the UI, so it holds regardless of the client
- [ ] Deleting a week removes it from the list without disturbing the other weeks or the entry point's resolution

## Blocked by

- #860
- #862

title: Leaving a week never costs you writing
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

#857 (part 2 of #822). See the `UnsavedGuard` and `Editor` artboards in `docs/design/bible-study-index/`.

## What to build

The weeks index makes moving between weeks one click. Without this ticket, that click is also how you lose an evening's writing — the exact failure #822 reported, inverted.

A Full-timer part-way through next week's outline clicks an earlier week. The app asks first, and offers a real choice.

Also: a new week should start from something that teaches the conventions without pretending to be content, and the Romans example currently baked into the editor should go.

Design canvas: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/abbe5271-3a17-4539-b720-89062eccde59

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Leaving a **Meeting** with unsaved changes — to the index, to another week, or by navigating away — asks before discarding
- [ ] The prompt offers three distinct actions: stay, discard and leave, save and leave. Cancelling and discarding are different intentions and never share a control
- [ ] Saving and leaving actually saves before navigating; discarding leaves without saving; staying leaves the editor exactly as it was, with the changes intact
- [ ] The editor shows that it has unsaved changes without the user having to try to leave to find out
- [ ] Leaving a Meeting with no unsaved changes does not prompt
- [ ] A new week opens with a small skeleton — one Section, a Passage stub, a Prompt line — visibly placeholder, teaching the three conventions
- [ ] A new week is never silently seeded from the previous week's text, which risks publishing last week's content under this week's date
- [ ] The hardcoded Romans example content is removed from the editor. It lives only in component state, so nothing needs migrating
- [ ] The editor no longer offers "Split into two" — a split week is a second **Entry point**, made with the duplicate action

## Blocked by

- #862

title: The weeks index
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

#857 (part 2 of #822). See [ADR 0011](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-bible-study-entry-points.md) and the `Main` / `IndexPhone` artboards in `docs/design/bible-study-index/`.

## What to build

The thing #822 asked for. A Full-timer opens Bible study and sees every week of the **Study** — what exists, what is published, and what a student scanning right now would actually get.

The weeks were never really being overwritten; they were unreachable. The screen already subscribes to every **Meeting** and renders none of them, so whichever loaded first was the only one you could edit. This replaces that screen with a list, and moves the editor to its own address.

Design canvas: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/abbe5271-3a17-4539-b720-89062eccde59

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bible study's top-level route is a list of the active Study's weeks, newest first, showing each week's date, title, section count and whether it is published
- [ ] The week a scan opens right now is marked distinctly — this is not the same as the newest week, and the gap between them must be readable without comparing dates
- [ ] A panel states what a scan opens right now, and why a newer draft is not showing
- [ ] The **Entry point** is visible on this screen: its name, its slug, the active Study, and the primary action to show the QR
- [ ] Showing the QR opens present mode
- [ ] The editor moves to its own per-Meeting route, reached by opening a week from the list
- [ ] Starting a new week is available from the list
- [ ] The screen works at 390px, since a Full-timer checks what is published from their phone
- [ ] Both the list and the editor remain Full-timer-only
- [ ] The list is driven by the existing data seam so its tests mock that module and assert on what renders

## Further note

The design includes an All / Published / Drafts filter. It earns its place at twelve weeks and is clutter at four; the recommendation from design review is to leave it out of v1. Build it only if you disagree after seeing it with real data.

## Blocked by

- #859
- #861

title: A real, scannable QR in present mode
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

#857 (part 2 of #822). See [ADR 0011](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-bible-study-entry-points.md) and the `Present` artboard in `docs/design/bible-study-index/`.

## What to build

A leader standing in front of the room opens present mode on their phone, holds it up, and people can actually scan it.

Today they cannot. What the app draws is a hand-authored SVG with fixed paths — the same picture regardless of the URL beside it — and there is no QR library in the project at all. Nothing that has ever been held up has been scannable. The panel is also hidden below `lg`, so on a phone it does not exist.

Design canvas: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/abbe5271-3a17-4539-b720-89062eccde59

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A QR is generated client-side from a pinned library, rendering from local state — not a server endpoint and not a third-party image service, because the room's wifi is not ours to rely on
- [ ] The encoded URL's origin comes from a new public app-URL environment variable defaulting to the production domain, documented alongside the existing auth-domain override that solves the same prod/QA split
- [ ] The origin is never derived from the browser's current location, which would render an unreachable `localhost` code in front of a room
- [ ] Present mode is a full-screen surface: the code dominates, the week and **Study** are named quietly beneath it, nothing else competes
- [ ] It renders on a light ground regardless of the viewer's theme — a dark ground behind a QR hurts scan reliability, and this screen has one job
- [ ] The screen is kept awake while present mode is open
- [ ] Any signed-in user can open it, not only Full-timers: the person holding the phone is often the Trainee running the room. Editing stays Full-timer-only
- [ ] It works at 390px, since that is the device it is shown from
- [ ] The editor's existing fake QR panel is replaced by a handoff to present mode
- [ ] Scanning the rendered code on a real device reaches the reader

## Blocked by

- #859

title: The reader says which week it is showing
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

#856 (part 1 of #822). See [ADR 0011](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-bible-study-entry-points.md) and the `EmptyStates` artboard in `docs/design/bible-study-index/`.

## What to build

A student scanning on Tuesday, before this week has been published, gets the most recent week to read — with its date stated at the top. Falling back is right; falling back silently is not. "Here is a study" and "here is last week's study" must never look identical.

Also the two remaining honest answers: a study that has never published anything says so, and a Full-timer can copy a link to one specific week to text to someone who missed it.

Design canvas: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/abbe5271-3a17-4539-b720-89062eccde59

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When the newest published **Meeting** is not the current week's, the reader shows it with its date stated plainly at the top of the screen
- [ ] A **Study** with nothing ever published renders a distinct state — not the same screen as the between-terms one, since the reasons differ and so does what the reader should do
- [ ] Neither empty state offers an action, because there is none a student can take
- [ ] A staff permalink route addresses one week by Study and date, carries `noindex`, and is linked from nowhere in the app
- [ ] The permalink is public rather than gated: the security rule already serves any published Meeting to anyone, so a UI gate would present an open door as protected
- [ ] The permalink shows the same dated treatment when the week it names is not the current one
- [ ] Requesting a permalink for a week that does not exist is handled rather than rendering an empty page
- [ ] Fallback, never-published, between-terms and permalink cases are all covered in the pure resolution function's tests, with no mocking

- #859

title: A scan resolves through an Entry point to a week
label: CLOSED
body:
## Parent

#856 (part 1 of #822). See [ADR 0011](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-bible-study-entry-points.md).

## What to build

The first end-to-end path. Seed a **Study** and an **Entry point**, point a phone at `/s/cisa-wednesday`, and read the newest published **Meeting** of whichever Study is active on that entry point — without signing in.

The entry point is the durable thing: a permanent slug that names a standing invitation rather than a term's content. It outlives every Study that passes through it, so starting a new term is a change of which Study is active, never a change of URL.

Two records, one resolution chain, one public route. No admin screens — those are #857.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Study record carries a title and term label; an Entry point record carries a slug, a display name, and the currently active Study
- [ ] Both are publicly readable (an anonymous scan must resolve both) and writable only by Full-timers
- [ ] A single pure function resolves entry point + Study + Meetings to a discriminated result, tested with plain data and no mocks. From the design round, the shape that encodes the decisions:

```
resolveScan(entryPoint, study, meetings, today, permalinkDate)
  -> { kind: 'meeting', meeting, isFallback, fallbackDate? }
   | { kind: 'never-published' }
   | { kind: 'no-active-study' }
```

- [ ] The existing "newest published meeting" helper is folded into it rather than left beside it
- [ ] `/s/:slug` renders the resolved Meeting for an anonymous visitor
- [ ] An entry point with no active Study renders the between-terms state: it says the study picks up again later, and that the code is worth keeping
- [ ] A Meeting can be hard-deleted only while unpublished — enforced in the rules, not only in a UI
- [ ] Both composite indexes are added to the index manifest: `(studyId, published, date desc)` and `(studyId, date desc)`. The first cannot serve a query that omits `published`, so both are needed
- [ ] A seed script creates a Study and an Entry point, so this ticket is verifiable on its own
- [ ] Existing `romans-fall26` test content is deleted rather than migrated

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

Nothing changes for anyone using the app. `siblingId` is declared on the **Meeting** type, copied by the data mapper, and validated in the security rules, and has behavior in none of those places — it was the field the abandoned "split a week into two Meetings" design would have used.
