title: Bible study: weeks index, editor rewrite, present mode (#822, part 2 of 2)
label: CLOSED
body:
Part 2 of 2 for #822. Depends on #856. Design and decisions: [ADR 0011](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-bible-study-entry-points.md) and the six artboards in `docs/design/bible-study-index/`, merged in #854.

Canvas: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/abbe5271-3a17-4539-b720-89062eccde59

## Problem Statement

This is the half of #822 the Full-timer actually feels. Today `/bible-study` is a single form. It subscribes to every **Meeting** in the **Study** and renders none of them — the handler that would select one is defined and never called — so the only week reachable is whichever loaded first. Writing next week means overwriting the form in front of you, with no list, no way back to an earlier week, and no warning if you navigate away mid-sentence.

The QR panel beside it draws a decorative SVG that encodes nothing, at a domain the ministry does not own, and it is hidden below `lg` — so on the phone a leader actually holds up in the room, it does not exist at all.

## Solution

Split the two jobs the one screen was doing. `/bible-study` becomes an index of a Study's weeks — what exists, what is published, and what a student scanning right now would actually see. `/bible-study/:meetingId` becomes the editor for one week, entered and left deliberately, with a guard so leaving never costs you what you wrote.

A real QR gets generated, and present mode gives the leader a full-screen code to hold up.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer, I want a list of every week in the Study, so that I can see the shape of the term at a glance.
2. As a Full-timer, I want to open any past week, so that I can fix a typo in something already published.
3. As a Full-timer, I want to see which weeks are published and which are drafts, so that I know what is reachable without opening each one.
4. As a Full-timer, I want the week a scan opens right now marked distinctly, so that the gap between what I am writing and what students see is visible without reading dates.
5. As a Full-timer, I want to start a new week, so that writing next week never means typing over last week.
6. As a Full-timer, I want a new week to start from a small skeleton rather than a blank page, so that I am reminded of the conventions without being handed last week's text.
7. As a Full-timer, I want to duplicate a week deliberately, so that I can reuse a structure when I choose to, and never by accident.
8. As a Full-timer, I want to be warned before leaving a week with unsaved changes, so that the list I asked for cannot cost me an evening's writing.
9. As a Full-timer, I want the warning to offer saving, discarding and staying as three separate choices, so that cancelling and discarding are never the same button.
10. As a Full-timer, I want to delete a week I have not published, so that abandoned drafts do not accumulate.
11. As a Full-timer, I want deleting a published week to require unpublishing first, so that I cannot remove something already on a student's screen in one click.
12. As a Full-timer, I want the reason delete is unavailable written where I can read it, so that a disabled control is not a mystery.
13. As a Full-timer, I want a real, scannable QR code, so that holding up my phone actually works.
14. As a Full-timer, I want the QR full-screen on a phone, so that a room can scan it from a distance.
15. As a Full-timer, I want the present screen to keep the phone awake, so that it does not lock while people are still scanning.
16. As a Trainee running the room that week, I want to be able to show the code, so that a Full-timer does not have to be present to start the study.
17. As a Trainee, I want editing still restricted to Full-timers, so that showing the code does not mean I can rewrite the reading.
18. As a Full-timer, I want the editor to tell me where the week goes when I publish, so that the relationship between this document and the code is stated rather than inferred.
19. As a Full-timer, I want to copy a staff link to one week, so that I can text it to a student who missed it.
20. As a Full-timer, I want the conventions to stay buttons rather than syntax, so that I never have to remember a marker.
21. As a Full-timer, I want the live preview to keep showing where the screen edge falls, so that I can see the Section break I own.
22. As a Full-timer on a phone, I want the weeks index to work, so that I can check what is published without opening a laptop.
23. As a Full-timer, I want the mock Romans content gone from a fresh install, so that the editor never opens holding someone else's example.

## Implementation Decisions

**Two routes replace one.** `/bible-study` is the weeks index; `/bible-study/:meetingId` is the editor. Both Full-timer-only, as today.

**The index is two columns, and they answer different questions.** The left column is what exists; the right is what a student scanning right now would see. Keeping them apart is the design: the newest draft can sit at the top of the list while an older week carries the live mark, making the gap legible without arithmetic.

**The index carries the entry point.** Slug, name, active Study, and the primary Show QR action. This is where the record introduced in #856 becomes visible to the person who owns it.

**The row menu holds duplicate, unpublish, copy staff link and delete.** Delete renders disabled for a published week with its reason written beneath it, not in a tooltip. Duplicate is also how a split week is made: a second entry point populated from here.

**The editor loses three things.** The week list moves to the index. The QR panel goes, replaced by a statement of where the week goes when published plus a handoff to present mode — the old panel taught the wrong model by putting a dated URL beside the document. "Split into two" goes, because splits are entry points now.

**The editor gains a dirty-state guard.** Without it, the index makes losing a week's writing a one-click action — the inverse of the bug being reported. Three actions: stay, discard and open, save and open.

**A new Meeting starts from a skeleton** — one Section, a Passage stub, a Prompt line, all obviously placeholder. Never a silent copy of the previous week, which risks publishing last week's text under this week's date.

**Present mode is its own surface**, reached from the index. Full-screen QR, the week and Study named quietly beneath, a wake lock while it is open. It renders on a **white ground regardless of theme** — every other reader surface follows the phone, but a dark ground behind a QR hurts scan reliability and this screen has one job.

**Showing the code is not an admin action.** Present mode is available to any signed-in user; editing stays Full-timer-only. The person holding the phone is often not the Full-timer.

**QR generation is client-side**, from a pinned library rendering SVG in the browser. Not a server endpoint and not a third-party image service: the code must render from local state in a room whose wifi nobody controls. Origin comes from `VITE_PUBLIC_APP_URL` (introduced in #856).

**The index and present mode must work at phone widths.** This reverses the earlier "desktop: admin editing only" position, for the plain reason that the QR is displayed from a phone.

**The mock Romans content is removed.** It lives only in editor component state — no seeded documents — so removal is local.

**Open question carried from design review:** the index's All / Published / Drafts filter earns its place at twelve weeks and is clutter at four. Recommendation is to cut it for v1.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts what a Full-timer would observe — which weeks are listed, which is marked live, whether the guard appears, whether delete is offered — never which component held which state.

**Seams — the same ones as #856, no new ones.**

- **The Bible study data module** stays the seam the views are tested against. Index and editor tests mock it wholesale and assert on rendered output, exactly as the existing reader view test does.
- **Any list-shaping or dirty-state logic that is worth testing goes in the pure module** beside `resolveScan`, so it is exercised with plain data rather than through a rendered component.
- **View tests** cover the index and editor at the component level with the data module mocked. Prior art: the existing editor and reader view tests.
- **The rules suite** needs nothing new here — the delete constraint lands in #856.

Cases that must be covered: the list renders newest-first with published and draft distinguished; the live-now mark lands on the newest published week, not the newest week; delete is offered for a draft and refused for a published week; navigating away from a dirty editor raises the guard and each of its three actions does what it says; duplicate produces a new week rather than mutating the source; present mode renders for a non-admin signed-in user while the editor does not.

## Out of Scope

- The Study and entry point records, resolution, rules, indexes and the three reader states — all #856.
- Any public archive. Students scan and read on the spot.
- Reaching the weeks index from the native app. Undecided, and would be its own piece of work.
- Restoring shared opening and closing Sections for split weeks.

## Further Notes

The design is six static artboards in `docs/design/bible-study-index/`, with values lifted from the app rather than approximated — Lexend and Plus Jakarta Sans, the Ink palette, 24px cards, 14px panels, 44px rows, the 232px rail. The Romans week titles and body copy in them are realistic sample content, not final copy.

The artboards were sized against the app's real desktop shell (1440x900) and phone width (390); the editor's third pane is tight, which is why the live preview phone is sized down from the shipped design.

title: Bible study: Entry point + Study records, and what a scan resolves to (#822, part 1 of 2)
label: CLOSED
body:
Part 1 of 2 for #822. Design and decisions: [ADR 0011](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-bible-study-entry-points.md), merged in #854. Glossary: **Entry point**, **Study**, **Meeting** in `CONTEXT.md`.

This part adds the records and the resolution chain. It ships no new screens — part 2 covers those.

## Problem Statement

A student scans the QR at Wednesday Bible Study and reaches a page. Which page they reach is decided entirely by which **Meeting** was published most recently, because that is the only thing the product can name. There is no **Study** record — the study is a string frozen in editor component state — and nothing owns the URL a QR points at. So:

- A Full-timer cannot start a new Study without a code change.
- Unpublishing this week silently shows last week's reading as though it were current, with nothing saying so.
- Between terms, a scan has no honest thing to say.
- The QR shown today encodes nothing at all — it is a hand-drawn SVG — and the URL it displays is on a domain the ministry does not own.

## Solution

A QR encodes a durable **Entry point** — a permanent slug such as `/s/cisa-wednesday` that names a standing invitation, not a term's content. It resolves through whichever **Study** is currently active to that Study's newest published **Meeting**.

The code never changes. Starting the spring study is a change of which Study is active. A scan that arrives before this week is published gets the most recent week **with its date stated**, never silently. A scan between terms says so plainly.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer, I want the Bible study QR to stay the same code forever, so that I never have to regenerate or re-show a new one each week.
2. As a Full-timer, I want to start a new Study for a new term without anyone changing code, so that the ministry is not blocked on a developer in January.
3. As a Full-timer, I want the entry point to keep working across terms, so that a code students have already used does not go dead.
4. As a Full-timer, I want unpublishing this week to fall back to the previous week visibly, so that I can pull a week back without misleading anyone who scans.
5. As a Full-timer, I want to know that a Meeting I have published may already be on a student's screen, so that deleting one is a deliberate two-step act.
6. As a Full-timer, I want a link I can text to a student who missed a week, so that I can send them one specific week without building them an archive.
7. As a student, I want to scan the same code every week and get this week's reading, so that I never have to find a new link.
8. As a student, I want the page to tell me when I am looking at an older week, so that I do not work through the wrong reading by accident.
9. As a student scanning before the study starts, I want to be told the week is not up yet, so that I do not think the app is broken.
10. As a student scanning a brand-new study's code, I want to be told nothing has been published yet, so that the empty page is explained.
11. As a student scanning between terms, I want to be told the study picks up again later, so that I know to keep the code.
12. As a student, I want the reading to work without signing in, so that scanning a code is the whole interaction.
13. As a student, I want the page never to ask me for anything, so that a **Prompt** stays something the room answers out loud.
14. As a Full-timer, I want the QR to point at the ministry's real production domain regardless of which build I am running, so that I never show a `localhost` or preview URL to a room.
15. As a Full-timer running the study in two rooms, I want a second entry point rather than a split week, so that each room's leader shows their own code from their own phone.
16. As a developer, I want the whole resolution chain in one pure function, so that every one of these states is testable without mocking Firestore.
17. As a developer, I want the reader to render a discriminated union rather than branch on nulls, so that a new state cannot be silently unhandled.
18. As a Full-timer, I want an unlisted staff permalink rather than a public archive, so that students are not invited to browse past weeks the ministry did not intend to publish as a library.

## Implementation Decisions

**Two new records.**

- A **Study** carries a title, a term label, and its identity. It is the named arc ("Romans, Fall 2026") a set of Meetings belongs to.
- An **Entry point** carries a slug (its identity), a display name, and the id of the Study currently active on it. Exactly one Study is active per entry point at a time.
- Both live in their own top-level collections beside `bible_study_meetings`.

**The entry point is standalone.** It is deliberately not bound to a **Rhythm**: a Rhythm is derived from an anchor `Event` via `parentEventId` and has no identity of its own, so binding would mean persisting an opaque event id and depending on that anchor surviving. Rejected in ADR 0011.

**Resolution is one pure function**, living beside the existing Meeting parsing and reader reducer, returning a discriminated union. Shape (this encodes the decisions more precisely than prose):

```
resolveScan(entryPoint, study, meetings, today, permalinkDate)
  -> { kind: 'meeting', meeting, isFallback: boolean, fallbackDate?: string }
   | { kind: 'never-published' }
   | { kind: 'no-active-study' }
```

The existing `currentMeeting` helper folds into it. `isFallback` is true when the returned Meeting is not the one whose date matches the current week — the reader states `fallbackDate` rather than implying it.

**Three reader states, deliberately distinct.** Falling back to an older week during a term is correct; saying the same thing in January is not. The entry point knowing whether it has an active Study is what separates them.

**Publish semantics.** Unpublishing is permitted and falls back with the date shown. A Meeting may be hard-deleted only while unpublished — the enforcement lives in the rules, not only the UI.

**`siblingId` is removed** from the Meeting type, the data mapper, and `firestore.rules`. It was declared in three places with behavior in none. Splits are two entry points (part 2 adds the duplicate action that populates the second).

**Routes.** `/s/:slug` is the public reader and takes an entry-point slug. `/study/:studyId/:date` is a staff permalink: public but unlisted, carrying `noindex`, and linked from nowhere. It is public because the Firestore rule already serves any published Meeting to anyone — gating the UI would misrepresent an open door as protected.

**Security rules.** Entry points and Studies are publicly readable (anonymous resolution requires both) and writable only by Full-timers. Meeting rules keep their existing public-read-when-published shape, lose `siblingId` validation, and gain the unpublished-only constraint on delete.

**Two composite indexes** on `bible_study_meetings`: `(studyId, published, date desc)` for the reader, and `(studyId, date desc)` for part 2's index screen. The first cannot serve the second — Firestore requires the equality fields to be a prefix, so `published` cannot be skipped. Both go in `firestore.indexes.json`, which CI publishes to `prod` and `qa-db` on merge.

**QR origin** comes from a new `VITE_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, defaulting to the production URL, documented in `.env.example` alongside the existing `VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN` note that solves the same prod/QA domain split. Never `window.location.origin`. Part 2 consumes it; part 1 introduces and documents it.

**A seed script** creates a Study and an entry point, following the existing one-off script conventions in the repo. Without it there is no way to create either record until part 2 ships, and part 1 cannot be verified on its own.

**No migration.** Existing `romans-fall26` content is test data and is deleted rather than adopted.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts what someone scanning or authoring would observe — which Meeting comes back, whether the date is stated, which of the three states renders — never how the resolution is computed or which Firestore call was made.

**Seams — no new ones.** The repo already has the right shape and this reuses it:

- **The pure module** holding Meeting parsing and the reader reducer gains `resolveScan`. This is the highest seam and the primary one: every decision in this spec is exercised here with plain data and no mocks. Prior art is the existing direct tests of `parseMeeting`, `currentMeeting` and `readerReducer`.
- **The Bible study data module** is the data seam, and gains the Study and entry-point reads/writes. Views mock this module wholesale; the module itself is tested against a mocked `firebase/firestore`. Prior art: the existing data-module test and the reader view test that mocks it.
- **The rules suite** covers the new collections' public-read/admin-write shape and delete-only-while-unpublished. Prior art: the existing rules tests. Note these need JDK 21 and skip silently without it — only CI proves a rules change.

Cases that must be covered: newest published wins; an older Meeting is returned as a fallback with its date when this week is unpublished; nothing ever published; no active Study; a dated permalink resolving inside the active Study; a dated permalink for a week that does not exist.

## Out of Scope

- The `/bible-study` weeks index, the editor rewrite, the unsaved-changes guard, present mode, and QR generation — all part 2.
- Any public archive of past weeks. Students scan and read on the spot.
- Reaching the weeks index from the native app.
- The shared-opening-and-closing behaviour the old split design promised.

## Further Notes

The QR displayed today is decorative — a hand-authored 21x21 SVG with fixed paths, identical regardless of the URL beside it, with no QR library in `package.json`. Nothing that has been shown to a room has ever been scannable. That is fixed in part 2, but it is worth knowing that this part changes nothing a student can currently reach, because there is nothing they can currently reach.

title: Spec: Password Visibility Toggle and First-Run Walkthrough Enhancements
label: CLOSED
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Problem Statement

Users and external testers evaluating CISA Campus Work Tracker encountered two primary usability and onboarding friction points:
1. When signing in with email and password, users cannot verify what they typed, leading to login errors and user frustration.
2. New users joining campus teams lack immediate visual progress feedback during their initial onboarding habits, making it harder to gauge what is expected of them in their first week or to revisit getting-started guidance once dismissed.

## Solution

1. Provide an accessible show/hide password visibility toggle directly inside the sign-in password input field, allowing users to toggle between obscured and plaintext input.
2. Deepen the existing role-aware first-run onboarding checklist (`FirstRunCard`) by introducing a clear visual progress bar and step indicators ("X of Y complete"), and provide an explicit affordance in Settings to restore the getting-started checklist if a user previously dismissed it.

## User Stories

1. As an unauthenticated user, I want to toggle password visibility with a single tap or click in the sign-in form, so that I can verify my input and prevent mistyped passwords.
2. As a screen reader user, I want the password visibility toggle to announce its current state via descriptive accessible labels (e.g. "Show password" vs "Hide password"), so that I understand whether my password is visible.
3. As an unauthenticated user, I want toggling password visibility to retain focus on the password field, so that I can continue typing without re-focusing.
4. As an unauthenticated user, I want the visibility state to automatically reset back to obscured whenever the form is submitted, so that my credential is not accidentally exposed.
5. As a new campus trainee or full-timer, I want to see a visual progress indicator on the First-Run card on my home screen, so that I have a clear sense of how far along I am in finding my feet with the app.
6. As a user working through the onboarding checklist, I want the progress bar to dynamically reflect live app activities (contacts added, conversations logged, prayers offered) without manual ticking, so that the checklist always tells the truth about my progress.
7. As a user who accidentally dismissed or put away the getting-started checklist, I want a control in Settings under Preferences/Help to bring it back to my home screen, so that I can revisit guidance for my role.
8. As a user who completed all first-run checklist tasks, I want the card to quietly disappear once fully complete, so that it does not create clutter on my daily dashboard.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Password Toggle Component**: Update the sign-in email/password form with an eye icon toggle button positioned inside the password input container. Use SVG eye/eye-off icons from the existing icon library (`lucide-react`).
- **Input Type Switch**: Toggle the input element's `type` between `"password"` and `"text"`.
- **Button Semantics**: The toggle button must specify `type="button"` so it does not trigger form submission on enter/space, and include `aria-label` changing dynamically based on state.
- **First-Run Progress Meter**: Enhance `FirstRunCard` to include an accessible progress meter (`role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin="0"`, `aria-valuemax="totalCount"`) showing visual progress calculated from `doneCount / totalCount`.
- **First-Run Revisit Affordance**: Provide a "Show getting started checklist" action in Settings that calls `FirstRunStore.bringBack(key)` and alerts the user that the card has returned to their home screen.
- **Out-of-scope Items**: Public App Store Optimization (ASO) and Play Store "Rate our app" prompts are explicitly rejected (`wontfix`) as this is a private, administratively provisioned ministry coordination workspace.

## Testing Decisions

- Only test user-visible behavior and accessibility roles, avoiding assertions on private internal state.
- **Password Form Behavior**:
  - Test initial render has `type="password"` and label "Show password".
  - Test clicking toggle transforms input to `type="text"` and updates label to "Hide password".
  - Test clicking again reverts back to `type="password"`.
- **First-Run Checklist Behavior**:
  - Test that `FirstRunCard` renders the progress meter with correct completion percentage and aria attributes.
  - Test that clicking "Put this away" invokes dismissal and hides the card.
  - Test that calling `FirstRunStore.bringBack(key)` restores visibility.
- **Prior Art**: Existing test suites in `src/test/App.test.tsx` and `src/test/FirstRun.test.tsx`.

## Out of Scope

- Overlay or spotlight tours that darken the screen with multi-step popovers (these break across layout updates and conflict with the app's reactive philosophy).
- Public ASO optimizations or public app store rating prompts.
- Modifying authentication credential handling in Firebase Auth backend.

## Further Notes

- Document the First-Run Checklist definition in `CONTEXT.md`.
- Record ADR 0010 documenting the architectural preference for reactive in-situ checklists over overlay walkthroughs.

title: E2E: announcements wizard spec waits on an "e.g. Campus News" placeholder that no longer exists
label: CLOSED
body:
`e2e/announcements-flow.spec.ts:41` does:

```ts
await page.getByPlaceholder(/e\.g\. campus news/i).fill(announcementTitle);
```

and times out after 30s. Grepping `src/` (components, views and `src/locales/en.json`) finds **no** "campus news" string anywhere, so the step-1 field of the announcement wizard no longer carries that placeholder — it was renamed, replaced, or the wizard step changed shape.

Because the spec is `mode: 'serial'`, this failure also skips the two tests after it (`:95` Trainee rail/thread view, `:163` Full-timer read receipts), so one stale selector costs three tests.

**This is a pre-existing failure**: it failed identically on the 3 Sep nightly (run 33713854618), so it is unrelated to the recent What's New popup work.

**Fix direction**

Open the wizard, read what step 1 actually renders, and re-point the locator — preferably at a label or role rather than a placeholder string, so a copy change doesn't break it again. Then re-check the two dependent tests, which have not run in some time and may have drifted too.

Found while investigating the nightly "Web E2E (Playwright)" failures.

title: E2E: mobile contact-editing spec fills a last-name field that is hidden behind a disclosure
label: CLOSED
body:
`e2e/mobile-and-pwa-contact-editing.spec.ts:43` fills `getByPlaceholder(/e\.g\. johnson/i)` and times out (30s).

The field exists, but it is inside the collapsed optional-details disclosure in `src/components/modals/NewContactModal.tsx`:

```tsx
<button type="button" onClick={() => setShowMore(prev => !prev)}>
  {showMore ? '− Show less' : '+ Add the rest (optional details)'}
</button>

{showMore && (
  ...
    <input ... placeholder="e.g. Johnson" />   // :384  LAST NAME
```

The spec fills first name (always visible) fine, then waits forever on last name because it never clicks the disclosure. Phone (`(555) 000-0000`, line 44) is presumably in the same collapsed block and would fail next.

**This is a pre-existing failure**: it also failed on the 3 Sep nightly (run 33713854618) with the identical error, so it is unrelated to the recent What's New popup work.

**Fix direction**

Have the spec expand the disclosure before filling optional fields:

```ts
await page.getByRole('button', { name: /add the rest/i }).click();
```

Worth checking whether the mobile flow is meant to surface last name / phone without an extra tap before settling on the test-side fix.

`e2e/settings-and-partners.spec.ts:11` asserts `getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Settings' })` is visible for the Full-timer (admin). It fails with `element(s) not found` after 15s. `src/views/Settings.tsx` has exactly one `

`, at `:2425`, and it sits inside the **non-manager** branch: ```tsx // ── Non-manager: a warm "My profile" page ── if (!isManager) { return (

{t('settings.title', 'Settings')}

``` The manager/admin view renders only `

` section headers ("Account & Session", "Appearance", "Navigation", "Notifications & Alerts", "Language", "What's New", "Roles & access", …), confirmed in the failure snapshot — it contains no `level=1` heading at all. So this assertion cannot pass for an admin regardless of timing. **This is a pre-existing failure**: it also failed on the 3 Sep nightly (run 33713854618) with the identical error, i.e. it is not related to the recent What's New popup work. **Fix direction** Decide which is right, then make them agree: - Give the admin Settings view an `

title: E2E: mobile-viewport spec times out on /support — page renders no main landmark
label: CLOSED
body:
`e2e/mobile-viewport.spec.ts:30` walks a list of routes and waits for `[aria-label="Main Navigation"], main, [role="main"]` on each. It times out (30s) on `/support`.

`src/views/Support.tsx` renders as a standalone page: no `<main>`, no `role="main"`, and no app shell / Main Navigation. `src/views/PrivacyPolicy.tsx` has the same shape, so `/privacy` — the next route in the list — would fail immediately after this one is unblocked.

**Evidence**

Failure snapshot from run 33921288704 is the Support page, with a "Back to Application" button and `heading "App Support & Help Center" [level=1]`, and no landmark the selector matches.

`src/views/Support.tsx` was last touched by `d79ac42` (#807, "off-palette pages"), which landed after the 3 Sep nightly (`67a8142`) where this spec still passed.

**Two ways to close it**

1. Give the standalone pages a `<main>` landmark. This is the accessibility-correct option — every page should expose one — and fixes both routes.
2. Or teach the spec that `/support` and `/privacy` are shell-less and wait on their own root element instead.

Option 1 is preferable; the overflow assertion the spec actually makes is still worth running on these pages.

Found while investigating the nightly "Web E2E (Playwright)" failures.

title: E2E: contact "Edit details" button moved into the More actions menu, breaking 2 board specs
label: CLOSED
body:
Two nightly E2E specs look for a visible `Edit details` button on the contact details modal. That affordance no longer exists as a top-level button — the contact-detail rework (`0d29333`, #783) moved editing into the "More actions" overflow menu (`MoreMenu`, `aria-label="More actions"`), with a separate "Edit" pill on the mobile header.

**Failing tests**

- `e2e/the-journey-board.spec.ts:67` — `getByRole('button', { name: /^edit details$/i })`
- `e2e/cross-role-journey.spec.ts:91` — `getByRole('button', { name: /edit details/i })`

Both fail with `Error: element(s) not found` after 5s.

**Evidence**

The failure snapshot shows the modal opening correctly and the edit entry point absent:

```yaml
- heading "Lila Chen" [level=2]
- button "More actions"
- button "Close"
- button "Overview"
```

Current source: `src/components/modals/ContactDetailsModal.tsx:1385` passes `onEdit` into `<MoreMenu>`; `:1255` is the mobile-only "Edit" pill. The only literal "Edit details" strings are a heading (`:1232`, `:1334`) and the `MoreMenu` item, which is not rendered until the menu is opened.

**Both specs passed** on the 3 Sep nightly (run 33713854618, `67a8142`) and fail from the 4 Sep run onward (33919424278, `92a7fcd`) — `0d29333` landed in that window.

**Fix direction**

Update both specs to open "More actions" first and click the `Edit details` item, e.g.

```ts
await page.getByRole('button', { name: /more actions/i }).click();
await page.getByRole('menuitem', { name: /^edit details$/i }).click();
```

(confirm the item's real role/name against `MoreMenu`). Alternatively, if a direct edit affordance is wanted back in the header, that is a UI decision to make first.

title: feat: tailor-made What's New popups with release note compilation and git commit fallback
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

When new features and bug fixes ship across both the desktop web PWA and mobile apps, users currently have no clear, user-facing notice explaining what has changed. Furthermore, raw developer commit messages and PR titles can be overly technical or jargon-heavy, so release notes need to be easily tailored, platform-targeted, and displayed automatically on launch after updates while remaining accessible on demand.

## Solution

Implement an in-repo What's New Announcement pipeline and UI for both Web PWA and Expo Mobile:
1. Manifests authored in Markdown with YAML frontmatter in `content/whats-new/<releaseId>.md`.
2. A CLI script `npm run whats-new:draft` that drafts starter release notes by parsing git commits (`feat`, `fix`) since the previous release.
3. A build script `npm run whats-new:compile` that compiles all release markdown files into a lightweight, sorted JSON manifest distributed to both web and mobile assets, with fallback commit parsing if no manual file exists.
4. An auto-popup modal triggered on app launch if the newest release ID is newer than `lastSeenWhatsNewId` in local storage, plus an on-demand "What's New" viewer in Settings.

## User Stories

1. As a Trainee or Full-timer opening the web PWA after an update, I want a "What's New" popup to appear automatically, so that I immediately learn about new features and workflow improvements.
2. As a mobile app user opening the app after an update, I want the same "What's New" announcement formatted nicely for mobile, so that I can see the latest additions on the go.
3. As a user who has already seen the announcement for version X, I do not want the popup to show again every time I refresh or open the app, so that it does not disrupt my work.
4. As a user who dismissed the popup, I want to open "What's New" from Settings whenever I want, so that I can re-read feature instructions or announcements.
5. As an author writing release notes, I want to tag specific bullet points or releases with platform tags (e.g. `[Web]` or `[Mobile]`), so that mobile users only see notes relevant to mobile and web users only see notes relevant to web.
6. As an engineer or agent preparing a new release, I want to run `npm run whats-new:draft` to automatically generate a markdown draft from recent git commits, so that I can quickly polish user-friendly copy without starting from a blank page.
7. As an engineer building the app, I want markdown notes compiled into static JSON at build time, so that neither web nor mobile bundles heavy markdown parsing libraries at runtime.
8. As a user offline or on a poor connection, I want the What's New announcement to display instantly without waiting for network requests to Firestore.

## Implementation Decisions

1. **Content Schema & Storage**:
   - In-repo markdown files with frontmatter (`id`, `version`, `title`, `date`, `platforms`) placed in `content/whats-new/*.md`.
   - Build-time compiler converts markdown to structured JSON items with parsed platform tags.
2. **Drafting CLI**:
   - `scripts/draft-whats-new.ts` runnable via `npm run whats-new:draft` parses git commits since the last tag into categorized sections.
3. **Compilation Script**:
   - `scripts/compile-whats-new.ts` runnable via `npm run whats-new:compile` (hooked into `build`) outputs to `src/generated/whats-new.json` and `apps/mobile/assets/whats-new.json`.
4. **Client Services & State**:
   - Web storage helper using `localStorage` key `cisa.whats_new.last_seen_id`.
   - Mobile storage helper using `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` key `cisa.whats_new.last_seen_id`.
   - Responsive UI modals: Tailwind dialog for web PWA with backdrop, and native React Native modal for mobile.
   - Settings integration: Add "What's New" item under Settings / More in both web and mobile.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior at unit and integration seams:
  - Compilation script: converts valid markdown files into sorted JSON, strips/parses platform annotations accurately, and generates fallback if empty.
  - Seen tracking logic: correctly determines if popup should open given current release ID and stored seen ID, and records dismissal.
  - Web UI: modal renders latest unread announcement, respects platform filters, and closes upon clicking "Got it".
  - Mobile UI: modal renders announcement for mobile platform and persists seen state.
- Prior art: existing Vitest tests in `src/test/` and Jest tests in `apps/mobile/__tests__/`.

## Out of Scope

- Remote cloud CMS / Firestore live authoring without deployment (per ADR 0008).
- Multi-language i18n translation of release notes in the initial iteration (plain English).

## Further Notes

- Documented in ADR 0008 (`docs/adr/0008-custom-whats-new-announcements.md`) and domain glossary (`CONTEXT.md`).
