title: Contact detail: reclaim the working area (delete the aside, compress the chrome, pane the threads)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

A Full-timer on a 1107×662 laptop opened a contact at `/people/:contactId` and could not comfortably work in it: "the contact detail it's hard to edit because the window is very small, for example discussion, I have to scroll up and down."

The measurement bears this out. At that viewport, in the rail shell, the page gives the user a working area of **220 × 435 px**:

- The 320px aside takes 41% of the usable width, leaving the main column 435px. The edit form's two-column breakpoint is a *viewport* breakpoint (`md:`), so at 1107px it goes two-up inside 435px — roughly 200px per field.
- 274px of the main column's 494px height is permanently pinned chrome: a ~166px head (the Call / Text / Email / Log interaction pills sit inside it), a 48px tab bar, and a ~60px footer whose job is a "Done" button on a page that is a route.
- A `min-h-[400px]` wrapper around the tab panels forces a scrollbar even on an empty tab.
- `.cd-page` is `height: 100%` inside a `main` that carries bottom padding, so the percentage resolves against the content box and the padding is added below it — a ~32px parasitic outer scroll on top of the inner one.
- `Thread` renders its message list in document flow and puts the composer *after* it, with no internal scroller. In a 220px window with a real Discussion, the "add a comment" box sits below every message. That is literally the reported "scroll up and down".

The same squeeze affects every tab, not only Discussion. Discussion is simply where it bites hardest.

## Solution

Give the contact detail page back its room, without adding anything to it. Four moves, all subtractive:

1. **Delete the 320px aside.** Its five sections — how to reach, where they are, cared for by, who else can see, tags — move into the Overview tab, which becomes the record's landing page. The main column goes from 435px to 779px at every width, and the rail's 232/76px collapse no longer changes the answer.
2. **Compress the head to a single 56px row**: avatar, name, stage, "Last connected … · Cared for by …", and a compact icon cluster on the right (Call / Text / Email, plus an overflow for Log interaction and Move step). Ownership stays visible at a glance from every tab, which is what the aside used to provide.
3. **Delete the footer.** "Done" goes — this is a route with a back affordance, not a modal. "Delete contact" moves to the end of Overview as a bordered danger block, where a destructive action gets the friction of a scroll. Save and Cancel become a 52px footer that renders **only while editing**.
4. **Let chat-shaped tabs own their height.** Discussion and Follow up become fill panes: the message list scrolls inside the pane, the composer is pinned to its bottom, and the pane opens scrolled to the newest message. Every other tab keeps flowing in the single content scroller.

Result at the reported viewport: **220 × 435 → 422 × 779**. Height +92%, width +79%.

The design of record is the canvas at `docs/design/contact-detail/` (four artboards at 1107×662, values lifted from the real stylesheet and component source rather than invented).

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer on a 13-inch laptop, I want the contact detail page's content region to be more than a fifth of my screen, so that I can read and work in a person's record without constant scrolling.
2. As a Full-timer, I want the Discussion composer to stay visible while I read the thread, so that I can respond to what the team said without scrolling back down to find the box.
3. As a Full-timer, I want Discussion to open on the newest message, so that I can see what the team said most recently without scrolling.
4. As a Trainee, I want the Follow up thread to behave the same way as Discussion, so that I don't have to learn two interaction models for two visually identical panes.
5. As a Trainee, I want the edit form's fields to be wide enough to read their contents, so that I can check a phone number or an Instagram handle without selecting the text.
6. As a Trainee, I want the edit form to lay out in two columns based on the space actually available, so that collapsing the navigation rail widens my fields instead of doing nothing.
7. As a Trainee editing a contact, I want Save and Cancel to stay reachable while I scroll the form, so that I never have to hunt for them.
8. As a Trainee, I want the Save/Cancel footer to disappear when I'm not editing, so that the height it costs is only spent when it's earning something.
9. As a Full-timer, I want to see who a person is cared for by from any tab, so that I know whose person this is without clicking into a tab.
10. As a Trainee, I want a person's name, stage and last-connected date visible at all times, so that I keep my bearings while moving between tabs.
11. As a Trainee, I want Call, Text and Email reachable from the head on every tab, so that acting on a contact never requires navigating first.
12. As a Trainee, I want Log interaction and Move step available from an overflow in the head, so that the common actions stay one click away without a row of buttons eating the viewport.
13. As a Full-timer, I want all of a person's profile fields — how to reach them, where they are, who cares for them, who else can see them, their tags — in one place, so that I have a single read view that pairs with the edit form.
14. As a Full-timer, I want Overview to be the page's landing tab, so that opening a person shows me the record rather than a preview of the tab beside it.
14a. As a Full-timer, I want every open prayer for a person visible on Overview, so that I can see what we are still holding without scanning the Prayer tab's answered and closed entries.
15. As a Trainee, I want the tab bar to fit its tabs without scrolling sideways, so that I can reach History and Prayer without discovering a hidden scroll.
16. As a Trainee, I want the tab order I already know to stay the same, so that my muscle memory keeps working.
17. As a Full-timer, I want "Delete contact" to require scrolling to the end of Overview, so that a destructive action is never adjacent to "Call".
18. As a Trainee, I want an empty tab to show as empty rather than forcing a scrollbar, so that the page tells me the truth about how much is there.
19. As a Trainee, I want the page to have exactly one scrollbar, so that a stray 32px outer scroll doesn't fight the inner one under my trackpad.
20. As a viewer-role user, I want the page's read-only behaviour unchanged, so that nothing about my access changes with this layout work.
21. As a Trainee on mobile, I want the contact sheet's editing flow to keep working exactly as it does today, so that a desktop layout fix doesn't destabilise the flow I use in the field.
22. As a Full-timer, I want deep links from a notification or the attention feed to keep landing on the right tab, so that `?tab=thread` still works.
23. As a Trainee, I want the page to keep the visual vocabulary of the rest of the app — the floating slab, the token palette, the type ramp — so that it doesn't read as a different product.
24. As a Full-timer with a narrow window, I want the profile fields to stay reachable when there's no room for two columns, so that shrinking the window degrades gracefully rather than hiding data.
25. As a developer, I want the phantom-scroll defect to be guarded by a test, so that a future change can't silently reintroduce it.

## Implementation Decisions

**Scope is the desktop `.cd-page` layout.** The mobile `.cdm-page` full-screen sheet keeps its current structure. ADR 0004's mobile and PWA contact editing flow is not reopened.

**The aside is removed outright**, not hidden behind a breakpoint. A conditional "Details" tab that appears and disappears as the window resizes was considered and rejected: a tab set that changes shape while you drag a window edge is disorienting, and keeping both an aside and a tab means two render paths for the same content. The five aside sections become part of the Overview tab panel.

**Overview absorbs the profile fields, drops "Lately", and keeps "Prayers we're holding".** Overview currently carries "What we know" (notes), "Lately" and "Prayers we're holding". These two are not the same kind of thing:

- **"Lately"** is `visibleInteractions.slice(0, 3)` — the three newest conversations, subtitled "our last few conversations". A true preview of the Interactions tab sitting next to it. **Dropped.**
- **"Prayers we're holding"** is `openPrayers` — every prayer that is neither answered nor closed. That is a *filter*, not a digest: the Prayer tab shows answered and closed entries too, so Overview is the only place open prayers are visible without scanning. **Kept**, above the profile fields. Dropping it would have made open prayers harder to find than they are today.

Overview becomes: notes, prayers we're holding, how to reach, where they are, cared for by, who else can see, tags, and the delete block. The tab keeps the name **Overview** so the existing `?tab=` vocabulary and deep links are untouched.

**The tab set and order are unchanged**: Overview · Follow up · Discussion (Full-timers only) · Interactions · Prayer · History. No reordering rides along with this change. At 779px the six tabs no longer overflow, which removes the cost that would have justified reordering.

**The head becomes a fixed-height single row** carrying avatar, name, stage, a combined "Last connected … · Cared for by …" line, and a right-aligned icon cluster (Call / Text / Email as icons, plus an overflow menu for Log interaction and Move step). The compression is unconditional — no height breakpoint — because two head layouts is a second thing to maintain and a jump the user feels while resizing. The action cluster stays in the head rather than moving to the tab bar's right edge: the tab bar is `overflow-x: auto`, so anything placed there can scroll out of reach.

**The footer is deleted in read mode and rendered only while editing**, carrying Cancel and Save. "Done" is removed entirely (the page is a route). "Delete contact" moves to the end of the Overview panel as a bordered danger block.

**Tabs declare a shape.** The content region becomes a flex column so a tab can opt into *fill* — owning the pane's height, scrolling its own list, pinning its own footer — while the default remains *flow* through the single content scroller. Discussion and Follow up are fill; Overview, Interactions, Prayer and History are flow. Interactions and Prayer open their forms from a button rather than carrying a persistent composer, so pinning would waste height nearly all the time.

**`Thread` gains a pane variant alongside its existing `compact` prop.** A variant is structurally required regardless of this change, because `Thread` has three call sites and one of them renders nested inside an interaction row, where filling the height would be wrong. Only the desktop Follow up and Discussion call sites opt in.

**Mobile's `Thread` call sites do not opt in.** Pinning a composer to the bottom of a `position: fixed; inset: 0` sheet with no `visualViewport` or `dvh` handling puts it under the iOS soft keyboard. The repository has no keyboard-avoidance plumbing, and ADR 0004 tuned that sheet for single-scroll ergonomics precisely because the in-flow composer is scrolled into view by the browser. Mobile still benefits from the shared fixes (the `min-h` floor). Pinning on mobile is a separate issue with its own testing.

**Vertical budget fixes**: the `min-h-[400px]` floor on the tab panel wrapper is removed, and `main`'s bottom padding is dropped for this route. That padding exists for the mobile bottom navigation, which the desktop rail shell does not have; removing it is what eliminates the parasitic outer scroll created by `height: 100%` resolving against a padded content box.

**Column breakpoints become container queries, not viewport queries.** Tailwind v4 is already in use. The edit form and Overview's field groups size against the column's actual width, because the navigation rail's 232px/76px collapse changes the available width without the viewport moving at all — a viewport threshold gets that wrong in both directions.

**ADR 0003's shell gutter is not touched.** The 16px track and the floating rail slab are the subject of an accepted decision; the vertical budget is recovered from the page's own chrome, not from the gutter that makes the slab read as an object.

**`ContactDetailsModal` keeps its filename.** It has not been a modal since `/people/:contactId` became a route, and the name is misleading, but renaming a 2,700-line file in the same commit as a layout change would bury the diff. The rename earns its own commit.

**A new ADR (0006) records this**: the aside's deletion, the chrome compression, the tab-shape model, and the mobile deferral. It is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts what a user can observe — that the profile fields are reachable from Overview, that Save appears only while editing, that the composer precedes nothing in the Discussion pane — and not how the layout is achieved. Assertions on class names, computed styles, or element nesting are implementation details and do not belong; jsdom has no layout engine, so any test phrased in pixels would be asserting on a fiction.

**Primary seam: `src/test/ContactDetailsModal.test.tsx`** — the existing, highest-level seam. It already renders the whole page with Firestore, auth and threads mocked, and every behavioural change in this spec is observable through it:

- Overview renders the person's phone, email, Instagram, location, owner, co-viewers and tags.
- The tab set and its order; Discussion is present for a Full-timer and absent for a Trainee.
- "Delete contact" is inside the Overview panel, not in persistent page chrome.
- Save and Cancel are absent in read mode and present while editing.
- The owner's name is present in the head without opening a tab.
- In the Discussion pane, the composer follows the message list in DOM order and both are within the pane.
- An empty tab renders its empty state without a forced minimum height.

**Existing seam reused: `src/test/Thread.test.tsx`** for the pane variant's own behaviour — that the default and `compact` renderings are unchanged, and that only the pane variant pins its composer.

**One guardrail, in the pattern of `src/test/accentToken.test.ts`**: that file exists because a token regression was invisible until 227 usages went dead, and it reads `src/index.css` directly rather than relying on jsdom's CSS support. The phantom-scroll defect is the same class of problem — invisible to every behavioural test, silently reintroduced by anyone who restores the bottom padding. A single assertion in that style guards the invariant. This is deliberately a guardrail, not a layout test: it asserts one relationship, not the design.

Prior art for all three patterns is already in `src/test/`; no new seam, harness or helper is introduced.

## Out of Scope

- **Pinning the composer on mobile.** Needs `visualViewport`/`dvh` keyboard handling that does not exist in this repository and that ADR 0004's sheet assumes the absence of. Separate issue.
- **Any change to the mobile `.cdm-page` sheet's structure**, beyond what it inherits from shared components.
- **Renaming `ContactDetailsModal`** to reflect that it is a page. Noted in the ADR, done in its own commit.
- **Reordering the tabs.**
- **Extending `?tab=` to accept every tab value.** It currently honours only `thread`; that is a pre-existing limitation, unchanged here and worth its own issue.
- **The navigation rail, the chrome strip, and ADR 0003's shell gutter.**
- **Any change to roles, permissions, or what Trainees versus Full-timers can see.**
- **Backfilling the `owner` field**; the head's "Cared for by" uses the same resolution the aside used, legacy fallback included.

## Further Notes

The design of record is the canvas at `docs/design/contact-detail/` — four artboards (`Today`, `Main`/Frame, `Panes`, `Editing`) at 1107×662, with every colour, radius, type size and control height lifted from `src/index.css` and the real component source. Per ADR 0003, the canvas is normative for shell chrome and `docs/design/DRIFT.md` is the register when the build diverges from it; a DRIFT entry is the right response if the built page ends up differing from these boards.

**Both questions that were open when this spec was first filed are now settled**, and [ADR 0006](../adr/0006-contact-detail-frame-and-tab-shapes.md) records the decision as Accepted:

1. **The aside's content moves into Overview as designed.** The cost is accepted knowingly: on Interactions, Prayer, Discussion or History you can no longer glance right for a phone number. "Cared for by" — the one fact people actually graze on — is promoted into the 56px head, so it stays on screen from every tab.
2. **"Lately" is dropped; "Prayers we're holding" stays.** See the implementation decision above — the second is a filter rather than a preview, and removing it would have been a regression dressed up as a simplification.

The head's height was initially estimated at ~100px during design discussion; drawing it from its real CSS showed ~166px, because the action pills sit inside `cd-head-main` rather than beside it. The 220px figure in the Problem Statement is the corrected number.

Glossary: **Discussion** was added to `CONTEXT.md` as part of this work — the Full-timers-only thread on a contact, distinct from **Follow up** (the Trainee/gospel-partner thread on the same page), from a Bible study **Prompt** of kind *Discuss*, and from **Questions for the team** at `/questions`.

title: Gatherings page: align the figures card, and fold a Rhythm into one row with the term at a glance (spec for #765)
label: CLOSED
body:
Spec for #765. Design settled in a grilling session; the canvas concept that preceded it is at `docs/design/gathering-page/` (it predates the last three rounds — read this spec, not the artboards, where they disagree).

## Problem Statement

Two complaints, one page (`/attendance`).

**The figures card is misaligned.** Beside "Who we've missed lately" sits a card holding three numbers. Its top edge sits ~48px above the person cards it is supposed to line up with, and it runs on past their bottom. Inside it, the three figures have no space between them and read as one block of numbers.

**A Rhythm is unfindable.** Recurring Gatherings are created for the whole term at once — which works, and should keep working. But "When we met" lists every Gathering newest-first, so a Rhythm running to December puts its *last* occurrence at the top and buries this week's a dozen rows down, wearing the same name as everything above it. Future Gatherings also sit in a list called "when we met", where they do not belong. A Full-timer opening the page to take attendance for tonight has to hunt for it.

Today the team runs three Rhythms: Bible Study on Wednesday, Bible Study on Thursday, and College Meeting on Thursday.

## Solution

**Alignment.** Lift the section heading out of the left column so it spans both, leaving the person cards and the figures card starting on the same line. Stop the grid stretching the figures card, and keep it in view while the list scrolls. Separate the three figures with hairlines so each gets its own line.

**Rhythms.** Stop listing a Rhythm as N rows. A Rhythm becomes one row carrying its own term at a glance: a strip with one chip per Gathering in time order, showing which have had attendance taken, which is this week, and which are still ahead — plus one control that returns the selection to the current week. Above the list, a "This week" band names the Gatherings falling in the current Monday–Sunday week, so taking attendance for tonight is the first thing on the page rather than something to search for.

For that glance to be truthful, a Gathering must be able to say attendance was taken. It cannot today: attendance lives on the Contact, so "we held it and nobody came" and "nobody has opened this" are the same empty answer.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer, I want the figures card to start on the same line as the person cards beside it, so that the section reads as one composed row rather than two things that slipped.
2. As a Full-timer, I want the figures card to stop stretching to the height of the list next to it, so that it is sized by its own content.
3. As a Full-timer, I want the figures card to stay in view while I scroll a long list of people we've missed, so that the totals stay available as context.
4. As a Full-timer, I want each of the three figures separated from the next, so that I can read one number without reading all three.
5. As a Full-timer, I want the "Who we've missed lately" heading to sit above both columns, so that it is obvious it titles the whole section and not just the left half.
6. As a Full-timer opening the page on a gathering day, I want this week's Gatherings named at the top of the page, so that I can start marking attendance without looking for them.
7. As a Full-timer, I want the week to run Monday to Sunday, so that a Sunday-evening Gathering belongs to the week it followed rather than the one starting.
8. As a Full-timer, I want the two Thursday Gatherings stacked under one Thursday heading, so that I mark both in one sitting instead of finding them separately.
9. As a Full-timer, I want a week with no Gatherings to say so plainly, so that an empty band reads as "nothing on" rather than as a page that failed to load.
10. As a Full-timer, I want a recurring Bible Study to occupy one row rather than seventeen, so that the list of what we do is as short as the number of things we actually do.
11. As a Full-timer, I want each Rhythm row to show every Gathering in the term as one chip, so that I can see the whole arc without opening anything.
12. As a Full-timer, I want a chip to show whether attendance has been taken for that Gathering, so that gaps in the term are visible at a glance.
13. As a Full-timer, I want this week's chip marked distinctly from the rest, so that I can find the current week by looking rather than by counting dates.
14. As a Full-timer, I want Gatherings still ahead shown faintly, so that I can tell what has happened from what has not.
15. As a Full-timer, I want one control that returns the strip to the current week, so that I can get back after looking at October.
16. As a Full-timer, I want to select any chip and see that Gathering's summary without leaving the row, so that checking an earlier week is not a navigation.
17. As a Full-timer, I want a marked chip to show how many of the expected roster came, so that a thin week is visible without opening it.
18. As a Full-timer, I want Rhythm rows ordered by day of week and to stay in that order, so that I learn where Wednesday lives and stop reading the page.
19. As a Full-timer, I want one-off Gatherings listed separately below the Rhythms, so that a Welcome BBQ is not filed among things that repeat.
20. As a Full-timer, I want future Gatherings out of "When we met", so that a past-tense list holds only things that happened.
21. As a Full-timer, I want to record that a Gathering was held and nobody came, so that an empty room is a fact rather than an absence of data.
22. As a Full-timer, I want to see who took attendance for a Gathering and when, so that I know whether a blank week is unrecorded or genuinely empty.
23. As a Full-timer, I want the expected roster to belong to the Rhythm rather than to each week, so that setting up "who usually comes" is done once per Rhythm.
24. As a Full-timer, I want to change one week's roster without changing the Rhythm's, so that a one-off guest does not become a regular.
25. As a Full-timer, I want the roster change prompt to stop asking "this one or all future?" on every edit, so that ordinary marking is not interrupted by a decision.
26. As a Full-timer, I want a Rhythm row to say how many are expected, so that "12 came" has a denominator.
27. As a Trainee, I want to open the page and see what is on this week without admin rights, so that I know what to turn up to.
28. As a Full-timer, I want the existing kind filters to keep working over the new grouping, so that filtering to Small Group still narrows the page.
29. As a Full-timer, I want a Rhythm with a long term to keep its strip usable, so that a year-long Rhythm does not break the row.
30. As a Full-timer, I want the page to keep working for Gatherings created before this change, so that history does not need a migration to stay readable.

## Implementation Decisions

**Grouping is a view concern for this change.** Rhythm identity is already derivable — `parentEventId`, falling back to the Gathering's own id when it is the first of the series. No schema change is required to fold a Rhythm into one row, and none should be made for it here.

**One new pure module is the seam.** A module that owns the whole reshaping: given the Gatherings, the Contacts and the current instant, it returns the view model the page renders — this week's Gatherings grouped by date, the Rhythms in day-of-week order each with their chips and selection, and the one-offs. The view becomes a renderer of that model and holds no grouping, week-bounding or chip-state logic of its own.

**Chip state is a four-way enum**, computed in that module: attendance taken; happened but not taken; falls in the current week; still ahead. Deriving "taken" from an empty present list is explicitly rejected — it permanently mislabels a Gathering nobody attended.

**New fields on the Gathering record**: when attendance is first recorded for a Gathering, stamp who did it and when. This is the only schema change in scope. Absent on every existing record, which reads correctly as "not taken" for past Gatherings and needs no backfill.

**Week bounds are Monday–Sunday**, in the viewer's local zone. Gathering dates are date-only strings and must keep being parsed as local midnight, not UTC — the existing helper in the view does this deliberately and the new module must not regress it.

**Two Rhythms falling on the same date group under one date heading** in the week band, each keeping its own row, roster and attendance beneath it.

**Ordering is stable**: Rhythms sort by day of week, then by name. Not by recency, not by how far behind they are — the page is visited weekly and position is what makes it scannable.

**Roster ownership moves to the Rhythm** with a per-Gathering override applied only where someone actually edited that week. This retires the confirm prompt that currently asks whether a roster edit applies to the series. This is the one part of the change that needs a real Rhythm record to hang from, and it is deliberately staged after the view work — see Out of Scope.

**"Who we've missed lately" keeps its current layout structure**, with the heading promoted to span the grid, the aside prevented from stretching, and the aside made sticky. The figures gain hairline separators. No change to the copy, the fill, the radius or the border.

**One figures treatment, not two.** The page currently renders the same three numbers as a sidebar card when people have been missed and as a horizontal bar when nobody has. Whichever survives, it should be one component used in both branches.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts what a Full-timer would notice: that this week's Gathering is named at the top, that a Rhythm appears once, that a chip for an unmarked past week is distinguishable from one still ahead. It does not assert class names, element order within a row, or that a particular helper was called.

**The new module carries the logic tests.** Because it takes data and an instant and returns a plain view model, every interesting case is a pure assertion with no rendering: a week containing two Gatherings on one date; a week containing none; a Rhythm whose first Gathering has been deleted; a Gathering with attendance taken and nobody present, versus one never opened; a Gathering dated in a week boundary hour; ordering across three Rhythms on two weekdays; one-offs excluded from Rhythm grouping. Prior art: `attendanceRoster.test.ts`, which tests the sibling pure module in exactly this shape.

**The view test asserts wiring only** — that the band names this week's Gatherings, that a Rhythm renders one row, that selecting a chip changes the summary shown. Prior art: `Attendance.test.tsx`, which already mocks the Firestore listeners and renders the page.

**The alignment fix gets no test.** It is pure styling with no assertable behaviour, and per the project's testing policy a snapshot written to satisfy the policy is worse than no test.

**Both existing seams must stay green**: `attendanceRoster.test.ts` and `Attendance.test.tsx`. The roster helpers are not being changed by this work.

## Out of Scope

- **Mobile.** `AttendanceMobile` is a separate view with the same flat-list problem. Deliberately excluded; it needs its own design, because a term-long chip strip does not survive a 390px screen by shrinking.
- **Rhythm as a stored record.** Making a Rhythm a real document — with the roster, cadence and location on it — is the structural follow-on, and the thing that makes story 23–26 real. It needs a migration and touches everything that reads Gatherings. File separately.
- **Rule-based recurrence.** Storing a cadence and materialising a Gathering only when attendance is taken was considered and rejected: creating them up front works today, and exceptions for cancelled or moved weeks are where that approach gets expensive.
- **A calendar view.** Replacing the list with a week or month grid was considered and rejected: with three Rhythms on two weekdays it is mostly empty cells.
- **A debt queue.** Ordering the page by "what still needs marking" was designed and then dropped in favour of ordering by Gathering — at a glance beat triage.
- **Orphaned Gatherings.** Deleting the first Gathering of a Rhythm currently orphans the rest, because series identity hangs off a real record. Real, out of scope, worth its own issue.
- **The stale `Weekly` gathering-type blurb**, which reads "Friday night, the whole fellowship" and matches no Rhythm the team runs.

## Further Notes

Vocabulary for this work is now in `CONTEXT.md`: **Gathering** (one occasion attendance is taken for), **Rhythm** (a Gathering that repeats), **Attendance taken** (the fact someone recorded it). The code's `Event` type and its `sessions` variables are the same concept under older names; renaming them is not required here, but new code should use the glossary terms.

Note the collision that is *not* a collision: a Bible Study is both a **Study** (the materials arc, its weeks being **Meetings**) and a **Rhythm** (the schedule its Gatherings hang off). These are separate objects on separate pages — College Meeting is a Rhythm with no Study, and a Meeting is explicitly not an attendance record. Do not merge them.

ADR 0005 governs roster semantics and still holds, with one amendment implied by this spec: it states that recurring instances "inherit the series roster" and that admins are prompted per edit. Moving the roster onto the Rhythm is the clean form of that intent and should update 0005 when it lands, not before.

title: Spec: The public Bible study — Meetings reachable by QR
label: CLOSED
body:
# Spec: The public Bible study — Meetings reachable by QR

Design: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ba2465c0-a117-42d7-88e4-6b94b876ff07
Design record and rationale: `docs/design/bible-study/` (PR #773)
Glossary: **Study**, **Meeting**, **Section**, **Passage**, **Prompt**, **Blank** are defined in `CONTEXT.md` and are used with those meanings throughout.

## Problem Statement

The Bible study lives on a Google Site. It works, and nobody is confused by it, but it is inert. Every week looks like every other week, the outline and the reading and the questions sit in one undifferentiated scroll, and nothing on the page helps a room actually work through the material together. A Full-timer who wants this week to land differently has no way to shape what a reader sees.

Getting people to the material is its own friction. Today the wider material means asking a student to install a third-party app (Subsplash) — a download, an account, and a decision, at exactly the moment someone is deciding whether this is for them.

Students in this context are almost always on a phone, in a browser they did not choose to open, in a room, next to people they may have just met. The current answer serves none of that.

## Solution

Each week of a Study is published as a **Meeting** at its own public URL, reachable by scanning a QR code displayed on a screen at the gathering. No download, no account, no app.

A Meeting is read one **Section** at a time: some outline points, a **Passage** shown in full, and a **Prompt** for the room. The reader taps to move on. A **Blank** — a hidden word in the outline or the Passage — is tapped to reveal, so reading does not stay passive. An auto-hidden index at the screen edge lets someone who arrives late jump straight to where the room is.

The page never asks for anything. It collects no answers, requires no identity, and writes nothing. Prompts are worked through out loud, by the people in the room.

Full-timers author Meetings on desktop, inside the app, and publish a week when it is ready. The QR for that Meeting is generated beside the document that produced it.

## User Stories

1. As a student, I want to scan a QR code shown at the gathering and land directly on this week's Meeting, so that I can follow along without downloading anything.
2. As a student, I want the page to work in whatever browser my phone opens — Safari, Chrome, Firefox — so that scanning just works.
3. As a student, I want to reach the material without making an account, so that nothing stands between me and the reading on my first night.
4. As a student, I want to read one Section at a time, so that I am looking at the same thing the room is talking about rather than scanning a wall of text.
5. As a student, I want to tap to move to the next Section, so that moving through the study takes no thought.
6. As a student, I want to step back to the Section before, so that a moment of distraction does not lose my place.
7. As a student, I want a Section longer than my screen to scroll, so that a long Passage is never cut off or shrunk to fit.
8. As a student, I want a scrolled Section to reset when I move on, so that the next Section starts at its own beginning.
9. As a student, I want to tap a Blank to reveal the hidden word, so that I am made to think before I am told.
10. As a student, I want a Blank I revealed to stay revealed while I move around the Meeting, so that I am not re-hiding my own progress.
11. As a student, I want revealing a Blank never to reveal a similar one elsewhere, so that each Section stays its own exercise.
12. As a student arriving late, I want an index of the Sections I can open from the edge of the screen, so that I can jump to where the room already is.
13. As a student, I want each index entry to show its Passage reference, so that "we're at Romans 5:3" is enough to find my place.
14. As a student, I want the index hidden until I reach for it, so that it never competes with the reading.
15. As a student, I want the page to follow my phone's light or dark setting, so that it is readable in the room I am actually sitting in.
16. As a student, I want a distraction-free mode, so that the reading can take the whole screen when I want it to.
17. As a student who has asked my phone to reduce motion, I want the transitions to become plain cuts, so that the page does not make me unwell.
18. As a student, I want the Passage printed in full, so that I am not asked to look it up somewhere else mid-discussion.
19. As a student, I want to see what kind of Prompt is in front of me — a Question, a Discuss, an Activity — so that I know whether to think, talk, or do.
20. As a student, I want never to be asked to type an answer, so that I stay in the conversation rather than on my phone.
21. As a student scanning an old code, I want to see the date of what I am reading, so that I am not confused about which week this is.
22. As a student who wants the study permanently, I want to add the page to my home screen, so that it opens with no browser chrome at all.
23. As a signed-in student, I want to read the same Meeting inside the app, so that I do not need the QR code once I am a regular.
24. As a Trainee, I want to read the Meeting in the app without being able to edit it, so that I can prepare without risk of changing it.
25. As a Full-timer, I want to write a Meeting on desktop inside the app, so that authoring does not mean a separate tool.
26. As a Full-timer, I want to decide entirely where a Section begins and ends, so that the pacing of the night is mine and not the software's.
27. As a Full-timer, I want to insert a Passage with a button, so that I never have to remember a markup convention.
28. As a Full-timer, I want to mark a Prompt as a Question, a Discuss, or an Activity with a button, so that the kind is explicit and consistent.
29. As a Full-timer, I want to mark a word as a Blank with a button, so that adding one costs a click.
30. As a Full-timer, I want to decide per Meeting whether it uses Blanks at all, so that the device stays a choice rather than an obligation.
31. As a Full-timer, I want a live preview that shows where the reader's screen edge falls, so that when I own the Section breaks I can see the break I own.
32. As a Full-timer, I want the Section list beside the editor to match the reader's index, so that I know what a latecomer will see.
33. As a Full-timer, I want a Meeting to stay a draft until I publish it, so that half-written material is never public.
34. As a Full-timer, I want to publish a week deliberately, so that publishing is an act rather than an autosave.
35. As a Full-timer, I want the QR code for a Meeting generated beside the document that produced it, so that getting the code onto a screen is not a separate errand.
36. As a Full-timer, I want to split a week into two Meetings when the room divides, so that each group reads its own material.
37. As a Full-timer splitting a week, I want the opening and the closing authored once, so that the shared parts of the night cannot drift apart.
38. As a Full-timer, I want each group's Meeting to show only its own Passage, so that neither half is reading ahead into the other's material.
39. As a Full-timer, I want a stable link to a Study that always resolves to the newest Meeting, so that I have something to send that is not a photograph of a QR code.
40. As a Full-timer, I want to be certain that opening this to the public cannot expose anything pastoral, so that the team's coordination notes stay the team's.
41. As a Full-timer, I want the public pages kept out of search engines, so that the study is reachable by QR without being indexed.

## Implementation Decisions

### Storage: a new collection, deliberately not the Board's

Meetings live in their own Firestore collection with their own security rules. They are **not** stored as Board documents, and the Board's audience ladder is not extended.

The reason is security, not tidiness. That ladder currently bottoms out at "anyone in CISA" and denies everyone unauthenticated, and it is the same ladder that guards the team's pastoral coordination notes. Adding an internet-visible rung to it would make every future edit of that ladder a security review, with a failure mode ("team notes went public") that would be discovered by a student rather than by a test.

What *is* reused is the machinery: the collaborative rich-text editor that already backs Board authoring, and the existing read-only markdown renderer, which already renders a stored document with no editor dependencies attached.

### Access rules

- A published Meeting is readable by anyone, signed in or not.
- A draft Meeting is readable only by staff roles.
- **Nothing anonymous may write anything, anywhere.** The public surface is read-only, full stop.
- Publishing and editing are restricted to Full-timers, matching Board authoring.
- The site-wide crawler exclusion stays as it is; QR links work without being indexed.

### Content model: markdown plus exactly two conventions

Meeting content is stored as markdown. Structure is derived at publish time:

- A heading starts a **Section**. The heading text is also the Section's label in the reader's index — this is why no separate index-label field exists.
- A blockquote is the **Passage**.
- A marked line is the **Prompt**, carrying its kind (Question / Discuss / Activity).
- A wrapped word is a **Blank**.

Parsing is **lenient**: every part of a Section is optional, and their order is whatever the author wrote. A Section with no Passage, or two, or a Prompt before the Passage, all render. There is no validation error, no auto-split, no type-shrinking, and no warning. This follows the governing principle settled in design: **the author decides, the page obeys.**

If the convention set ever needs to grow beyond these, that is the signal to move to a structured block editor instead — not to add a third marker.

The author never types a marker. The editor inserts all of them with toolbar buttons, which is what makes a convention-based format survivable for a weekly author.

### The seam: one module in the shared core package

All logic that is worth testing lives in a single Bible-study module in the shared core package, behind three pure entry points:

- **`parseMeeting`** — stored markdown to a Meeting structure.
- **`currentMeeting`** — given a Study's Meetings and today's date, which Meeting a bare Study URL resolves to, and whether a dated permalink is stale.
- **`readerReducer`** — the reader's entire interaction state machine.

Everything outside this module is intended to be thin: the route resolves and renders, the reader component dispatches actions and paints state, the editor writes markdown. The reducer is in core specifically so that the reader's behaviour is testable without rendering, and so that leader-paced follow mode — parked, but expected — arrives later as one more action on an existing machine rather than as a rewrite.

The following shapes come from the working prototype and encode decisions more precisely than prose:

```ts
type PromptKind = "question" | "discuss" | "activity";

type Blank = { before: string; word: string; after: string };
type Text  = { before: string };                  // no Blank in this part

type Section = {
  id: string;                                      // stable; follow mode will address these
  title: string;                                   // also the index label
  ref?: string;                                    // Passage reference, shown in the index
  points: (Blank | Text)[];
  passage?: Blank | Text;
  prompt?: { kind: PromptKind; text: string };
};

type Meeting = {
  id: string;
  studyId: string;
  date: string;                                    // yyyy-MM-dd
  title: string;
  sections: Section[];
  published: boolean;
  siblingId?: string;                              // set on both halves of a split week
};
```

```ts
type ReaderAction =
  | { type: "advance" }                            // clamps at the last Section
  | { type: "back" }                               // clamps at the first
  | { type: "jump"; index: number }                // from the edge index; closes it
  | { type: "revealBlank"; key: string }           // key is `${sectionIndex}:${slot}`
  | { type: "openIndex" } | { type: "closeIndex" }
  | { type: "toggleUnadorned" };                   // distraction-free mode
```

The Blank key is deliberately scoped by Section and slot: revealing a Blank must never reveal a similar Blank in another Section. Revealed Blanks persist for the reading session and are never written anywhere.

### Routing

- A bare Study URL resolves to the newest published Meeting.
- A dated URL is a permalink to one Meeting.
- Both are public and must **not** sit behind the app's authenticated route guard. The app already has non-guarded routes, so this is an existing pattern rather than a new hole.
- A dated permalink that is not the newest shows the Meeting **with its date** and does not redirect. A permalink that silently shows something other than what was linked is worse than a visible date; a redirect breaks anyone deliberately revisiting.

### Split weeks

A split week is **two Meetings**, each with its own URL and its own QR code, cross-linked by sibling id. The shared opening and closing are authored once and carried into both at publish, so they cannot drift. Neither Meeting shows the other's Passage.

### Reader surfaces

- Public web, phone-first. **There is no desktop reader** — the QR audience is on a phone by definition, and nobody scans a poster with a laptop.
- The same Meeting is readable inside the native app and the installed PWA for signed-in users, in the app's own shell.
- The in-app shell costs roughly 114px of vertical room, so a Section tuned to sit perfectly on the public page will not sit perfectly in the app. Nothing is cut — it scrolls — but this is a known and accepted difference, not a bug to chase.

### Theme and motion

- Both palettes come from the app's existing light and dark design tokens. No new palette.
- The reader follows the device setting by default.
- Section transitions are a staggered rise; two background grounds drift at differing rates behind the Sections.
- All motion collapses to plain cuts under a reduced-motion preference.

### Fullscreen

The expand control is a **CSS distraction-free mode**, not the Fullscreen API.

iPhone Safari does not expose the Fullscreen API for ordinary elements — only video can go fullscreen there. Android Chrome does. Since students scan into Safari on a phone, calling `requestFullscreen` would silently do nothing for a large share of them. The app already ships this exact CSS pattern for the messages view, so this follows precedent rather than inventing one.

True fullscreen on iOS has one reliable route: Add to Home Screen. The web manifest already declares standalone display, so an installed copy runs with no browser chrome. This should be offered as an invitation to a returning reader and **never as a wall** — it is the one place the no-download promise softens.

*The implementer should confirm the iOS behaviour against the current target iOS version before building on it.*

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts **external behaviour**: given this stored markdown, these Sections; given these Meetings and this date, this resolution; given this state and this action, this next state. Tests should not assert on internal helper names, intermediate parse structures, class names, animation timings, or markup shape. No snapshot tests of the reader — markup will churn and the snapshots would only ever be re-blessed.

### The seam carries almost all of it

Because the reducer and the parser both live in the shared core module, nearly every behaviour above is testable without rendering anything.

**`parseMeeting`** — table-driven fixtures over stored markdown:
- A Section with all three parts, in the ordinary order.
- Lenient cases: no Passage; two Passages; a Prompt before the Passage; a Section with only a heading. All must parse, none may throw.
- Order is preserved exactly as authored.
- Each Prompt kind is recognised, and an unmarked line is not a Prompt.
- Blanks in outline points and Blanks inside a Passage.
- A Meeting with no Blanks at all.
- Section ids are stable across re-parses of unchanged content.
- The heading becomes both the title and the index label.

**`currentMeeting`**:
- Newest published Meeting wins for a bare Study URL.
- A draft is never resolved to, even when it is newest.
- A dated permalink to the newest Meeting is not stale; to an older one, it is.
- A Study with no published Meetings resolves to nothing, and the caller renders an empty state rather than crashing.

**`readerReducer`**:
- Advance clamps at the last Section; back clamps at the first.
- Jump moves and closes the index in one action.
- Revealing a Blank toggles only its own key.
- Blanks with the same word in different Sections do not co-reveal — this is the regression test for the keying decision.
- Distraction-free toggles without disturbing position or revealed Blanks.

Prior art for pure-logic tests in the shared core package: the Board and markdown-helper suites already there.

### Rules tests are not optional here

This feature opens a URL to the public, so the rules suite gets cases of its own. The existing rules test file already builds unauthenticated contexts, so this is an extension of an existing pattern:

- Unauthenticated read of a **published** Meeting succeeds.
- Unauthenticated read of a **draft** Meeting is denied.
- Unauthenticated write of any kind, to any path in the collection, is denied.
- A non-Full-timer cannot publish.
- **Unauthenticated read of Board documents is still denied** — a standing guard proving this feature did not widen that ladder.

### Thin coverage above the seam

A light component test only, asserting things the seam cannot:
- The public route renders without an authenticated user.
- A stale permalink shows its date.
- Tapping a Blank reveals its word.

End-to-end coverage follows the existing specs' shape: scan-equivalent navigation to a published Meeting as an anonymous visitor, and a Full-timer authoring and publishing a week.

## Out of Scope

- **Leader-paced follow mode.** Considered and deliberately parked: it assumes a presenter, and there isn't one. Section ids are stable so it can be added later as a `currentSection` field and one reducer action.
- **Answer capture of any kind.** Prompts are for the room, out loud. No typing, no submission, no per-student record. This is a product decision, not a limitation.
- **A desktop reader.** Desktop is the authoring surface only.
- **Second-pass reading features**, all parked knowingly: Spanish toggle, tap-to-expand cross-references, read-aloud.
- **Attendance, RSVP, or prayer-request integration** from the Meeting page.
- **Analytics** on who opened a link or how far they got.
- **Offline caching.** The service worker is push-only today; making Meetings readable offline is real work, not a flag.
- **Authoring conveniences**: duplicate-last-week, term templates.
- **Migrating existing Google Site content.** Needed eventually, but it is a content project with its own shape, not part of building this.

## Further Notes

- The design canvas is live and the student's reader on it is interactive — tap to advance, tap a Blank, tap the edge grip. Worth opening before writing code; several decisions above are much faster to understand by using it than by reading them.
- Every obvious name in this domain was already taken by something else in the product. "Bible study" is a sign-up interest, "Questions" is the team destination for trainee questions, "Session" is a Board concept, and "Group" means three different things already. The glossary entries in `CONTEXT.md` name the collision each term avoids; please use them rather than reaching for the natural-sounding word.
- The two hardest constraints in this spec are both about restraint, and both were reached deliberately after being argued: the page never writes anything, and the page never second-guesses the author. Where an implementation choice is ambiguous, those two are the tiebreakers.

title: Mobile pass follow-ups: touch targets, action ordering, loading fallback, off-palette pages
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

A Trainee or Full-timer working from a phone hits a set of small, avoidable
frictions that the fix for #748 deliberately did not touch.

Buttons are too small to hit reliably. On People, the pill actions in the
header stand 36px tall and the bulk-select actions around 32px — both below
the 44px floor this app already honours in Settings. On a moving bus, one-handed,
that is the difference between tapping "Add someone" and tapping the page.

The primary action is buried. #748 fixed the header overflow by letting the row
wrap, which is correct but has a side effect: on a phone, **Add someone** — the
thing a Trainee opens People to do — now sits on a second row *beneath* Combine
tags and Smart Import, two actions a Trainee rarely wants and a Full-timer uses
occasionally.

Pages briefly look wrong while they load. My Day, Gatherings, Prayer, The Journey,
Visits and Coordination Notes each swap to a purpose-built mobile layout only
once their data has arrived. Until then a phone renders the desktop layout at
390px. On Visits and History, an *error* does the same thing permanently: the
shared error card renders wrapped in the full desktop page chrome instead of on
its own.

Support and Privacy do not look like the app. Both are hardcoded slate and cyan
rather than the Ink tokens, so they ignore the light/dark toggle entirely. They
are also the first two pages an app-store reviewer opens.

The native app still has purple in it. `apps/mobile` carries an Android
adaptive-icon background of `#5c5595` and a splash of `#eaeef4` from the palette
the app retired — the same leftover class as the manifest `theme_color` that #748
just cleared.

## Solution

Every control a phone user can reach is comfortably tappable; the action a
Trainee came to the page for is the first one they see; a page looks like itself
from first paint through to loaded, including when it fails; and the two public
pages and the native app icon carry the same palette as everything else.

Concretely:

- Interactive controls on mobile-reachable surfaces meet a 44px minimum height.
- On People, the primary action leads on a phone; the secondary actions step back.
- The mobile layout decision stops depending on whether data has arrived.
- Support and Privacy are rebuilt on Ink tokens and follow the theme.
- The Expo adaptive-icon and splash colours match the Ink palette.

And, so this does not silently regress a third time, one end-to-end guard that
walks the mobile-reachable routes at a phone viewport and fails on horizontal
overflow or an undersized control.

## User Stories

1. As a Trainee on a phone, I want every button on People to be at least 44px tall, so that I can tap the one I meant without zooming in.
2. As a Trainee on a phone, I want the bulk-select actions (Stage, Tag, Email, Remove) to be comfortably tappable, so that I do not accidentally hit Remove when reaching for Email.
3. As a Trainee opening People on a phone, I want **Add someone** to be the first action I see, so that the thing I came to do is not below two administrative actions.
4. As a Full-timer on a desktop, I want the People header to keep its current left-to-right order, so that raising the mobile hit targets does not reshuffle a layout that already works.
5. As a Trainee on a phone, I want Combine tags and Smart Import to stay reachable even if they step back visually, so that the mobile layout does not cost me functionality.
6. As a Trainee opening My Day on a phone, I want the mobile layout from the very first paint, so that I do not watch a desktop layout flash past before the page settles.
7. As a Trainee opening Gatherings on a phone, I want the loading skeleton to be the mobile skeleton, so that the page does not visibly change shape as data arrives.
8. As a Trainee opening Prayer on a phone with a slow connection, I want the mobile layout throughout, so that the wait does not look like a broken page.
9. As a Trainee opening The Journey on a phone, I want the mobile stage switcher present while loading, so that the page's structure is stable.
10. As a Full-timer opening Visits on a phone when the data fails to load, I want a clean error card, so that I am not reading an error through desktop page chrome squeezed into 390px.
11. As a Full-timer opening History on a phone when the data fails to load, I want the same clean error card, so that failures look the same everywhere.
12. As a Trainee opening Coordination Notes on a phone, I want the mobile layout while the documents and notes load, so that the editor does not appear to jump.
13. As any user on a phone, I want no page to scroll sideways, so that content never sits off the right of the screen the way People's header did.
14. As a Full-timer, I want a test that fails when a row runs off the right edge on a phone, so that the fix for #748 cannot quietly regress.
15. As a Full-timer, I want that same test to fail when a control drops below 44px, so that the touch-target floor is enforced rather than remembered.
16. As a community member opening the Support page, I want it to look like the rest of the app, so that I do not wonder whether I have landed somewhere else.
17. As a community member reading Support in dark mode, I want the page to be dark, so that it does not flash white at night.
18. As a community member reading the Privacy Policy, I want the same treatment, so that the two public pages are consistent with each other and with the app.
19. As an app-store reviewer, I want the Support and Privacy pages to look finished, so that the submission does not raise an avoidable question.
20. As a Full-timer, I want the Support and Privacy pages to fall under the existing colour-token guard once converted, so that new hardcoded colours cannot creep back into them.
21. As a user installing the native app on Android, I want the adaptive-icon background to match the app's palette, so that the icon does not carry a colour the app abandoned.
22. As a user launching the native app, I want the splash colour to match the app's background, so that the launch does not flash a colour from an old design.
23. As a Full-timer reviewing the change, I want the icon and splash change called out separately, so that I can decide knowingly that this alters what ships to the store.
24. As a developer, I want the mobile-viewport guard to run against the QA Database in the emulator, so that it needs no cloud secrets to run in CI.
25. As a developer, I want the mobile-layout branching covered by the existing view tests, so that I do not need a browser to know the loading path is right.
26. As a developer, I want the guard to name the offending route and element when it fails, so that I can find the row without re-deriving the measurement.

## Implementation Decisions

**Touch targets.** Raise the People header pills and the bulk-select action pills
to a 44px minimum height on all viewports rather than only on mobile. The desktop
rendering changes by a few pixels; a viewport-conditional height would mean two
layouts to reason about for no real gain. Settings already sets this precedent
with an explicit minimum-height on its destructive action.

**Action ordering on People.** Below the `sm` breakpoint, collapse Combine tags
and Smart Import behind an overflow control and leave **Add someone** standing
alone as the primary action; at `sm` and above the current three-across row is
unchanged. This removes the wrap on a phone rather than merely tolerating it.
The overflow control follows the pattern the top navigation already uses for its
"More" menu — same disclosure behaviour, same dismissal, same placement of the
panel — rather than inventing a second menu idiom.

**Mobile layout branching.** The condition that selects the mobile layout
currently reads "is mobile AND not loading AND not errored". Reduce it to "is
mobile". Each affected view then needs its mobile component to render its own
loading state, so the loading and error guards move *inside* the mobile branch
or ahead of it, depending on which the view already has:

- Views that already return the shared error card before the mobile branch keep
  that ordering; only the loading guard moves.
- Visits and History currently render the shared error card deep inside their
  desktop tree. Hoist it to an early return, matching the other views, so a
  phone gets the card on its own.
- Coordination Notes gates on two independent loading flags and has no error
  guard; it gets the same treatment, gating only on viewport.

This is the one change in the spec that alters control flow rather than
presentation, so it is the one that most needs the view-level tests below.

**Support and Privacy.** Rebuild both on the Ink tokens — surface, on-surface,
on-surface-variant, outline-variant, and the accent token for links. Do not
invent new colours; these pages have no content that the existing token set
cannot express. Note that the `--accent` invariant applies: interactive text on
these pages must stay visually distinct from body text and keep its underline
affordance. Once converted, the existing diff-scoped colour guard covers them
going forward at no extra cost.

**Expo palette.** Set the Android adaptive-icon background and the splash
background to the Ink light background. Flag in the pull request that this
changes the shipped icon, so the decision is made deliberately rather than
inherited.

**Out of the app's control flow.** Nothing here changes data shape, Firestore
rules, or any API contract. No schema change, no migration.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts what a person on a phone can see and touch — a page
that does not scroll sideways, a control big enough to hit, the mobile layout
appearing when the viewport is a phone. It does not assert that a particular
Tailwind class is present: the class is the mechanism, not the behaviour, and a
test that checks for `flex-wrap` passes just as happily when the layout is
broken some other way.

**Seam 1 — one new end-to-end spec, `e2e/mobile-viewport.spec.ts`.**
Layout only exists in a real browser; jsdom has no layout engine, so this is the
only seam where overflow and control height are observable at all. One spec file
covers findings 1–3 and locks in the #748 fixes as regressions:

- viewport `390 × 844`, `isMobile`, `hasTouch` — the same configuration
  `e2e/mobile-and-pwa-contact-editing.spec.ts` already uses
- signs in through the existing `signInAs` helper against the emulator, so it
  needs no cloud secrets
- for each mobile-reachable route: assert `scrollWidth === clientWidth` on the
  document element, and assert that no visible `button` or `a` has a bounding
  height below 44px
- failures report the route and the offending element's text, so the row is
  identifiable from CI output alone

Prior art: `e2e/mobile-and-pwa-contact-editing.spec.ts` for the mobile viewport
configuration and the sign-in helper; `e2e/permissions.spec.ts` for walking a
set of routes per role.

**Seam 2 — the existing view tests.** The loading/error branching is ordinary
component behaviour and belongs in the suite that already covers these views.
Extend the existing specs for the six affected views using the
`useMediaQuery` mock helper the repo already ships: with the viewport mocked as
mobile, assert that the mobile component renders while loading, and that an
error renders the shared error card on its own rather than inside the desktop
tree. No new seam, no new helper.

Prior art: the existing per-view specs for the mobile components, and
`DataLoadError`'s own spec for what the error card asserts.

**Not tested.** The Expo icon and splash colours are configuration values with
no runtime behaviour to observe; a test asserting a hex string equals itself is
noise. Reviewed by eye at build time instead.

## Out of Scope

- Everything already merged for #748 — the People header and bulk-bar wrapping,
  the Smart Import tab strip, the `no-scrollbar` rename, and the PWA
  `theme_color` and `theme-color` changes. That work is in its own pull request.
- Any redesign of People beyond the ordering of its header actions.
- Building mobile layouts for views that do not have one today (People, Settings,
  Messages, Questions and the landing views all render their desktop layout on a
  phone by design; only their overflow is in scope, via the guard).
- Raising touch targets app-wide. This spec covers People, where the problem was
  reported. A wider sweep should be its own issue with its own inventory.
- The native app's own layout. Only two colour values in its configuration are
  in scope.
- Anything about the Firestore emulator's Java requirement, which blocked local
  verification during #748 but is a developer-environment concern, not a product one.

## Further Notes

The #748 investigation could not run the app locally — the Firestore emulator
requires a JDK 21 or newer and the machine had 17 — so the overflow numbers in
that pull request came from rendering the affected rows against the project's
real stylesheet at 375px and measuring each element's right edge. The end-to-end
guard proposed here is the durable version of that ad-hoc measurement, and CI
does have a usable JDK.

Two of the findings are judgement calls rather than defects and could reasonably
be dropped:

- The overflow menu on People (decision 2) trades a wrapped row for a hidden
  menu. If wrapping reads fine on a real device, keep the wrap and close that
  part of the issue.
- Changing the Expo adaptive-icon background changes what ships to the store. If
  a release is imminent, defer it.

The 44px figure is not arbitrary: it is the floor Settings already applies, and
it matches both platforms' published guidance.
