title: Announcements: rework sending and reading (spec for #725)
label: CLOSED
body:
*Spec for #725. Drafted from the design canvas at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2104e43c-bd73-4be5-8ca8-70a2d77766b6 (sources in `docs/design/announcements/`), with every claim about current behaviour checked against source.*

---

## Problem Statement

A Full-timer needs to tell everyone on campus one thing — reading week moves the
gathering, the intake form changed, the retreat needs drivers — and be reasonably sure it
landed. A Trainee needs to find out what changed without reading it as though it were a
text from a friend, and needs some way to respond when they have a question.

Neither works today.

Sending one means opening New message, switching to the Announcement tab, and ticking
every recipient out of the full directory one at a time. Nothing remembers who the
audience was, so the same weekly announcement is the same two dozen taps every week, and a
missed tick is silent — that person simply never sees it. Once written, it is posted with
the same one-line composer used for "ok, see you at 7", with nothing on screen saying how
many people are about to be pushed. It then arrives on every recipient's phone titled
**"New message"**, bodied "Naomi Kwan: …", indistinguishable from a direct message and
triaged like one. The only announcement-shaped notification the app sends is the one fired
when the *channel is created*, which is the least important moment in its life. And once
sent, the sender has no idea whether anyone read it.

Receiving one is worse. The channel sits in the conversation list distinguished only by a
bell glyph. Its posts render as chat bubbles clamped to 62% of the pane, tucked beside an
avatar — the visual grammar of one side of a conversation. And where the composer would
be, a Trainee gets a single line of italic grey text reading *"This one's an announcement
— replies go to the team directly."* That sentence describes a route that does not exist:
the same permission flag that hides the composer is also passed to the thread pane, so the
reply box there is closed too. The only way to answer is to leave, remember who posted,
and start a direct chat by hand. Beside that sentence sit four emoji buttons which react
to *the newest message in the channel*, whatever the reader has actually scrolled to — so
reacting to Monday's post silently puts your reaction on today's. Finally, italic grey is
the typography this app reserves for absence: a deleted message, a deleted conversation,
an empty list. The entire recipient-facing half of the feature is set in the styling of
something that isn't there.

## Solution

Separate the broadcast from the chat, at both ends, and make the promise the app already
prints — that a reader can reply — actually true.

**Sending.** The Announcement tab addresses a named audience rather than a list of people,
and re-resolves that audience every time a Full-timer posts, so someone who joined last
week receives this week's announcement without anyone editing the channel. Composing
becomes three deliberate steps — name it and choose who, write it, then review what is
about to happen and to how many people — instead of a one-line composer. The resulting
In-app Notification and push are titled with the channel name and say an announcement was
posted, rather than "New message". And each post carries back how many people have read it
and who has not, so the sender knows whether to chase it in person.

**Receiving.** Announcement channels lift out of the conversation list into their own
section above it, as cards carrying a preview — the shape the mobile member home already
uses. Inside, posts render full-width as posts, with the author, their role, the time, and
a footer of their own carrying reactions, a reply control, an acknowledgement, and the
read count. The header states who the channel goes to. The italic read-only bar is
retired: it becomes a plain line of guidance, because every action it was reaching for now
lives on the post it belongs to.

**Replying opens up threads.** A Trainee can reply to any announcement post, in a thread
hanging off that post, using the thread pane the app already has and currently locks shut.
The channel's main stream stays a broadcast — only Full-timers post at the top level — but
a question about the rota is answerable in place, attached to the thing it is about,
visible to the people it concerns.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer, I want to address an announcement to "everyone in the app" rather than ticking two dozen names, so that opening a channel takes seconds instead of a minute of clicking.
2. As a Full-timer, I want the audience I chose to be remembered on the channel, so that I never have to re-pick it.
3. As a Full-timer, I want people who joined after the channel was created to receive my next post in it, so that new Trainees are not silently excluded from campus-wide news.
4. As a Full-timer, I want to keep the hand-picked recipient list as an option, so that the occasional announcement to a specific handful is still possible.
5. As a Full-timer, I want a proper body field when composing an announcement, so that a three-paragraph update does not have to be typed into a one-line chat composer.
6. As a Full-timer, I want to see how many people an announcement will reach before I send it, so that I am reminded of its weight while I can still change my mind.
7. As a Full-timer, I want to see how many of those recipients will actually get a push, so that I know how many will only see it next time they open the app.
8. As a Full-timer, I want to see what the notification will look like on a recipient's phone, so that I can fix a first line that reads badly when truncated.
9. As a Full-timer, I want to go back from the review step and edit, so that reviewing is not a dead end.
10. As a Full-timer, I want to attach a to-do, gathering, contact or note to an announcement, so that a post about the retreat can carry the retreat.
11. As a Full-timer, I want to pin an announcement, so that standing information stays at the top of the channel rather than scrolling away.
12. As a Full-timer, I want each post to show how many recipients have read it, so that I can tell a post that landed from one that did not.
13. As a Full-timer, I want to open that count and see exactly who has read it and who has not, so that I know which people still need telling in person.
14. As a Full-timer, I want to see how many people have acknowledged a post, so that I can distinguish "saw it" from "will act on it".
15. As a Full-timer, I want the composer inside an announcement channel to remind me that I am posting to everyone, so that I do not type a casual aside into a broadcast at 11pm.
16. As a Full-timer, I want replies to appear in a thread on the post they answer, so that I can see what a question is about without asking.
17. As a Full-timer, I want to be notified when someone replies to my announcement, so that a Trainee's question does not sit unanswered.
18. As a Full-timer, I want to reply inside a thread myself, so that the answer is visible to everyone with the same question.
19. As a Full-timer, I want an announcement's In-app Notification to be titled with the channel name, so that it is distinguishable in the bell from ordinary chat.
20. As a Trainee, I want announcement channels grouped separately from my conversations, so that I can tell news from a chat at a glance.
21. As a Trainee, I want to see a preview of the latest announcement in that list, so that I can judge whether to open it now.
22. As a Trainee, I want an announcement I have not read to be visibly marked, so that I can find what is new without opening everything.
23. As a Trainee, I want that unread mark to clear once I have read it, so that the marker stays meaningful.
24. As a Trainee, I want announcements to render as full-width posts rather than chat bubbles, so that a long update is comfortable to read.
25. As a Trainee, I want to see who posted an announcement and that they are a Full-timer, so that I know it is official.
26. As a Trainee, I want the channel header to tell me who else receives this, so that I understand whether it is campus-wide or for a few of us.
27. As a Trainee, I want to react to a specific post, so that my reaction lands on the thing I actually read.
28. As a Trainee, I want to see reactions in each post's own footer, so that I can tell which post people responded to.
29. As a Trainee, I want to acknowledge an announcement, so that the person who sent it knows I have taken it on and does not need to chase me.
30. As a Trainee, I want my acknowledgement shown back to me, so that on returning to the channel I can tell what I have already dealt with from what I have merely scrolled past.
31. As a Trainee, I want to undo an acknowledgement, so that a mis-tap is recoverable.
32. As a Trainee, I want to reply to an announcement post, so that I can ask a question without leaving and hunting for the person who wrote it.
33. As a Trainee, I want my reply to hang off the post it answers, so that whoever reads it knows what I am asking about.
34. As a Trainee, I want to see how many replies a post already has, so that I can check whether my question has been asked.
35. As a Trainee, I want to read other people's replies, so that I do not ask something already answered.
36. As a Trainee, I want the footer to say plainly that only Full-timers post at the top level but anyone can reply, so that I understand what I am allowed to do.
37. As a Trainee, I want to be notified when someone replies in a thread I am part of, so that I see the answer to my question.
38. As a Trainee, I want to see a pinned announcement marked as pinned rather than merely outlined, so that pinned and unread are not confused.
39. As a Trainee, I want the message announcing that a channel was opened to look like a system note rather than a post, so that the channel does not appear to start with an empty announcement.
40. As a Trainee, I want announcement notifications titled with the channel, so that I can tell campus news from a message in my notification bell.
41. As a Trainee, I want my read of a post recorded without my having to do anything, so that acknowledging stays a deliberate act and is not confused with merely looking.
42. As a Trainee on a phone, I want the same read view, per-post footer and thread replies at 390px, so that the feature works where most reading happens.
43. As a Trainee on a phone, I want the footer's controls to be comfortably tappable, so that acknowledging or replying does not require precision.
44. As a Trainee, I want the announcements filter pill in the conversation list to keep working, so that an existing habit is not broken.
45. As a Trainee who is not a Full-timer, I want the top-level composer to stay hidden, so that I never attempt a post that the permission layer will silently refuse.
46. As any user, I want announcement copy available in Spanish, so that the feature matches the rest of the app.
47. As any user, I want the announcement view to be legible in both light and dark themes, so that the unread and pinned marks are visible whichever I use.

## Implementation Decisions

**Where the seams are.** Every seam this needs already exists. No new module boundaries
are introduced. The chat service keeps its current surface; the Messages view keeps its
current shape; the create-chat modal keeps its two tabs; the thread pane keeps its props
and simply stops being locked shut.

**Replies are threads, and the rules change to allow exactly that.** The message create
rule currently requires a Full-timer for any message in an announcement room. It is
widened so a room member who is not a Full-timer may create a message **only when it is a
reply** — it carries a parent, that parent exists in the same room, and that parent is
itself a top-level post. Requiring the parent to exist costs one document read on the
reply path only, never on the read path, and it is what stops a member writing arbitrary
orphan documents into a channel they cannot otherwise post to. Requiring the parent to be
top-level stops threads nesting. Creating a message with no parent stays Full-timer-only,
so the broadcast stream is unchanged.

Two alternatives were considered and rejected: routing replies to a direct chat with the
poster, which the existing service call would have made nearly free but which scatters a
member's replies when several Full-timers post to one channel; and routing them to a group
of the channel's Full-timers, which is closest to the wording of today's copy but makes a
member's question visible to all staff — a different privacy promise than they have now.

**The thread pane opens for members in announcement rooms.** It is currently handed the
same permission flag that hides the top-level composer, which is why the reply box is shut.
That flag is separated: one value governs posting at the top level, another governs
replying. The main composer stays hidden for non-Full-timers; the thread reply box does
not.

**Acknowledgement and read receipts ride the existing message-update rule.** The messages
update rule already permits any room member to change *only* the reaction and pin fields on
a live message, and the announcement restriction is applied at create, not update — so
recipients can already write to a post today. Acknowledgement and the read set are two more
field-level acts of the same kind, added by widening that rule's allowed key set. No new
collection, no per-member document, no extra document read to display them, and no change
to how membership is evaluated.

Unlike the existing reaction rule, which permits a member to write the whole reaction array
without policing whose reaction it is, the acknowledgement and read fields **are** checked
for ownership: a member may only add or remove their own entry, because these fields are a
claim about a named person rather than a shared tally. The existing permissiveness on
reactions is pre-existing and out of scope to change here.

**Read receipts are stored on the post, not in a subcollection.** Displaying "read by 9 of
24" on every post in view has to be cheap, and a subcollection would mean a query per post.
The read set therefore lives on the message document alongside the reactions, so the count
arrives with the post itself at no extra read. The cost is write contention: every recipient
writes to the same document when they open the channel. This is mitigated by marking a post
read once, when it comes into view, debounced, with the write fired without blocking and its
failure swallowed — a lost read receipt is not worth an error in front of a reader. **This
design is sized for channels of tens of people, not hundreds**; if an announcement channel
ever needs to serve hundreds, the read set moves to a subcollection with a counter, and that
should be revisited rather than discovered.

**Reading is passive; acknowledging is deliberate.** They are separate fields and separate
affordances. A post being read means it appeared on screen. A post being acknowledged means
the reader pressed a control saying so. The footer shows both, and never conflates them.

**Every action lives on the post; the bottom bar stops being an action bar.** Reactions,
reply, acknowledgement and the read count all belong to a specific post, so they sit in that
post's own footer — which is also the fix for the current bug where the channel-level
reaction buttons fire at the newest message rather than the one being read. What remains at
the bottom of the pane is one line of guidance stating that only Full-timers post here and
that anyone may reply. The italic grey read-only bar is retired rather than restyled.

**The per-device "new to you" marker reuses the unified per-user entity state store.** That
store already models a read axis keyed by entity reference and already has a message
namespace. The unread mark on an announcement post is that, and needs no Firestore data at
all. It is per-device by design, consistent with how the app already treats "scanned", and
it is deliberately distinct from the shared read set, which is what the *sender* sees.

**Audience presets resolve to concrete membership, and re-resolve on every post.** The
security rules gate announcement reads on the room's member list, so an audience cannot be
stored purely as a rule without a rules redesign. Instead the chosen preset is stored on the
channel *and* the membership is reconciled in the send path: before a post goes out, the
preset is re-resolved and anyone newly matching is added to the channel's members. This
delivers story 3 with no further rules change. The design canvas overstates this as "stored
as the rule, not the membership" — the spec is the correction.

**Only the roster-free presets ship.** "Everyone in the app" is every approved user, which
the create-chat modal already queries, and "Pick people" is today's picker. The per-team
presets drawn on the canvas depend on a `team` field on the user document that
[#727](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-tracker/issues/727) proposes and which
does **not exist** — the app user record carries uid, email, display name, photo, approved
and role, and nothing else. Team presets are deferred to #727, and the preset list must be
written so that adding them later is additive.

**The notification branch needs the room type at the call site, not a fetch.** The send path
is already given the member list by its caller, so the room document is not re-fetched on
the hot path; adding a fetch to learn the type would be a new read on every message in the
app. The room type is passed in instead — the caller already holds it. Both the In-app
Notification and the push take the branch, since they share the call. A reply in an
announcement thread notifies the post's author and the other participants in that thread,
not the whole channel.

**Announcement posts get their own presentation, and the chat bubble is left alone.** The
bubble component continues to serve direct and group rooms unchanged. The post is a sibling
presentation selected on room type, at full pane width, carrying author, role, time, body,
optional attachment, and its footer. Emphasis is carried on the border rather than a fill,
because the card already sits on a raised surface against a page-white pane. The
announcement accent is the token the bell glyph already uses; it clears contrast in both
themes (4.2:1 on the card in light, 7.7:1 in dark), unlike the news feed's unread border,
which does not render.

**Copy changes go through the locale files.** The i18n check fails on hardcoded UI strings,
and the misleading sentence being removed is user-facing in both languages.

## Testing Decisions

**What makes a good test here.** Assert what a Full-timer or a Trainee can observe: which
controls are present for which role, what text is on screen, what the service was called
with, and what the rules allow or deny. Do not assert class names, internal state, or the
shape of a render tree. The existing announcement tests are the model — they assert that the
composer is present for one role and replaced for another, not how that branch is
implemented. Every behaviour below is a bug fix or new logic, so the repo's TDD policy
applies: failing test first.

**Modules under test, all at existing seams:**

- *The Messages view* — the room list's new sections, the post presentation replacing bubbles
  for announcement rooms, the unread and pinned marks, the guidance line replacing the
  read-only bar, and the per-post footer. The reaction-target fix needs an explicit test: a
  reaction fired from a post's footer must land on that post and not on the newest message in
  the channel. Read and acknowledgement counts must render from the post's own data. Prior
  art: the existing announcement describe block, and the filter-pill test that already
  exercises the Announcements pill.
- *The thread pane* — this is where the behaviour inverts, so it needs the most care. A
  Trainee must be able to open a thread on an announcement post and send a reply; the same
  Trainee must still not be able to post at the top level. A Full-timer must be able to do
  both. Prior art: the pane's existing tests, which already drive it with the permission prop
  set both ways.
- *The create-chat modal* — the Announcement tab's preset options, that the tab remains
  Full-timer-only, that the review step reports the right recipient count, that going back
  preserves what was typed, and that a failed create keeps the modal open. Prior art: the
  existing tab-visibility, creation and failure tests, which already mock the chat service and
  assert the arguments it was called with.
- *The chat service* — that an announcement post produces a notification and a push titled
  with the channel rather than "New message"; that an ordinary message is unchanged; that a
  thread reply notifies the post's author and thread participants rather than the whole
  channel; and that membership is reconciled against the stored preset before a post goes out.
  Prior art: the existing create-announcement-room test, which already asserts the exact
  notification title, message and push body.
- *The security rules* — the largest new surface, and the one where a mistake is invisible in
  the UI. A member who is not a Full-timer may create a message in an announcement room when
  it is a reply to an existing top-level post in that room, and may not when it has no parent,
  when the parent does not exist, when the parent is itself a reply, or when the parent is in
  another room. That member may set their own acknowledgement and their own read entry on a
  live post, may not set or remove anyone else's, and may not touch a deleted post. A
  non-member may do none of it. Prior art: the existing chat room and message rules tests, run
  against the emulator.

**Coverage.** Thresholds are enforced and ratchet upward only; they must not be lowered to
accommodate this work.

## Out of Scope

- **Per-team audience presets**, which depend on #727's unbuilt user field.
- **Scheduled or recurring announcements.**
- **Editing a posted announcement.** Messages are immutable apart from the field-level acts
  the rules name, and changing that is a larger decision than this issue.
- **Tightening the existing reaction rule** so a member may only write their own reaction.
  That permissiveness predates this work; the new fields are stricter, but changing the old
  one is a separate concern.
- **Announcements outside the Messages page** — a My Day surface, or a digest email.
- **The native mobile app.** Its member home already presents announcements as cards; this
  spec is the web and PWA. Any change there is its own issue.
- **Reworking direct or group chat presentation.** The bubble stays exactly as it is.
- **Scaling the read set beyond channels of tens of people.** Named as a known ceiling in the
  Implementation Decisions rather than solved here.

## Further Notes

The design canvas is the visual reference and carries measurements, states and the rejected
alternatives with their costs:
https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2104e43c-bd73-4be5-8ca8-70a2d77766b6 — sources in
`docs/design/announcements/`, with a README recording what the drawings assume about the
code.

**The canvas is deliberately out of step with this spec in two places** and the spec wins:
it draws replies as opening a direct chat with the poster, and it draws a channel-level
footer carrying acknowledge, reply and reactions. Both decisions were taken the other way —
replies are threads, and every action moved onto the post. `Footer.dc.html`'s three-option
panel should be read as the record of why, not as the answer. Redrawing is a follow-up.

Two things found while drawing that are true regardless of whether this spec is built:

1. The read-only bar promises a reply route that does not exist. This spec makes it true by
   opening threads, which is the closest of the three routes to what a reader expects when
   they read that sentence next to a post.
2. The quick reactions fire at the newest message in the channel rather than the one being
   read. That is a plain bug and worth fixing even alone.

Nothing has been added to `docs/design/DRIFT.md` for any of this. The register is for drift
that has been settled; now that the reply route is decided, the read-only bar's copy earns a
row once this ships.

Sample names, counts and copy on the canvas are illustrative, not real roster data.

title: Global Search: centred popup instead of an anchored dropdown (#689)
label: CLOSED
body:
Spec for #689. Design canvas: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/30e7d46b-95b1-48f8-95a3-1e34581c5a6b

## Problem Statement

Global Search (⌘K) is the do-everything palette: it jumps to any destination, finds a person, a conversation, a coordination note or a history entry, and runs quick actions, all role-filtered and frecency-ranked. But on desktop it presents itself as an autocomplete hanging off a text field in the corner of the screen, and that framing costs it.

- The panel is anchored under the 300px topbar field and right-aligned to it, so it is stuck at 420px wide in the top-right corner of a screen that is usually 1440px or wider. Conversation snippets and coordination-note titles ellipsise long before the sentence is readable — the exact content a Full-timer is searching *for* is the content that gets cut.
- The results list clips at 440px. A Full-timer searching a common name gets People, Conversations, Coordination Notes and the History toggle, and is scrolling inside a small box almost immediately.
- Because the panel is anchored to whichever shell mounted it, the same ⌘K produces a panel in two different places: in top-bar mode it hangs off the bar, in rail mode off the chrome strip above the content. The palette has no stable home.
- The page behind stays fully lit and click-away is bounded by the field's own container, so the palette never reads as having the floor. It looks like a suggestion list, not the primary way to move around the app.

Reported from `/visits` (#689): "can we have the search show a popup instead of a dropdown?"

## Solution

Lift the desktop palette off the field and centre it over the page as a modal popup on a scrim.

The search field comes with it: the topbar keeps a search-shaped **trigger** that opens the popup, and the actual input moves into the popup's head, so the caret and the results it drives sit together in one place. Freed from the 300px field it was tethered to, the panel widens from 420px to 640px and its results region grows from 440px to 520px — snippets read as sentences, and a full set of grouped results is visible without scrolling.

Nothing inside the panel changes. The rows, tonal icon nodes, group labels, role gating, frecency ranking, quick actions, shortcut listing and footer hint are the palette exactly as it shipped in #653. What changes is the container and where it lives.

On mobile the palette is already a full-screen overlay — a popup by any other name — so nothing below the large breakpoint changes.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer, I want the search results centred on screen, so that my eye is not dragged to the far top-right corner every time I search.
2. As a Full-timer, I want a conversation snippet in the results to be readable as a sentence, so that I can tell two similar conversations apart without opening both.
3. As a Full-timer, I want a coordination-note title to show in full, so that "March outreach — the dorm sweep" and "March outreach — follow-ups" are distinguishable in the list.
4. As a Trainee, I want to see People, Conversations and Coordination Notes results at once, so that I do not scroll a small box to discover a group exists.
5. As a Trainee, I want the palette to appear in the same place regardless of whether I use the rail or the top bar, so that the muscle memory I build transfers between shells.
6. As a Full-timer, I want the page behind the palette dimmed, so that it is obvious the palette has my whole attention and nothing behind it is live.
7. As a Full-timer, I want to click anywhere outside the palette to dismiss it, so that getting out is as cheap as getting in.
8. As a keyboard user, I want Escape to close the palette, so that I never have to reach for the mouse to back out.
9. As a keyboard user, I want the palette to tell me Escape closes it, so that I do not have to guess at the exit.
10. As a keyboard user, I want the caret in the palette the moment it opens, so that I can start typing without a click.
11. As a keyboard user, I want ↑ and ↓ to move through results and ↵ to open the focused one, so that I can search and navigate without leaving the keyboard.
12. As a keyboard user, I want focus returned to the search trigger when the palette closes, so that Tab order picks up where I left it.
13. As a screen-reader user, I want the palette announced as a dialog with a name, so that I know a modal opened rather than a list appearing somewhere.
14. As a screen-reader user, I want the search trigger announced as a button that opens something, so that I am not told there is a text field I cannot type into.
15. As a Full-timer, I want the topbar search to look exactly as it does today, so that the thing I already aim at is still there.
16. As a Full-timer, I want ⌘K to keep opening the palette from anywhere, so that the fastest route in is unchanged.
17. As a Full-timer, I want clicking the topbar search to open the palette, so that the mouse route in is unchanged.
18. As a Full-timer, I want the ⌘K hint to stay on the trigger, so that the shortcut keeps teaching itself to people who reach for the mouse.
19. As a Trainee, I want to clear my query from inside the palette, so that I can start a new search without closing and reopening.
20. As a Trainee, I want the empty palette to still lead with Go to, Recent people and Quick actions, so that ⌘K remains useful before I type anything.
21. As a Student, I want to see only the groups my role can reach, so that the roomier panel does not start showing me things I could not open before.
22. As a Full-timer, I want the "Search history too" toggle to stay where it is in the results, so that opting into history costs the same as it does today.
23. As a Full-timer, I want frecency ranking unchanged, so that the people I open most still come first.
24. As a Full-timer, I want the palette to fit on a small laptop screen, so that a 1280×720 window does not clip the panel or push the footer off-screen.
25. As a Trainee on a narrow window, I want the panel to shrink rather than overflow, so that the palette never causes a horizontal scrollbar.
26. As a Trainee, I want the palette to open with the same quick fade it has today, so that it does not feel slower than the dropdown it replaces.
27. As a Full-timer, I want the page behind the palette not to scroll while it is open, so that dismissing it does not leave me somewhere else on the page.
28. As a Student on a phone, I want the search overlay to behave exactly as it does today, so that a desktop change does not disturb my only way to search.
29. As a Community member, I want the palette to look like the rest of the app, so that it reads as part of the product rather than a bolted-on control.
30. As a developer, I want the palette to keep one implementation across both shells, so that a fix in one place fixes it everywhere.
31. As a developer, I want the change confined to presentation, so that a search regression can be ruled out by reading a small diff.

## Implementation Decisions

**Module.** `GlobalSearch` keeps its shape as a single component with both existing mount points — inside the bar in top-bar mode, inside the shared chrome strip in rail mode. No new component is introduced. What changes is the desktop branch of its render: from a positioned sibling of the trigger to a portalled overlay.

**Portalling.** The desktop popup renders through a portal into the document body, as the mobile overlay already does. Anchoring it inside the shell would place it inside the sticky header's stacking and clipping context, and would reintroduce the shell-dependent positioning this spec exists to remove. Portalling is what makes the palette land in the same place in both shells.

**The trigger.** The topbar field becomes a button, not an input. It keeps the shipped appearance exactly: fixed 300px, 16px radius, surface fill, the always-on inset outline with its hover and focus states, placeholder-styled prompt text, and the ⌘K hint pill. Three things change: it holds no text input, it never displays a query, and its ⌘K pill is now permanent — the pill previously yielded its slot to a clear ×, and the clear × has moved into the popup. It carries an accessible name, a dialog popup hint, and an expanded state reflecting whether the palette is open.

**The field row.** The single desktop text input moves into the popup as a 56px head above the results, separated by a bottom border. It carries the search glyph, the existing "Search or jump to…" placeholder key, the clear × while a query is present, and an `esc` chip while the query is empty. It receives focus on open.

**The overlay.** A fixed, full-viewport layer that centres its panel horizontally and pins it 96px from the top — the same top offset the app's other top-anchored modal uses. The scrim is a separate absolutely-positioned element behind the panel, at 40% black with a small backdrop blur, matching the contact-details modal. Putting the scrim on its own element rather than on the overlay keeps the panel itself unblurred. Clicking the scrim closes the palette.

**The panel.** 640px wide, capped to the viewport less a 2rem gutter so it shrinks rather than overflows on narrow windows. Surface fill, outline-variant border and 24px radius are unchanged from the dropdown. The elevation shadow steps up from `0 8px 16px` to `0 16px 32px` at the same 16% black — the design system's pop shadow — because the panel now floats above a scrim rather than resting under a field. The results region grows from `min(60vh, 440px)` to `min(62vh, 520px)` and keeps its existing custom scrollbar.

**Dismissal and click-away.** The existing click-away listener, which bounded the panel by the trigger's container, is replaced by scrim click. The Escape branch already present in the keydown effect is retained and is now also advertised: by the `esc` chip in the field row, and by " · esc close" appended to the footer hint. The footer's hint is one translatable sentence, so the existing string value is extended in both English and Spanish rather than a second key being introduced. The `esc` chip is a key name rather than prose and stays literal, as the `K` in the ⌘K pill does; if the hardcoded-UI-string check flags it, it gets its own key rather than a suppression.

**Modal semantics.** The panel is a dialog with a modal flag and an accessible name. Focus moves to the popup input on open and returns to the trigger on close. The existing body-scroll lock is retained.

**Motion.** The portalled overlay stays under the existing presence wrapper. The scrim fades opacity only; the panel fades and settles from a slightly smaller scale and a small negative offset. Duration stays at the dropdown's existing 0.12s so the palette does not feel slower than what it replaces.

**Focus targeting.** The desktop input and the mobile input remain separate elements gated by the large breakpoint, so the existing viewport check that decides which one to focus on open is kept as-is.

**Explicitly unchanged.** The Firestore listeners and their error handling; the shortcut registry binding for ⌘K; role gating; destinations, quick actions and the shortcut listing; frecency ranking and its open/close event recording; the group cap; the history opt-in toggle; every row's anatomy, tone and copy; the mobile overlay. No new design tokens, no schema change, no API change.

## Testing Decisions

**What makes a good test here.** Assert what a person using the palette can observe: what is on screen, what they can type into, what they can click, what the keyboard does, and where navigation lands. Do not assert internal state, refs, effect ordering or the portal mechanism. The one justified exception is the small set of structural assertions that already exist for #653 — the shipped design's measurements are a deliberate contract, and those tests are what stop a restyle from silently undoing it; they are rewritten for the new container rather than removed.

**Seam.** One seam, and it already exists: rendering `GlobalSearch` directly in `src/test/GlobalSearch.test.tsx`, with the hoisted mocks already in that file for the Firestore snapshot listeners, the auth provider, the layout context that owns open state, the motion primitives and the router's navigate. No new test file, no new mount point, and no test through the two shells — they mount the same component and the popup is portalled out of both, so a shell-level test would assert nothing the component-level test does not.

**Existing tests.** All current behavioural tests must keep passing with their intent unchanged. Two mechanical adjustments are expected: the query for the "Search or jump to…" placeholder now resolves the popup's input rather than the topbar's, and the handful of tests that reach the trigger by walking parent elements are rewritten to find it by its button role and accessible name. The typing helper needs no change.

**Rewritten structural tests.** The trigger test asserts a button carrying the same 300px width, 16px radius, surface fill and inset-outline states, and a ⌘K pill that is now permanent. The pill-swap test splits in two: the trigger's pill never yields, and the popup's field row shows the clear × only while a query is present and restores the `esc` chip when cleared. The dropdown-elevation test becomes a popup test asserting the scrim, the centred top-anchored placement, the 640px panel, the 24px radius, the outline-variant border and the stepped-up shadow.

**New tests.** That opening renders a dialog with an accessible name; that the popup input holds focus on open; that clicking the scrim closes the palette; that Escape still closes it; that the footer advertises Escape; that the topbar trigger never displays the query typed into the popup; that activating the trigger opens the palette; that the results region carries the 520px cap; that a narrow viewport does not widen the panel past the viewport gutter; and that the mobile overlay's markup and behaviour are untouched.

**Prior art.** `src/test/GlobalSearch.test.tsx` is the closest and richest example — its hoisted-mock setup, role fixtures and structural assertions are the pattern to follow. For modal dismissal and focus behaviour, the add-event and contact-details modal tests. For shell chrome assertions, the top-nav and dashboard-layout shell tests.

**Coverage.** The thresholds in the vitest config are a ratchet: they must not be lowered to accommodate this change, and should rise if the rewritten tests improve the numbers.

## Out of Scope

- The mobile overlay below the large breakpoint. It is already full-screen and is not touched.
- Giving each Go to destination its own navigation icon. Every destination currently shares one glyph, and the 640px panel has the room to fix it — but that is a separate change and would muddy the diff this spec is meant to keep readable.
- The lighter 20% scrim used by the add-event modal. It was weighed against the 40% scrim during design and the heavier one was chosen; revisiting it is a follow-up, not part of this.
- Merging the desktop popup and the mobile overlay into one implementation. Tempting once both are overlays, but it changes mobile, which this spec explicitly does not.
- Frecency scoring, role gating, result types, group caps and the shortcut registry.
- End-to-end coverage. The component seam is sufficient for a presentation change.
- Any change to the Firestore data model, security rules or server routes.

## Further Notes

The design canvas has four artboards: the popup at rest and mid-search over the `/visits` page it was reported from, a before/after against today's dropdown at matched scale, and a build-notes sheet carrying the measurements above. https://claude.ai/code/artifact/30e7d46b-95b1-48f8-95a3-1e34581c5a6b

The 640px width is the substantive decision, not the centring. Centring alone would move the panel; the width is what makes the snippets readable, and it is only available *because* the panel stopped being anchored to a 300px field. If a reviewer wants to argue the change down, the width is the part worth defending.

Names, snippets and counts in the mockups are invented sample data.

Closes #689.

title: The navigation preference
label: CLOSED
body:
## What to build

Rail, Compact or Top bar is chosen in Settings and remembered per user. Adds the provider that owns the stored preference and derives the effective shell from viewport width — modelled on the existing theme provider, which is also the prior art for its tests.

Specified in `docs/specs/navigation-shell-preference.md`. The three states, the Settings control and the width rules are drawn in `docs/design/ink/NavPref.dc.html`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Settings offers all three states, with copy making clear the setting is desktop-only
- [ ] The preference persists across reloads
- [ ] The correct shell renders on first paint — no flash of the wrong navigation and no reflow
- [ ] Below the large breakpoint all three fall through to mobile navigation; the preference is neither consulted nor changed
- [ ] At intermediate widths the rail renders collapsed regardless of preference, and this does **not** write to storage
- [ ] Widening the window again restores the stored preference
- [ ] The preference is one flat enum, so "top bar, collapsed" is unrepresentable
- [ ] The provider is tested at its seam, following the theme provider's test as prior art
- [ ] The forced-collapse-does-not-persist case is covered — the defect most likely to ship, because the UI looks correct while it happens

## Blocked by

- #665

title: The compact rail
label: CLOSED
body:
## What to build

The rail collapses to an icon-only strip and expands again from a control on the rail itself. Same destinations, less width.

The collapsed rail is the look from the original reference. It is not the default, because thirteen unlabelled glyphs is a memory test — it is what the rail collapses *to*, on request.

Specified in `docs/specs/navigation-shell-preference.md`. Both widths are drawn at 1:1 in `docs/design/ink/NavPref.dc.html`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A chevron on the rail collapses and expands it
- [ ] The control moves only between the two rail widths — leaving the rail entirely is a Settings decision, not a one-click action
- [ ] Group labels become hairline dividers; the grouping survives without the words
- [ ] Items are square at the interactive radius, not pills
- [ ] Count badges become a dot — "something here" without the number
- [ ] Labels appear in a tooltip on hover **and on focus**
- [ ] Collapsed destinations keep an accessible name
- [ ] The control is a real button exposing its expanded state
- [ ] The wordmark reduces to the mark; the account block reduces to an avatar with name and role in its menu

## Blocked by

- #664

title: The rail replaces the top bar on desktop
label: CLOSED
body:
## What to build

On desktop, a Full-timer sees all thirteen destinations grouped in a vertical rail and reaches any of them in one click. The More menu is gone from this path.

Includes the shell restructure this implies: Global Search, notifications, the season indicator and the avatar move to a strip above the content; page gutters move from the page container to the shell; impersonation and owner-view banners take their place at the top of the content column; and the destination list scrolls inside the rail with the mark, account block and controls pinned.

**Sequencing risk, flagged deliberately:** this removes the top bar on desktop, and #665 is what brings it back as a preference. Either accept a rail-only interim on `main`, or fold the preference into this ticket. Worth an explicit decision before starting rather than discovering it at release.

Specified in `docs/specs/navigation-shell-preference.md`. Design sources in `docs/design/ink/` (`Shells.dc.html`, `NavPref.dc.html`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The rail shows every destination the signed-in role can reach, grouped
- [ ] The current destination is unmistakable
- [ ] Global Search opens on the same keyboard shortcut as before
- [ ] Impersonation and owner-view banners remain prominent
- [ ] The destination list scrolls within the rail; mark, account block and controls stay pinned
- [ ] Below the large breakpoint, mobile navigation is used unchanged
- [ ] One integration test that the expected destinations render and the current one is marked
- [ ] Existing top-bar tests pass, or are updated where they assumed the top bar was the only shell

## Blocked by

- #662

title: Ink tokens, typography and the theme blocks
label: CLOSED
body:
## What to build

The application wears Ink: a white page with grey cards, borders receded so surfaces separate by fill rather than by line, black as the accent, brighter data hues, and a display face carrying the headings. Both light and dark.

Component markup is not touched. Roughly 4,254 semantic utility usages already read from these tokens, so re-valuing them retints the whole application at once. `--bg` and `--panel` simply exchange roles.

Specified in `docs/specs/ink-design-system.md`. Design sources in `docs/design/ink/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--bg` and `--panel` exchange roles; cards read grey-on-white with no markup change
- [ ] Accent tokens are neutral; violet no longer appears anywhere in the shell
- [ ] `--accent-on` is theme-dependent for the first time — white content in light, near-black in dark
- [ ] Signal colours (success, warning, danger and their containers) carried over from Bento unchanged
- [ ] Data hue chroma and lightness raised; the eight hue angles and the legacy `board-*` names unchanged
- [ ] Shape scale gains an extra-large radius and a pill radius
- [ ] Heading font alias points at a display face with 700/800 weights; the font stylesheet loads both families with metric-compatible fallbacks
- [ ] Dark mode walked end to end, with particular attention to anything placing white content on a primary fill
- [ ] No unit tests added asserting token values — see the spec's testing decisions
- [ ] Change is contained to the stylesheet and the font link, and reverts in a single commit

## Blocked by

- #660

title: Prefactor: destination grouping in permissions
label: CLOSED
body:
## What to build

A grouping function returns the ordered groups of destinations a given role can reach — Today, People, Gatherings, Prayer — alongside the existing per-role navigation helpers.

No user-visible change. This is the data the rail needs, landed on its own so that the rail ticket is about the rail.

Specified in `docs/specs/navigation-shell-preference.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For every role, the returned groups contain exactly the destinations that role can reach
- [ ] No destination appears twice or goes missing across the groups
- [ ] Group ordering and within-group ordering are stable
- [ ] Settings is excluded from the groups — it is pinned separately by the shell
- [ ] Tested at the existing permissions seam
- [ ] Existing navigation helpers and their tests are unchanged

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Colour-token regression guard
label: CLOSED
body:
## What to build

New hardcoded colours fail CI. A guard scans only the lines added in the current diff for raw hex values and raw Tailwind palette classes in component source, so the ~14 existing hardcoded hexes and ~109 raw palette classes are not flagged, but no new ones can land without going through a token.

The existing i18n regression guard is the direct prior art for both the diff-scoping approach and the CI wiring — it already runs as its own CI step.

Specified in `docs/specs/ink-design-system.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scans only lines added in the diff, matching the i18n guard's approach
- [ ] Raw hex values and raw palette classes in component source fail
- [ ] CSS custom property definitions in the stylesheet are not flagged
- [ ] Exposed as an npm script and run as its own CI step
- [ ] Passes on the current tree with no changes to existing files
- [ ] The guard itself has tests

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Prefactor: selection states fill solid instead of tinting
label: CLOSED
body:
## What to build

Selected rows, chips and menu items fill solid with the accent colour and invert their content, instead of tinting at low alpha. This ships in the current Bento palette, where it reads as a deliberate emphasis change.

It is a prefactor for the Ink token swap. At Ink's near-black accent, an `--accent-soft` tint is effectively invisible — and a selection state that renders without error while communicating nothing is the defect most likely to ship unnoticed. Doing this first means the token swap that follows is a pure value change with no landmine in it.

Specified in `docs/specs/ink-design-system.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every selection state that currently tints with `--accent-soft` fills solid with the accent and inverts its content
- [ ] Inverted content meets WCAG AA contrast against the filled background
- [ ] Filter chips, which already fill solid, are unchanged
- [ ] The complete/done state continues to use `--success` — complete must never read as selected
- [ ] Verified in both light and dark themes
- [ ] Existing tests pass without modification

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Restyle Global Search (⌘K) trigger + dropdown to PICKED shell design (Bento border & elevation)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

The ⌘K search in the topbar does not look like the PICKED shell design (Direction B, 18 Aug). It renders as a borderless pill (`border-0 ring-0`, no background border — documented in feedback #354), with a Tailwind `shadow-lg`/`shadow-2xl` when open. The design specifies a Bento SearchBar: radius-16, an always-on inset 1px outline (neutral-40), hover neutral-60, a violet 2px focus ring (#5C17E5), a ⌘K hint pill inside the field's right end, fixed 300px width, and menu surfaces at radius-24 with `0 8px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.16)` elevation. The design files (`Shell - 3 directions.html`, direction B PICKED) show ⌘K as "the real navigation" promoted into the topbar.

## Solution

The topbar search looks like the shipped design: a rounded-16 rectangle with a crisp always-visible outline that darkens on hover and glows violet on focus, a ⌘K hint pill at its right end (replaced by the clear × while typing), fixed 300px width, and the results dropdown floating on the design's elevation shadow with neutral hover rows. Keyboard behavior, role gating, frecency ranking, and all existing commands stay exactly as they are.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer, I want the topbar search to show a visible outline border, so that it reads as a search field rather than a flat pill (feedback #354).
2. As a Full-timer, I want the search field to use a 16px-radius rounded rectangle (not a fully-round pill), so that it matches the PICKED shell design.
3. As a Trainee, I want a ⌘K hint pill inside the empty search field, so that I can discover the keyboard shortcut.
4. As a Trainee, I want the ⌘K pill to disappear and a clear × to appear once I type, so that the two affordances never collide (they share the same slot).
5. As a Full-timer, I want the field's outline to darken on hover, so that it feels interactive.
6. As any user, I want the field to show a 2px violet focus ring when focused, so that I can see where keyboard input goes.
7. As any user, I want outline changes rendered as inset box-shadows, so that the field never shifts layout between states.
8. As any user, I want the search field a fixed 300px wide, so that the topbar matches the design's proportions and "Search or jump to…" fits without cramping at 220px.
9. As any user, I want the results dropdown to float on `0 8px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.16)` elevation over a white surface with radius-24 and neutral hover rows, so that it matches the design's menu look.
10. As a Full-timer, I want ⌘K to keep opening the palette with the empty-state groups (Go to / Recent people / Quick actions / Shortcuts), so that "do everything" navigation is unchanged.
11. As a Trainee, I want role-gated quick actions and destinations to keep filtering by my role, so that I only ever see commands I can use.
12. As any user, I want the mobile full-screen search overlay to be unchanged, so that phone behavior stays intact (the design files are desktop-only).
13. As any user, I want the dark theme to keep working via the app's existing semantic tokens (design `.sh-dark` values: primary #27313F, secondary #1A212B, outline #333E4C, enabled border #3C4959, hover #525E6F), so that the border/shadow look holds in both themes.
14. As a Full-timer, I want the input text to inherit the app's font (not Lexend), so that the control stays consistent with the rest of the product.
15. As any user, I want the existing placeholder "Search or jump to…" unchanged, so that copy matches design direction B.
16. As any user, I want the existing search scope (People, Conversations, Coordination Notes, History) and frecency ranking unchanged.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Scope: restyle only.** Desktop trigger + dropdown surface + ⌘K pill in `GlobalSearch.tsx`; the TopNav wrapper width; nothing in `commands.ts`, frecency, search logic, routes, or the mobile overlay. Current palette coverage is the definition of "everything" — no new commands or search scopes.
- **Trigger shape**: `rounded-full` h-10 pill → `rounded-2xl` (16px) with always-on inset outline. Border states are inset box-shadows (no layout shift): enabled `inset 0 0 0 1px #9AA8BC` (light) / `#3C4959` (dark), hover `#525E6F` (both themes), focus `inset 0 0 0 2px` in the app's accent violet (light `#5C17E5` = design; dark `#9A8FFF` per the app's `.dark` accent convention). Background is the surface/panel token (white light, `#27313F` dark), matching the design's `--background-primary`.
- **Width**: fixed 300px, owned by the `GlobalSearch` root (component-level, not the TopNav wrapper) so it is testable; TopNav wrapper stops constraining.
- **⌘K pill**: inside the trigger, absolutely positioned `right:12px`, vertically centered, `pointer-events:none`; 20px tall, `0 6px` padding, `rounded-lg` (8px), background-secondary (`bg-background`), 1px outline-variant border, 12px/500 secondary text. Visible while the query is empty; replaced by the existing clear × while typing (the input keeps its reserved right padding).
- **Dropdown surface**: `bg-surface` (white light), `rounded-3xl` (24px), `0 8px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.16)` elevation (replaces `shadow-2xl`), keep `border-outline-variant`. Row hover → `rgba(203,212,225,0.2)` (design neutral-20-20, same in dark per `.sh-dark`); selected row keeps the existing `bg-surface-container-highest` treatment.
- **Font**: inherit the app font — no Lexend import (size/weight via existing input typography).
- **Dark mode**: uses existing app tokens + arbitrary-value classes; the only new plumbing is one CSS variable for the enabled-outline color (`--gs-outline`: `#9AA8BC` light, `#3C4959` dark), following the app's existing token pattern.

## Testing Decisions

- **What makes a good test**: assert the observable contract — which affordances render in which state (⌘K pill when empty, clear × when typing), the trigger's fixed width and radius classes, the inset-outline/focus-ring classes, and the dropdown's elevation/radius classes. Class-level assertions are the agreed seam for geometry in jsdom; pixel rendering is verified by a browser smoke check during implementation, not by unit tests.
- **One seam**: extend the existing `src/test/GlobalSearch.test.tsx` (already covers ⌘K open, role gates, filtering, Esc, quick actions, clear, frecency — prior art for this component). New "visual contract" describe block. `commands.test.ts` untouched. No new test seams; no e2e additions.
- The `container.closest('.relative.w-full.h-10')` helper in the existing focus/clear test must be updated to the new trigger classes.

## Out of Scope

- New commands or expanded search scope (prayer burdens, Settings, impersonation, feedback) — current coverage is "everything".
- Font change (no Lexend import).
- Mobile search overlay changes.
- Modal/persistent-input interaction changes — ⌘K open behavior is unchanged.
- Global design-token migration beyond what the search needs.
- The `localeCompare` crash half of feedback #354 (separate bug; the restyle addresses the "no background border" half).

## Further Notes

- Design source: `tmp/cisa-design/Shell - 3 directions.html`, direction B (PICKED 18 Aug) — `shell/sh-b.jsx`, `shell/shell.css`, Bento tokens (`radius-8/16/24`, `--shadow-outline-input-*`, `--shadow-elevation-medium`, neutral-20-20).
- Feedback #354 (closed) documents the "no background border" wart this addresses.
- #19 (closed) was the original Global Search (⌘K) overhaul; #337/#328 built the command registry + frecency.
- The app already runs Bento tokens in `src/index.css` (light + `.dark`), so most design values map onto existing tokens.

title: Remove interactions with undo (web Conversations + mobile Story)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

Staff log follow-up conversations with contacts, but once an interaction is logged there is no way to remove it from any surface. The web Conversations tab in the contact detail is edit-only; the mobile Story tab is read-only (the v2 redesign deliberately dropped the v1 delete affordance). Wrong-person entries, duplicates, and mis-worded records are permanent. The underlying data-layer helper (`deleteInteraction`) and the Firestore permission rule both exist but have no call sites, and the mobile wrapper is dead code.

## Solution

The person who logged an interaction — or any Trainee/Full-timer — can remove it from a contact's Conversations (web) / Story (mobile) list. Removal takes effect in the UI immediately, with a short Undo window; the deletion (and its audit entry) commits only when the window expires. Undo restores the entry in place. No Firestore schema or rules changes; the existing owner-or-manager rule is kept and finally exercised. Contact activity stamps and interaction-created tasks are untouched.

## User Stories

1. As a Trainee who logged an interaction by mistake, I want to remove it from the contact's Conversations log, so that incorrect entries do not stay in the record.
2. As the staff member who logged an interaction, I want an Undo affordance immediately after removal, so that an accidental removal can be reversed.
3. As a Trainee, I want to remove an interaction on a contact I manage even if I did not log it, so that I can keep the record clean on contacts in my care.
4. As a Full-timer, I want to remove any interaction on any contact, so that I can clean up junk entries team-wide.
5. As a Community member, I want no remove affordance on any interaction, so that viewer access stays strictly read-only.
6. As a Student, I want the remove affordance only on interactions I logged myself, so that my read/write role boundaries are preserved.
7. As a Trainee, I want the removed interaction to disappear from the list immediately, so that the mistake is visibly gone without waiting.
8. As a Trainee, I want an Undo action that restores the interaction with its original content, type, date, author, and position in the list, so that a mis-tap costs nothing.
9. As a Trainee, I want the interaction to stay gone once the Undo window passes, so that a stale "deleted" state never lingers.
10. As a Trainee, I want removal to keep working when I navigate away from the contact before the window expires, so that the delete still commits.
11. As a Full-timer, I want the removal to appear in the contact's History as "deleted an interaction for", so that the audit trail records who removed what and when.
12. As a Trainee, I want the History entry to appear only when the deletion actually commits, so that an undone removal does not leave a false "deleted" record.
13. As a Trainee, I want an explicit confirmation when the interaction has an Alongside conversation thread, so that I am warned the thread will no longer be reachable.
14. As a Trainee, I want thread messages themselves left in storage when their interaction is removed, so that no team discussion is destroyed by removing a log entry.
15. As a Trainee, I want to-dos created from an interaction to survive its removal, so that an actionable follow-up is never deleted as a side effect.
16. As a Full-timer, I want the contact's "last contacted" stamps (lastSeen/lastContactedDate) unchanged by a removal, so that deleting a stray entry does not rewrite relationship history.
17. As a Full-timer, I want a contact whose only recent interaction was removed to naturally show as stale, so that the prayer list's stale badge stays truthful.
18. As a Trainee, I want the removed interaction gone from "Lately", "Every conversation", the attention feed, and global search immediately, so that no surface resurrects the deleted entry.
19. As a Trainee, I want a failed removal (e.g. lost permission) to restore the row and show an error message, so that a failed delete is never silent.
20. As a Trainee, I want no remove affordance on visit-mirror interactions (the `visit_<id>` copies), so that visit records keep a single management path through the Visits flow.
21. As a Trainee, I want the remove affordance hidden while that row is being edited, so that edit and delete cannot race on the same entry.
22. As a Trainee, I want a deep link to a removed interaction to open the contact normally without an error, so that stale links degrade gracefully.
23. As a Spanish-speaking user, I want all new copy (remove, undo, confirmation, errors) translated, so that the feature is not an untranslated island.
24. As a Trainee, I want the same removal behavior on web and mobile, so that I am not surprised by platform differences.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Hard delete, no schema or rules change.** Deletion commits with `deleteDoc` on the existing `contacts/{contactId}/interactions/{interactionId}` path. The existing owner-or-manager rule (`existing().userId == request.auth.uid || isManager()`) is kept as-is. No `deletedAt` field.
- **Delayed-commit undo (5 s window), not immediate delete + re-create.** The row leaves the UI instantly; the `deleteDoc` and audit entry fire only when the window expires. Undo cancels the pending commit, so the document id and `createdAt` are untouched. This deliberately avoids the board-docs soft-delete trash pattern (the interaction update rule does not permit a `deletedAt` field, and no Trash surface exists for interactions) and avoids re-create semantics (a fresh `createdAt` would re-flag the contact as newly touched in last-touch/attention queries). Deviation from the coordination-notes convention is intentional and documented in Further Notes.
- **Session-scoped pending registry.** Pending deletions live in a module-level in-memory registry keyed by interaction id, so navigating away (or closing the modal) does not cancel the commit; only explicit Undo cancels. Multiple pending removals run independent timers. App kill within the window leaves the interaction intact — benign, accepted.
- **Audit entry on commit only.** On window expiry the platform layer writes `logActivity({ action: 'deleted an interaction for', … })`, continuing the existing audit-action vocabulary ('logged an interaction for', 'updated an interaction for'). Undone removals write nothing.
- **UI gating mirrors the rule**: the remove affordance is visible to the interaction's `userId` or a Trainee/Full-timer; hidden for everyone else. Note: the existing web Edit affordance is stricter (owner-or-admin); that pre-existing gate is intentionally unchanged.
- **Thread warning.** When the interaction has thread messages, removal requires an explicit confirmation stating the message count will no longer be visible. Thread docs are not deleted and are not migrated to contact-level.
- **No cascade.** Contact activity stamps (`lastSeen`/`lastContactedDate`/`lastContactedById`) are not recomputed; todos keep their `sourceInteractionId`/title; attention-feed rows referencing the removed interaction simply stop resolving. The prayer stale badge reacts naturally via its existing interaction subscription.
- **Visit mirrors excluded.** The remove affordance is hidden on interaction ids matching the `visit_<id>` mirror pattern — those are owned by the Visits flow (`deleteVisit` already cascades its mirror).
- **Shared core unchanged.** `packages/core` `deleteInteraction` keeps its `deleteDoc` contract; the pending-commit registry and audit composition live in the platform wrappers (web modal handler; the mobile wrapper's dead `deleteInteraction` is wired into `useContactDetailData` and becomes live). No new core module.
- **Undo UI reuses existing primitives**: web `UndoSnackbar` + `useUndoSnack` (already shared with coordination notes); mobile `Snackbar` (built for the v1 delete-with-undo).
- **i18n**: all new copy lands in the web `src/locales` and mobile dictionaries; the `check:i18n` CI guard applies.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts external behavior only: affordance visibility per role, remove takes the row out of the list, undo brings it back in place, window expiry commits the delete and the audit entry, the thread-confirmation gate, and the failed-delete restore path. Data-layer calls are mocked at the component seams; timers use fake timers for the 5 s window. Three seams, each existing:

1. **Web component test** — `ContactDetailsModal.test.tsx`. Prior art: interaction add/edit rendering, contact delete-confirm-abort, `logActivity` assertions, role-gated access tests. Mocks `src/lib/firebase` (`logActivity`, `handleFirestoreError`) and Firestore writes. Covers stories 1, 2, 4-13, 15-21, 23, 24 on web.
2. **Mobile component test** — `apps/mobile/src/components/contact/ContactScreen.test.tsx`. Prior art: renders interactions through the mocked `useContactDetailData` hook (which gains a `deleteInteraction` entry); jest fake timers drive the undo window. Covers the same stories on mobile (Story tab), including the deep-link and thread-warning paths.
3. **Rules test** — the interactions describe block in `src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts` (currently create-validation only). Add delete cases: owner allowed, Trainee/Full-timer allowed, non-owner non-manager denied, unauthenticated denied. The rule is unchanged; this locks the contract the UI now relies on.

No e2e additions: the Playwright suite targets journeys, and the 5 s undo window is timing-hostile to deterministic e2e; component tests cover the full contract. A Maestro flow for mobile undo is a possible follow-up, not part of this spec.

## Out of Scope

- Soft-delete / trash / archive surface for interactions, and any purge job
- Cascading thread-message deletion or migrating threads to contact level
- Recomputing contact activity stamps (`lastSeen`/`lastContacted*`) after deletion
- Bulk / multi-select removal
- Changing the pre-existing web Edit gate (owner-or-admin) or any Firestore rules
- Removing visits or their mirrors through this UI

## Further Notes

- Web list order is by `dateTime`, so an undone removal restores the entry in its correct position (CHANGELOG #399).
- This restores the capability shipped and then dropped in the mobile v2 redesign (CHANGELOG "Interactions: delete-with-undo" #160/#161) and extends it to web for the first time.
- The delayed-commit undo is a deliberate departure from the board-docs soft-delete convention; rationale in Implementation Decisions. If audit-preserved removal later becomes a real requirement, revisit soft-delete with a `deletedAt` rule change and a Trash surface — treat that as a separate spec.
- CONTEXT.md gains a glossary entry for "Remove an interaction" with this feature.

## Problem Statement

const Icon = NAV_ICONS[href] ?? LayoutDashboard;
