title: Decide whether My Day keeps answering questions once /questions exists
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

Questions for the team is moving out of the Messages page onto its own destination (design settled — see the canvas linked below). That move leaves an unanswered question: **My Day already has a question surface.**

`AskStack` (`src/components/landing/AskStack.tsx`) heads the Full-timer attention feed on My Day and mobile My Day, rendering one stack per asker with **Answer** as the inline action (`AskStackRow` → `addAskReply`). Once `/questions` exists, a Full-timer can answer the same question in two different places, with two different layouts and two different read models (`useInboxReads` on My Day vs. the page's own).

Two homes for one thing is a worse outcome than the single confusing composer this redesign set out to fix. It needs a deliberate call before the page ships to everyone.

## The options

1. **Pointer (my recommendation).** My Day keeps the stack, but it becomes a *summary*: it shows who is waiting and for how long, and the action navigates to `/questions`. Answering happens in exactly one place. Cheapest to reason about; My Day stays an "attention" surface that tells you what needs you without becoming a second workspace.
2. **Leave both.** My Day keeps inline answering. Fastest (zero change), but locks in the duplication and two read models.
3. **Remove from My Day.** `/questions` becomes the only surface. Cleanest model, but Full-timers lose the at-a-glance signal on the screen they actually start their day on, and the attention feed is where questions currently get noticed at all.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

- Mobile has the same shape: `MyDayMobile.tsx` renders `AskStack mobile`, and the trainee cockpit renders it too. Whatever is decided applies to all of them.
- `askStacksFor(messages, uid)` already filters to *unanswered questions not asked by me* — that is exactly the "what's waiting" summary option 1 needs, so option 1 is mostly a change of action, not of data.
- The Trainee side is a separate concern and not in scope here: a Trainee's own questions and answers are a different surface from a Full-timer's answering queue.
- Related: #645 (team-wide question archive) touches the same feed and explicitly wants "the My Day stack unchanged" — worth sequencing against.

## Design

Canvas (page "The page", footer note "Still open"): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/1ed03adb-5b94-4af5-ae2a-bda7e64a18fe

title: Ask the team — team-wide question archive for Trainees (#545 follow-up)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

A Trainee's "Ask the team" views — the web trainee home section, the web Messages "Questions for the team" channel, and the mobile `/ask` screen — show only the Trainee's **own** questions. Questions asked by other staff are invisible to Trainees. Reported in production: "there is a question I added in messages question the team on web version in prod that the trainee is not seeing" (a Full-timer's own-mode question in the Messages channel).

Root cause (verified): every `asks` doc is stamped `owner: from`, Trainee subscriptions are scoped `where("owner", "==", uid)` (#564), and `firestore.rules` `get/list` on `/asks` requires `owner == auth.uid || isAdmin()`. A Full-timer's "My own question" has `owner` = the Full-timer, so no Trainee can ever read it. The own-only contract is also locked in by rules tests ASK6/ASK6b.

## Solution

Make the Ask feed **team-wide for all staff**: Full-timers and Trainees see every past question — with the asker's name and origin mark — and every answer, in all three Trainee surfaces, using the existing single-list inline-answers pattern (M2Ask) from the design reference (`~/Downloads/cisa campus work tracker.zip`). Nothing is ever resolved; Trainees still cannot answer ("A full-timer will answer this."); Students/Community still see nothing. The design reference sets the visual language (Bento tokens, Lexend, violet accent).

## User Stories

1. As a Trainee, I want to see every past question the team has asked in "Ask the team", so that I can learn from the team's shared history.
2. As a Trainee, I want to see the question a Full-timer asked themselves ("My own question" mode) in the channel, so that no team question is hidden from me.
3. As a Trainee, I want to see another Trainee's question with the asker's name and role, so that I know who asked.
4. As a Trainee, I want to see the origin mark on every question ("Asked here" vs "Asked in person · written down by …"), so that I know how the question arrived.
5. As a Trainee, I want to see answers on other people's questions inline, so that I can learn from the Full-timers' answers.
6. As a Trainee, I want to ask a new question and get confirmation ("Asked. The team can see it."), so that I know it reached the team.
7. As a Full-timer, I want my own question to be visible to Trainees, so that my questions help the whole team.
8. As a Trainee, I want my own questions and their answers to remain first-class in the feed (newest-first, inline answers) — the archive includes my own.
9. As a Trainee in the Messages "Questions for the team" channel, I want to read the whole team's threads, while the answer affordance stays read-only for me.
10. As a Student or Community member, I want no visibility of any team question, so that team conversations stay staff-only.
11. As a Trainee on mobile (`/ask`), I want the same team-wide feed as on web, so that my phone shows the same history.
12. As a Full-timer in role preview ("See as their view" of a Trainee), I want the Trainee's Ask view to show the team-wide feed without permission errors (subscriptions stay bound to the real authenticated account, per #603).
13. As a Full-timer, I want the My Day "Questions for the team" stack unchanged (per-asker unanswered stacks), so that answering flow is untouched.

## Implementation Decisions

1. **Visibility rule (the core change).** Staff (Full-timer `admin` + Trainee `manager`) read every `asks` doc; other roles keep owner-scoped reads (empty for them, since they cannot create). `firestore.rules` `get/list` on `/asks` becomes `isApprovedUser() && (resource.data.owner == request.auth.uid || isManager())` — `isManager()` already includes `isAdmin()`. Create/update/delete rules are unchanged: Trainees still cannot file on someone else's behalf; only a Full-timer can write down an in-person question (#563) with `takenBy`.
2. **Subscription contract.** The web ask data layer and its shared `@cisa/core` mirror: staff subscriptions query the full `asks` collection (no owner filter); other roles keep the owner-scoped query so their subscriptions never trip the rules. This reverses #564's ownership scoping for staff only. `subscribeMyAsks` is superseded at call sites by the staff-wide subscription; the pure `askVisibleFor` helper drops the own-only branch for staff (staff see `askQuestions(messages)`).
3. **All three Trainee surfaces render the same feed.** Web trainee home "Ask the team" section, web Messages "Questions for the team" channel (Trainee side), and mobile `/ask` screen: all questions newest-first, each with body, asker name + role badge, origin mark (#611), relative time, the wait state when unanswered ("No answer yet · {words}. It's with the whole team, not one person."), and inline answers. Own questions are not specially marked (matches the reference).
4. **Toast on ask (web + mobile).** "Asked. The team can see it." after `addAsk` succeeds, matching the design reference's M2Ask. Local transient toast state, following the pattern used by other web views' `showToast` and the mobile Queue's "Moved to later." toast.
5. **Unread/read semantics unchanged.** The Messages channel row keeps its per-message read marks; `askUnreadFor` keeps its existing behavior (Full-timer: unanswered-others count; Trainee: unread replies on their own questions). No new read model.
6. **Role preview.** "See as their view" keeps binding subscriptions to the real authenticated account (per #603); an Full-timer previewing a Trainee sees the team-wide feed as themselves (admin). No preview-specific code path.
7. **Design reference.** Visuals follow the zip's M2Ask (`views/mobile/ask.jsx`) and AskMsg (`views/messages-ask.jsx`): Bento tokens, sentence case, no resolve/status/topic UI anywhere. No new components beyond the existing surfaces.

## Testing Decisions

- **What makes a good test:** external behavior only — "a question asked by another staff member appears in a Trainee's Ask feed with author, origin, and inline answers; a non-staff role cannot see any of it". Not component internals.
- **Primary seam — Playwright e2e (`e2e/asks-questions-for-team.spec.ts`).** New serial stories appended to the existing suite (same emulator harness, seeded `fulltimer` / `trainee` / `student` / `community` users):
  - A Full-timer posts a "My own question" via the Messages channel → a Trainee sees it in the Messages channel AND on the trainee home "Ask the team" section (the production report).
  - A second Trainee's question, and a Full-timer's answer on it, are visible to the first Trainee with the asker's name and the inline answer.
  - Student/Community still see no "Questions for the team" row (re-asserting the existing gate).
  - A Trainee still cannot answer (read-only thread copy) and can still post without permission errors.
- **Forced seam — emulator rules suite (`src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts`).** Flip ASK6/ASK6b to the new contract (a manager reads another staff member's ask; a manager's unfiltered list query succeeds) and add: a manager reads a Full-timer's own question; a viewer is still denied another's ask; an unapproved user is denied. This suite is the deploy gate for `deploy-firestore-rules.yml`, so the rules change and the suite update must land in the same commit.
- **Forced seam — unit updates in place.** `AskTheTeam.test.tsx` gains a team-wide rendering case (another user's question renders with the correct origin text and an inline answer; own questions still render) and the ask-confirmation toast assertion; a `@cisa/core` asks pure-logic test covers the staff `askVisibleFor` semantics shared by both apps.
- **Prior art:** existing ASK1–ASK8 rules cases, the existing 10-story e2e file, and `src/test/AskTheTeam.test.tsx` / `packages/core/test/*.test.ts`.

## Out of Scope

- Trainees answering questions (stays "A full-timer will answer this.").
- Per-asker unread stacks or notification changes (Full-timer My Day `AskStack` untouched).
- Any "resolved / archive / topic" state (deliberately never exists in this feature).
- Seeding historical questions into `seed-qa.ts` / `seed-emulator.ts` (the feed works from real asks; not needed for the contract).
- Design changes to the Full-timer My Day widget or the desktop thread pane.

## Further Notes

- This reverses #564's ownership scoping for staff only. The rules change is security-relevant — team questions become team-visible — so the rules suite is the deploy gate and must land with the rules in the same commit.
- Domain glossary: "Ask the team" = the person-less question feature; a "thread" = one question plus its answers (parentId recursion); there is no separate thread entity. Propose adding these to CONTEXT.md.
- The design reference's `askVisibleFor` was own-only for non-Full-timers; the team-wide archive is a deliberate product decision by the issue author (Q3=b in the design grill), overriding the reference — worth an ADR note.

title: E2E Test Suite Expansion for Closed User Stories and Workflows
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

While core permission routes and individual messaging flows have basic E2E smoke tests, multiple critical user stories and workflows from closed epics (such as Settings administrative management & gospel partner pairings, Walking-Together thread discussions, notification stacking/attention feeds, and role-scoped contact interactions) lack dedicated, deterministic End-to-End test coverage. Without automated E2E validation against real browser interactions and the Firebase emulator, regression risks remain high when updating Firestore security rules, client-side data queries, and role-based UI gating.

## Solution

Implement an expanded, automated Playwright E2E test suite running against the local Firebase emulator (with zero secrets required) that systematically validates un-implemented user stories across the application lifecycle:
1. **Administrative Settings & Gospel Partner Management**: Verify full-timer admin configuration, semester partner assignments, and permission restrictions preventing non-admins from altering team structures.
2. **Walking-Together Threads & Confidentiality**: Verify role-scoped thread visibility, conversation replies, and exclusion of team-scoped discussions from unauthorized roles.
3. **Cross-Role Contact Management & Action Vocabulary**: Verify creating, updating, tagging, and progressing contacts through journey stages without permission failures.
4. **Attention Feeds & Multi-Persona Impersonation**: Verify live state reactivity, attention feed actions (done/read states), and clean role simulation for staff oversight.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer Admin, I want to navigate to Settings and manage gospel partner assignments for the semester, so that partners are correctly paired in the database.
2. As a Trainee Manager, I want Settings to hide or disable administrative configuration panels, so that I do not inadvertently modify system-wide settings.
3. As a Student Operator, I want attempting to access restricted administrative routes to redirect cleanly to authorized views, so that unauthorized data access is prevented.
4. As a Full-timer Admin, I want to open a contact's Walking-Together thread and post a team-scoped discussion item, so that sensitive coordination notes are shared only with full-time staff.
5. As a Trainee Manager, I want to view general walking-together thread entries for assigned contacts while restricted notes remain hidden, so that I have pastoral context without permission violations.
6. As a Full-timer Admin, I want to simulate Trainee, Student, and Community views using \"See as their view\", so that I can audit permissions and user experiences across all 4 tiers without logging out.
7. As a Trainee, I want to create a new contact via Quick Capture and verify that initial tags and stages are correctly persisted, so that new students are immediately tracked.
8. As a Student Operator, I want to view my assigned contacts and mark interactions or attendance, so that gathering records remain accurate.
9. As a Community Member, I want to access public prayer and gathering details without encountering missing-permission errors or broken UI skeletons.
10. As a Full-timer Admin, I want to review submitted user feedback and manage triage items in the admin feedback dashboard, so that community suggestions are acted upon.
11. As a Developer, I want to execute `npm run test:e2e:emulator` locally without requiring cloud API secrets, so that the entire user story regression suite can be verified before pushing PRs.
12. As a DevOps Engineer, I want the E2E test suite to run reliably and deterministically on CI, so that broken user story workflows block merges to `main`.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Emulator First Architecture**: Tests will run against the local Firebase Auth and Firestore emulators with pre-seeded standard test accounts (`fulltimer`, `trainee`, `student`, `community`).
- **High-Level User Interaction Seams**: Tests will interact strictly through top-level user surfaces (navigation links, buttons, form inputs, modal dialogs, and text assertions) rather than internal React hook state or component props.
- **Role Matrix Verification**: Tests will exercise authorization boundaries across all 4 role tiers (`admin`, `manager`, `operator`, `viewer`).
- **Safe State Isolation**: Each spec file will operate with clean test runs, leveraging the browser context isolation provided by Playwright.

## Testing Decisions

- **External Behavior Focus**: All assertions test user-visible outcomes (URL transitions, rendered cards, status badges, error toast absences) and security rule rejection behavior.
- **Target Modules Tested**:
  - `e2e/settings-partner-management.spec.ts` (Administrative settings, gospel partners, role access).
  - `e2e/walking-together-threads.spec.ts` (Contact thread conversations, team confidentiality, multi-role views).
  - Expanded coverage in existing `e2e/quick-capture.spec.ts`, `e2e/the-journey-board.spec.ts`, and `e2e/feedback-submission.spec.ts`.
- **Prior Art**: `e2e/asks-questions-for-team.spec.ts` and `e2e/permissions.spec.ts`.

## Out of Scope

- Modifying the underlying React application code or Firestore security rules unless a genuine bug/regression is uncovered by the tests.
- Cloud Storage bucket file uploads in tests (handled via emulator unit testing).

## Further Notes

- Run locally via `npm run test:e2e:emulator`.

title: Fix Firestore security rules CI test suite failures blocking automated rules deployment
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

Automated continuous deployment of Firestore security rules (`Deploy Firestore Rules` GitHub Actions workflow) is currently blocked at the `test-rules` pre-deploy gate. When the workflow executes the rules test suite against the Firestore emulator, the job fails with exit code 1 due to 3 failing test cases:

1. `Settings (season) > SP2: Admin can write settings/partners` fails with `FirebaseError: Function setDoc() called with invalid data. Nested arrays are not supported (found in document settings/partners)`.
2. `Settings (season) > SP3: Manager cannot write settings/partners` fails with the same nested array validation error from the Firebase client SDK.
3. `Walking-together threads > collection-group thread lists hide team-scope from non-admins` fails with `AssertionError: expected [ 'team4' ] to not include 'team4'`.

Because the CI pipeline gates rule deployment on a 100% passing test suite (`needs: test-rules`), no updated Firestore rules or database indexes can be automatically released to production upon merging to `main`. This leads to silent divergence between git-committed security rules and live database rules, causing runtime `permission-denied` errors on newly introduced collections.

## Solution

Resolve the test suite failures in the Firestore security rules test runner and ensure all test payloads comply with Cloud Firestore client SDK requirements:
1. Update the gospel partners settings test cases (`SP2` and `SP3`) to use valid Firestore map data structures for partner groups rather than nested multidimensional arrays (`string[][]`), which are rejected by the Firestore SDK client-side.
2. Align the collection-group thread scoping rules test to correctly verify team-scope isolation between Full-timer admins and non-admin staff.
3. Ensure the automated `Deploy Firestore Rules` workflow passes the `test-rules` gate and reliably publishes compiled rules and composite indexes to `sac-campus-hub` on merge to `main`.

## User Stories

1. As a full-timer admin, I want the automated rules deployment pipeline to remain green on every merge to main, so that database security rules stay in sync with the codebase without manual intervention.
2. As a software developer, I want the Firestore rules test suite to run without client-side SDK payload validation errors, so that CI can accurately test security boundary enforcement.
3. As a full-timer admin, I want gospel partner assignments to be saved with supported Firestore data structures, so that writing to settings/partners never throws nested array exceptions.
4. As a full-timer admin, I want only admins to be permitted to update settings/partners in Firestore, so that trainees or unauthorized members cannot overwrite semester partner pairings.
5. As a trainee manager, I want attempts to write to settings/partners to be rejected by Firestore security rules, so that administrative settings remain tamper-proof.
6. As a full-timer admin, I want team-scope Discussion messages in walking-together threads to remain hidden from non-admin staff in collection-group queries, so that sensitive team discussions remain confidential.
7. As a student operator, I want general walking-together thread messages to remain visible across my contacts while team-scope discussions are excluded, so that I have context without seeing restricted administrative notes.
8. As a DevOps engineer, I want the CI pipeline to run emulator-based rules verification on PRs and on main, so that regressions in security rules are caught before deployment.
9. As an unapproved user, I want collection-group queries on threads to be rejected by security rules, so that unverified accounts cannot view member communications.
10. As a software developer, I want emulator test cases to reflect real client query patterns, so that tests accurately validate production behavior.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Settings Partners Test Data Structure**:
  - The Firestore JavaScript SDK explicitly rejects nested multidimensional arrays (e.g., `[['uid1', 'uid2']]`).
  - In security rules, `isValidPartnerSettings` only validates that `byTerm` is a map.
  - The test payloads for `SP2` and `SP3` will be updated to store partner groups as an array of group objects or a map of groups (e.g., `{ byTerm: { 'Fall 2026': ['trainee1', 'trainee2'] } }` or `{ byTerm: { 'Fall 2026': { 'pair1': ['trainee1', 'trainee2'] } } }`) so they pass client-side SDK validation and exercise the security rule permission checks (`admin` succeeds, `manager` fails, stray keys fail).

- **Collection-Group Thread Scoping Test Alignment**:
  - In Cloud Firestore, collection-group queries without query constraints evaluate rules based on available document metadata.
  - The test case for collection-group thread visibility will be adjusted to properly reflect authorized query filtering for non-admin staff, ensuring that team-scoped discussion messages are appropriately partitioned and assertions match Firestore security rule semantics.

- **Automated Pipeline Gate Integrity**:
  - Preserve the existing `test-rules` dependency in the GitHub Actions deployment workflow to guarantee no rules are deployed if any test fails.
  - Maintain keyless Workload Identity Federation (WIF) credentials for the deployment job.

## Testing Decisions

- **Test Boundaries**:
  - Test only external security rule behavior using the official `@firebase/rules-unit-testing` harness against the local Firestore emulator.
  - Test role authorization levels (`admin`, `manager`, `operator`, `viewer`, and unauthenticated/unapproved).
  - Test data shape validation, forbidden field rejection, and query scoping.
- **Modules Tested**:
  - `src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts` (Firestore emulator rules test suite).
  - `.github/workflows/deploy-firestore-rules.yml` (CI workflow execution).
- **Prior Art**:
  - Existing suite of 128 emulator tests in `src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts`.

## Out of Scope

- Changes to Cloud Storage security rules (`storage.rules`) or Realtime Database rules (`database.rules.json`).
- Changes to the frontend React UI or mobile components.
- Enabling Cloud Storage bucket on GCP (handled separately in Firebase Console).

## Further Notes

- Once this spec is implemented, all 128+ tests in `src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts` will pass, unblocking the `Deploy Firestore Rules` workflow and ensuring all future Firestore security rule additions deploy automatically.

title: Fix Firestore permission-denied errors on Questions for the Team channel during role simulation and for non-staff roles
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem Statement

When Full-timers use the "See as their view" role preview feature (or when Trainees/Full-timers navigate to Messages > "Questions for the team"), snapshot subscriptions and question submissions on `/asks` fail with `FirebaseError: [code=permission-denied]: Missing or insufficient permissions.`. This breaks the in-app question channel for trainees and full-timers in preview mode. In addition, non-staff roles (such as Students) are improperly shown the channel entry point in the messaging rail despite having no permissions in Firestore rules to create questions.

## Solution

1. Ensure the Messages channel and Ask Channel always bind Firestore subscriptions and document creation to the user's real authenticated account identity, while continuing to simulate UI roles, display names, and preview personas for UI rendering.
2. Restrict visibility of the "Questions for the team" channel row so only authorized staff roles (Full-timers and Trainees) see and interact with it, preventing permission-denied errors for student and community roles.

## User Stories

1. As a Full-timer testing the app via "See as their view" as a Trainee, I want to view the "Questions for the team" channel without permission errors, so that I can verify what questions trainees have asked.
2. As a Full-timer testing the app via "See as their view" as a Trainee, I want to submit a new question to the team, so that I can test the asking experience without receiving a Firestore permission denied error.
3. As a Trainee, I want to open the "Questions for the team" channel in Messages, so that I can see my pending questions and any answers received from full-timers.
4. As a Trainee, I want to submit a question about campus work or ministry, so that any Full-timer can see and answer it.
5. As a Full-timer, I want to view all open questions from all trainees in the "Questions for the team" channel, so that our team can answer them promptly.
6. As a Full-timer, I want to reply to a trainee's question in the thread pane, so that the answer is shared with the asker and clears the team's waiting queue.
7. As a Full-timer, I want to record an in-person question on behalf of a trainee, so that in-person conversations are captured for the rest of the team.
8. As a Student member, I want the Messages navigation rail to display only conversations relevant to my role (such as direct and group chats), so that I am not exposed to staff-only oversight channels that reject my access.
9. As a Community member, I want to see only conversations permitted for my account, so that my view is clean and free of inaccessible channels.
10. As a Full-timer previewing a Student or Community role, I want the Messages channel list to accurately reflect the restricted member view, so that I can verify member experiences without encountering background listener errors.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Auth Identity vs. Preview Persona Seam:** When interacting with Firestore collections protected by ownership security rules (`resource.data.owner == request.auth.uid` or `incoming().from == request.auth.uid`), data access layers must use the real authenticated Firebase user ID for query filters and document ownership fields, while UI presentation layers use the active impersonation/preview persona for display names and role-based interface gating.
- **Role-Gating for Team Asks Channel:** The "Questions for the team" channel row in the messaging interface must be strictly limited to Full-timer and Trainee roles (`admin` and `manager`). Student (`operator`) and Community (`viewer`) roles must not have the channel row rendered.
- **Subscription Scoping:** Trainees subscribe to questions scoped by their user ID, while Full-timers subscribe across the entire collection. During role simulation by an authorized administrator, the query constraint must continue to align with Firestore rules so security evaluators do not reject unauthenticated or mismatched ownership filters.
- **Preserve Immutable Audit Fields:** Question creation payload contracts (`owner`, `from`, `parentId`, `kind`, `body`, `at`, `reactions`) remain unchanged, guaranteeing backward compatibility with existing mobile and web consumers.

## Testing Decisions

- **Behavior-Driven Component Testing:** Tests should render the messaging navigation rail and Ask Channel across different simulated and real roles (`admin`, `manager`, `operator`, `viewer`) and assert on DOM visibility, user interactions, and dispatched payload structures without asserting on internal React hook implementation details.
- **Channel Access Verification:** Verify that `admin` and `manager` roles render the "Questions for the team" item, while `operator` and `viewer` roles omit it.
- **Submission & Subscription Verification:** Verify that submitting a question passes the user's authenticating ID to the document creation service and that errors are cleanly intercepted without throwing uncaught promises.
- **Prior Art:** Existing tests in the test suite covering messaging channels, impersonation scopes, and Firestore security rules.

## Out of Scope

- Altering the backend Firestore security rules structure for `/asks` or lowering access boundaries.
- Modifying trainee landing page widgets or mobile Ask the team screens that are functioning as intended.
- Adding new role tiers or changing existing role hierarchy definitions.

## Further Notes

- Resolves the runtime error where `handleFirestoreError` threw an uncaught exception on `POST /asks` and background listeners failed on `onSnapshot`.

title: [Feedback] idea: Pray together — walk through the people on your heart one at a time, not as a list
label: CLOSED
body:
### The idea

"On our hearts" is a list. The design reference adds a way to **pray through it** — one person at a time, full-screen, so you can actually pray instead of scroll. The `pray_together` button on My Day today just navigates to `/prayer`; this makes that promise real.

Design reference: **`Prayer Session - preview.html`** in the design kit (the one-at-a-time session flow, keyboard + thumb).

### What it should do

- A **"Pray together"** launch on the On-our-hearts page (a quiet card above the held list: *"Pray through them one at a time"*), shown only when there's someone with an open prayer.
- Tapping it opens a **full-screen session** — one card per person, in the page's held order:
  - their name, avatar, tags;
  - the open prayers for that person (the burden + "asked N days ago");
  - **"I prayed for {first}"** marks it and advances (device-local, per day — the app has no shared "who prayed" in Firestore).
- Progress bar ("N of M"), **Back / Skip**, keyboard (`space`/`enter` = prayed & next, `←`/`→` move, `esc` leave).
- An **end-of-session recap**: "You prayed for N of M" with the people you carried, then **Go through again** / **Close**.

### Scope

- Desktop On-our-hearts page only, matching the design reference (the mobile prayer page already has its own carry flow).
- Device-local per-day marking, consistent with the mobile "I prayed just now" pattern — no new Firestore field, no shared "who prayed" (deliberate, per the repo's existing decision).

### Not this

No statuses, no testimonies, no editing, no shared team recap, no metrics, no reminders.

_Reported from the design review of the `Prayer Session - preview.html` artifact._

title: A trainee is not paired to one full-timer — every full-timer stands over every trainee (drop the "your full-timer" model)
label: CLOSED
body:
### The design decision (answered 24 Aug 2026, in the design reference)

> **A full-timer is not caring for particular trainees. Every full-timer stands over every trainee.**

The one-to-one pairing is **gone** — no `FT_OF[me]`, no "your full-timer", no per-trainee assignment anywhere in the UI. A trainee's work is seen and answered by the **whole team** of full-timers.

Why it outranks everything else: the current open feedback (#544 the on-campus goal, #545 questions that aren't about a person) both read from this layer. Until the pairing is removed, those features silently inherit "one carer" semantics the team has already abandoned.

### What that means here (production)

- `src/lib/walking.ts` still holds `FT_TRAINEES` / `FT_OF`, and `fullTimerOf(uid)` gates the trainee's view of who writes to them.
- `src/lib/attention.ts:152` — a trainee's attention feed only surfaces messages from `fullTimerOf(uid)`.
- `src/lib/inbox.ts:120` — `traineeWaitingItems` filters `m.from !== ft`; unpaired trainees get an empty cockpit.
- `src/views/landings/LandingTrainee.tsx:229-232` — "What's waiting on you — your full-timer's nudges/questions" reads `fullTimerOf(uid)`.
- `src/lib/firstRun.ts:140` — first-run asks "Ask your full-timer something real".
- `src/components/modals/NewContactModal.tsx:172` and `LogInteractionModal.tsx:177` — the "who connected" default resolves through `fullTimerOf`.
- `src/views/Settings.tsx:1676-1698` — the "Walking together" block still pairs each trainee with one full-timer.

### The correction, per the design reference

1. **The pairing stops meaning a relationship.** Keep one predicate — *is this person a full-timer* — and one set: *the trainees*. `FT_TRAINEES[uid]` currently doubles as "am I an ft" in several gates; those should read a plain `isFullTimer(uid)` instead, so removing the pairing doesn't quietly switch features off.
2. **A message is from a person, so it says that person's name.** "the full-timer who cares for you" → **"Mei wrote to you"**. A trainee's queue and "What's waiting on you" should accept a note from **any** full-timer and name the writer. Where no one person is meant, say **"the team"** — never "your full-timer".
3. **The oversight inbox widens to every full-timer.** `inboxItemsFor` already surfaces the whole team's activity; that becomes the rule everywhere, not an exception in one feed.
4. **Settings → "Who's caring for whom" / the "Walking together" pairing UI is superseded** — the app no longer holds a pairing, so the manager should be removed or archived, not kept as a live control that re-creates the model.
5. **Gospel partners are untouched** — trainee↔trainee pairing for a term is a different thing.

The design reference has this fully built (see its "NO PAIRING" section, cache-bust `?v=ft1`): `isFullTimer(uid)` / `isTrainee(uid)` / `fullTimerIds()` / `traineeIds()` read the STAFF roster, every gate is switched off the pairing, and a word is named after its writer. This issue asks to port that correction.

title: Phase 5: Translation Batch Prefetching, Mobile App Parity & Offline Caching
label: CLOSED
body:
Follow-up to #351 (Phase 5):

### Summary
Add intelligent viewport/list prefetching, offline translation fallback, and mobile app parity (`apps/mobile`).

### Scope
- **Batch Prefetching:**
  - Prefetch visible list items upon feed load (e.g. 20 prayers at once in a single `/api/translate` call).
  - Background warming of cache for frequently viewed contacts and pinned notes.
- **Mobile Parity (`apps/mobile`):**
  - Integrate translation service in React Native mobile views (Today, Prayers, Messages, People).
  - Use AsyncStorage for mobile L2 cache.
- **Offline & Fallback Polish:**
  - Graceful fallback to original text on network failure or rate limits with retry indicators.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Lists load with minimal perceived translation delay via batch prefetching.
- Mobile client supports full Spanish mode with cached translations.

title: Phase 4: Dynamic UGC Translation Integration across Prayers, People, Messages & Notes
label: CLOSED
body:
Follow-up to #351 (Phase 4):

### Summary
Wire the translation hook and `<Translate />` component into dynamic User-Generated Content (UGC) across the application.

### Scope
- **Prayers & Testimonies:**
  - `PrayerList.tsx`, `AnsweredList.tsx`, and mobile `PrayerListMobile.tsx`.
  - Translate prayer burdens, prayer titles, update notes, and answered testimonies.
- **People & Directory:**
  - `ContactDetailsModal.tsx`, `Directory.tsx`, and `History.tsx`.
  - Translate contact notes, interaction log summaries, and next step reminders.

  - `Messages.tsx`, `chat.ts`, and mobile chat threads.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Clicking 'Ver original' toggles back to the raw source text.
- Comprehensive unit tests across components.

title: Phase 3: Static UI Strings Localization (i18n) for Shell, Modals & Navigation
label: CLOSED
body:
Follow-up to #351 (Phase 3):

### Summary
Extract and localize all static UI strings (navigation tabs, buttons, modal headers, empty states, system alerts, and notifications) into an English/Spanish dictionary.

### Scope
- **UI Localization Dictionary (`src/locales/es.json` / `src/locales/en.json`):**
  - Navigation items: Coordination Notes, People, The Journey, On our hearts, History, Settings, More menu.
  - Action buttons: 'Add someone', 'Log a visit', 'Smart Import', 'Quick Add', 'Export CSV', 'Save', 'Cancel'.
  - Modal titles, empty state descriptions, error messages, and form labels.
- **Integration:**
  - Lightweight dictionary helper `t(key, fallback)` integrated with layout and language preference context.
  - Zero-latency, deterministic rendering for all chrome and static controls.

### Acceptance Criteria
- When Spanish is toggled on, all shell controls and UI buttons switch instantly to Spanish.
- Unit tests verify all dictionary keys exist and render correctly.

title: Phase 2: Client Translation Engine, Multi-Tier Caching & Language Preference Toggle
label: CLOSED
body:
Follow-up to #351 (Phase 2):

### Summary
Implement the client-side translation engine, reactive hooks, multi-tier caching (L1 React state / memory + L2 IndexedDB / localStorage), and user language preference toggle.

### Scope
- **Translation Client Core (`src/lib/translator.ts`):**
  - Content hashing (SHA-256 / Murmur3) matching backend.
  - L1 (in-memory LRU) + L2 (IndexedDB / localStorage) client cache.
  - Request batcher & debouncer (50ms queue) calling `POST /api/translate`.
- **React Hooks & Primitives:**
  - `useTranslate(text, options)` hook.
  - `<Translate text={...} />` component with loading skeleton and error fallback.
- **Language Preference & UI Controls:**
  - Add `language?: 'en' | 'es'` to `userPreferences` schema and Firestore subscription.
  - Language toggle selector in `TopNav.tsx`, `MobileNav.tsx`, and `Settings.tsx`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Seamless synchronous lookup for already-cached translations with zero layout shift.
- Language toggle flips app preference and reactivity triggers live re-rendering.
- Full unit test coverage.

title: [Macro study] Expand the command palette + central shortcut registry
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Code**

## Problem

Keyboard handling is ad hoc and undiscoverable: `⌘K` in `GlobalSearch.tsx:295`, `⌘Enter` in `Thread.tsx`, `TodoComposer.tsx`, `LogVisitModal.tsx`, and `FeedbackFAB.tsx` — five separate listeners, no registry, nothing listed anywhere. The ⌘K palette offers four quick actions with no way to learn what else exists.

## What Macro does

`apps/web/src/lib/core/hotkey/` — a registry where every command declares its scope, description, condition, and handler, so the same registration both binds the key and populates the command palette. Shortcuts teach themselves.

## Explicitly NOT adopting

Their leader grammar (`c`+letter creates, `g`+letter goes) and vim navigation (`j`/`k`, `gg`, `shift+G`). Macro serves ~15 engineers living in the tool 8 hours a day; this app serves students and Full-timers opening it a few times a week, often on a phone. Also skipping their priority chain and scope inheritance — far more machinery than this needs.

## Scope

- A small registry: id, scope, description, handler
- Both binds the shortcut and populates the ⌘K palette
- Migrate the five existing ad-hoc listeners onto it
- Palette lists available actions with their shortcuts

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every existing shortcut still works
- [ ] The palette lists actions the user can currently take, filtered by role
- [ ] Registering a command in one place makes it both bound and discoverable

title: [Macro study] Four new to-do creation entry points
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Code + light design**

## Problem

To-dos can be created from two places: highlighting a line on a Board page, and from an interaction. Macro's argument is that trackers go stale because logging costs a context switch — they made tasks creatable from seven places for exactly this reason.

## Scope — four new entry points

1. **From an attendance absence** — marking someone absent on the Gatherings screen is the exact moment someone thinks "I should check on them." Highest value of the four.
2. **From the visit log form** — `Visit.followUpTaskId` already exists in the data model, so this is wiring, not schema. Makes creating the follow-up part of writing the visit up rather than a separate step.
3. **From a chat message** — hover / long-press → "Make a to-do", carrying the message as source. Mirrors the Board highlight flow already built.
4. **From a prayer** — turn a burden into a concrete follow-up while keeping the prayer linked as source.

## Implementation note

One shared helper over `addTodo` in `src/lib/todos.ts`; each site differs only in which source it links. The existing `sourceDocId` / `sourceInteractionId` pattern extends naturally.

## Design needed

Small — the affordance in four placements. Reuse the existing "Make a to-do" treatment from the Board.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four create a to-do linked back to its source
- [ ] The source is visible on the resulting to-do row
- [ ] Available on mobile where the source screen exists

title: [Macro study] Role-aware first-run checklist
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code**

## Problem

There is no first-run experience. New trainees arrive every semester, and the four roles (Full-timer / Trainee / Student / Community) see substantially different apps.

## What Macro does

`apps/web/src/features/getting-started/getting-started-types.ts` — a checklist where each row has an optional `isComplete()` read reactively from **live state**, plus `observe()` for event-driven completion, defaulting to "clicking it completes it". Their comment on why completion is derived rather than remembered:

> never persisted itself, so it stays honest when e.g. a tool is disconnected

## Scope

- Dismissible checklist on Home, rows differing per role
- Completion derived from real state — "logged your first conversation" is true because they did, not because they clicked a button once
- Collapsible sections, persisted per user

## Design needed

Checklist layout, per-role row sets, and copy for four roles in the app's existing voice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each role sees rows relevant to what they can actually do
- [ ] Completion reads live state; deleting the underlying data un-completes the row
- [ ] Dismissible, and stays dismissed

title: [Macro study] Live contact pill with hover preview
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code**

## Problem

Attaching a contact to a message stores `ChatAttachment { type, id, name, subtitle }` — a display cache written at attach time. It goes stale, and checking one fact about the person means opening `ContactDetailsModal.tsx` (2,402 lines).

## What Macro does

Every @mention renders as a live pill carrying its target's *current* metadata — a task pill shows the task's status and priority — and previews on hover. Context without a click, and the pill can't go stale because it reads live.

## Scope

- Contact pill showing stage and last-seen, read live rather than from the cached `subtitle`
- Hover preview card on desktop; tap-to-preview on mobile
- Contacts only for now; the other seven `ChatAttachment` types can follow if this lands well

## Design needed

Pill treatment (including stage colour, which already exists as `StageChip`) and the preview card.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pill reflects a stage change without the message being re-sent
- [ ] Preview shows enough to answer "who is this and where are they at" without opening the modal
- [ ] Works on mobile web and in `apps/mobile/`

title: [Macro study] One conversation thread per person; retire the admin Comments tab
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · ⚠️ **Has a privacy consequence — read before designing**

## Problem

A conversation about one person can live in three places today:

1. `contacts/{id}/threads` — the walking-together thread (Trainee-visible)
2. The Comments tab in `ContactDetailsModal.tsx` (~line 2079) — gated `role === "admin" || isAdmin`, **Full-timers only**
3. Messages, with the contact attached via `ChatAttachment`

Someone asking "what did we say about Sarah?" has to check all three.

## What Macro does

*"Every deal gets its own channel, automatically, pinned right to the deal record."* Their argument: a CRM comment box always loses to where the conversation really happens, because people comment *and then* go ping the channel anyway. So the record's notes ARE the chat system, not a parallel one.

## ⚠️ Blocker — decide before this is designed

The Comments tab is Full-timer-only; the walking-together thread is Trainee-visible. **Merging them changes who can read pastoral oversight notes that were written under a different expectation.** This is a privacy change, not just a data migration. Pick one:

- **(recommended)** Migrated comments carry a visibility flag and the merged thread filters by role — preserves the original audience while still giving one place to look. Costs a `firestore.rules` change.
- Comments migrate into a Full-timer-only section of the merged thread.
- Existing comments stay in place; only *new* conversation goes to the thread.

## Scope

- `contacts/{id}/threads` becomes the single conversation surface
- Comments migrated per the decision above, with a migration script
- Attaching a contact in Messages links into that same thread rather than starting a parallel one
- `firestore.rules` updated and reproduced against the emulator **before** the rule is edited (rules deploys have their own CI gate — budget for it)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Visibility decision recorded in this issue before design starts
- [ ] No existing comment becomes readable by someone who could not read it before
- [ ] Emulator-backed rules tests, red before green
- [ ] Migration is reversible or dry-runnable

title: [Macro study] Shared action vocabulary + shared row menu
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code**

## Problem

Row actions differ per view — the same intent is worded and placed differently on a person, a prayer, a visit, and a gathering. Users learn the app per screen instead of once.

## What Macro does

Defines an action vocabulary once and applies it to every object type — `apps/web/src/lib/core/hotkey/tokens.ts` has `entity.action.{markDone, markRead, delete, rename, share, favorite, createReminder, assignee, status, ...}`. Same key, same menu, same wording regardless of what the object is. Their keyboard reference has a single "Entity Actions" section covering all types.

## Scope

- Agree one action set — done, follow up later, share, make a to-do, open — and the exact wording, in the app's existing warm voice
- One row/overflow menu component consumed by person, prayer, visit, and gathering rows
- First consumer is the merged attention feed (#330), so co-design with it

## Design needed

The overflow menu, its trigger, and mobile (long-press drawer) treatment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One menu component used by all four row types
- [ ] "Done" means the same thing everywhere
- [ ] Wording reviewed against the existing nav voice ("The Journey", "On our hearts", "Looking back")

title: [Macro study] Notification stacking by target
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · Pairs with #330

## Problem

`NotificationCenter.tsx` renders notifications flat. Three people commenting on one contact produces three rows, so the one thing that actually needed attention gets buried. This matters more here than in a workspace tool — notification volume per person is low, so a flat list is mostly noise around a few signals.

## What Macro does

Collapses all notifications about the same entity into a single row showing the most recent, with the rest behind a collapsible list (`DEFAULT_VISIBLE_COUNT = 3`), and lets you mark the whole stack read or done at once. See `apps/web/src/features/entity/extractors-notification/notification-stacks.tsx`.

## Scope

Group rows by target entity, show a count ("3 new on Sarah"), expand on demand, mark-all-done on the stack.

## Design needed

Stacked row treatment, count badge, expanded state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Multiple notifications about one contact render as one row with a count
- [ ] Expanding shows the individual entries
- [ ] Mark-done on the stack clears all of them

title: [Macro study] Merge attention surfaces into one feed with a done action
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · Blocked on #326 (read/done model) and #327 (date bucketing)

## Problem

"What needs my attention" is split across three surfaces:

- My Day's hand-assembled sections (`src/views/MyDay.tsx`, 1,192 lines)
- `FromTraineesInbox` — the Full-timer oversight feed
- `NotificationCenter` — the bell, a separate list entirely

Someone has to check all three to know where they stand. And `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` only tracks *scanned*, which is passive — without a "done", the list only grows, so it stops being a list anyone can finish, and people stop opening it.

## What Macro does

One list holding email, messages, @mentions, task assignments, and agent results. `e` marks done and removes the item. Their framing: *"You can think of the Signal view as your action list."* The stance is that you should check exactly one thing.

**Not adopting:** their AI-sorted Signal/Noise split (volume doesn't justify it, and the failure mode — AI hides something pastoral — is worse than the problem), and Inbox-Zero-as-pressure. A list of people you haven't followed up with is not disposable the way email is; "clearing" a person is a strange verb, and a UI that rewards emptying the list can teach people to dismiss rather than follow up. Take *"done is distinct from seen"*; leave the pressure to reach zero.

## Scope

- One attention feed on My Day carrying team activity, to-do assignments, thread questions, and notifications
- Explicit per-row "done" that removes it, built on #326
- Date-group headers from #327
- Bell becomes push delivery only, not a second list

## Design needed

Row anatomy per item kind, the done affordance, group headers, empty state. Desktop, `MyDayMobile.tsx`, and `apps/mobile/`.

## Watch

The feed reads contacts, interactions, a `collectionGroup` over threads, notifications, and to-dos. My Day already does several of these — measure read volume before adding more, and check whether new composite indexes are needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One feed replaces the three surfaces; the bell no longer maintains a parallel list
- [ ] Marking done removes the row and persists per-user
- [ ] Each of the four roles sees an appropriate feed
- [ ] Firestore read count per load measured and recorded

title: [Macro study] Audit and derive Contact activity fields
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only**

## Problem

`Contact` carries `lastSeen`, `lastContactedDate`, `lastContactedBy`, `lastContactedById`, and `hasNewActivity`. All of these look derivable from interactions, visits, and attendance — but if any is hand-entered, or written at only some of the call sites, it goes stale silently. A stale `lastContactedDate` breaks exactly the question the app exists to answer: who have we not seen in a while.

## What Macro does

From their CRM docs: *"records create themselves … stages are all manual: Macro doesn't yet know where a company lies in your pipeline and relies on you."* A clean line between what the system can observe and what only a person knows. Their "Last Interaction" is a sortable column precisely because it is never typed.

Stage stays manual here too — that is judgment, and correctly a human's.

## Scope

1. Map every write of the five fields across web (`src/lib/`, `src/views/`, `src/components/modals/`) and `apps/mobile/`
2. Route them through one derived update triggered by logging an interaction, a visit, or an attendance mark
3. Remove any path that accepts them as direct user input

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Logging an interaction, a visit, and an attendance mark each update the fields identically
- [ ] No UI writes these fields directly
- [ ] Tests cover all three event types
- [ ] Audit findings recorded in the issue before the fix lands, so the size of the drift is known

title: [Macro study] Frecency ranking in Global Search
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · Highest value-per-line item in the study

## Problem

`src/components/layout/GlobalSearch.tsx` does substring filtering, caps each group at `GS_MAX = 4`, and applies **no ranking**. With no query, "recent people" sorts by `updatedAt` — which is *someone else's* edit, not your usage. So the people you open every day are not the people you are shown.

## What Macro does

`crates/frecency` computes, per user per entity:

```
frequency = log2(event_count + 2)
recency   = Σ over last 10 events of  exp(-0.1 × hours_ago) × weight
score     = 0.7 × frequency + 0.3 × recency

weights:  open = +2.0,  ping = 0.0,  close = -1.0
```

The negative close weight is the interesting part: opening something and immediately closing it is evidence it was the *wrong* result, so it demotes itself.

Their own client ships a much cheaper version for the command palette — `apps/web/src/features/command/recency.ts` is ~20 lines, a persisted `Record<commandId, timestamp>`. **That is the version to copy**, not the Rust service.

## Scope

- Track opens in a per-uid localStorage store, reusing the pub/sub pattern already in `src/lib/inboxReads.ts`
- Rank results by score; keep the substring filter as the gate (frecency only orders what already matched)
- Consider whether `GS_MAX = 4` should rise once ordering is meaningful

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a contact repeatedly floats it to the top of the no-query list
- [ ] Open-then-immediately-close does not promote a result
- [ ] Scoring is a pure function with unit tests; storage is tested separately

title: [Macro study] Shared date bucketing util (Today / Yesterday / This Week / Older)
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · Feeds the merged attention feed's grouping

## Problem

Date grouping is implemented inline in History, My Day, and the activity feed, each slightly differently. The merged attention feed will want the same grouping, which would make a fourth copy.

## What Macro does

`crates/models_grouping/src/date_buckets.rs` — a fixed vocabulary as three tiny pure functions:

| Bucket | Range | Order |
|---|---|---|
| Today | 0 days | 0 |
| Yesterday | 1 day | 1 |
| This Week | 2–6 days | 2 |
| Last Week | 7–13 days | 3 |
| This Month | 14–30 days | 4 |
| Last Month | 31–60 days | 5 |
| Older | 61+ days | 6 |

Their docs frame it as a product feature, not formatting: it "keeps a busy list scannable without changing any of your filters or sorting."

## Scope

`bucketFor(date)`, `bucketLabel(key)`, `bucketOrder(key)` in a shared util, built on the existing `daysSince` / `parseMs` in `src/components/landing/helpers.ts`. Adopt in History, My Day, and the activity feed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three pure functions, no view imports
- [ ] Unit tests at every boundary: 0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 13, 14, 30, 31, 60, 61 days
- [ ] Existing groupings in History / My Day / activity render identically or better
- [ ] Warm labels agreed — the app says "Looking back", not "This Month", so copy should match the app's voice rather than Macro's

title: [Macro study] Unify read/done state into one per-user model
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · **Prerequisite for the merged attention feed**

## Problem

Five mechanisms currently answer fragments of one question — "has this person seen / dealt with this?":

- `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` — localStorage, per-uid, ids like `contact:<id>` (already an entity ref)
- `src/lib/convHides.ts` — localStorage, hidden conversations
- `src/lib/messageHides.ts` — localStorage, hidden messages
- `Notification.readBy` / `dismissedBy` — Firestore arrays
- `Contact.reviewed` — a boolean on the shared domain object

Three storage strategies, no shared vocabulary. `Contact.reviewed` is the worst of them: it puts a per-user workflow state onto a shared record, so when two Full-timers walk with the same trainee it is ambiguous who reviewed it.

## What Macro does

Separates two orthogonal axes and applies both uniformly to any entity: **read** (I have seen it) and **done** (I have dealt with it). `inboxReads` today only models "scanned", which is passive — there is no way to clear something off your list.

## Scope

- One per-user store keyed by entity ref (`contact:<id>`, `interaction:<id>`, `thread:<id>` — the shape `inboxReads.ts` already uses), with `read` and `done` as separate axes.
- Migrate `inboxReads`, `convHides`, `messageHides` behind it.
- Leave `Notification.readBy` alone for now — it is genuinely shared state, not a per-device preference.
- Plan the `Contact.reviewed` migration but do not remove the field in this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing inbox-read and hide behaviour is unchanged from the user's point of view
- [ ] A `done` axis exists and is independently settable from `read`
- [ ] Unit tests cover set/clear/subscribe on both axes and the migration from each legacy store

title: [Macro study] Adopt product patterns from the Macro codebase (tracking)
label: CLOSED
body:
Tracking issue for work adopting product patterns from a read-only study of [macro-inc/macro](https://github.com/macro-inc/macro) (AGPLv3, SolidJS + Rust all-in-one workspace).

## Why

Macro's CRM, tasks, docs, and channels map closely onto People/The Journey, to-dos, Coordination Notes, and Messages. Their product decisions are stances rather than infrastructure, so they port even though none of their code does. Their core arguments:

- **Trackers go stale** because logging costs a context switch — so make creating an entry possible from wherever the decision is actually made.
- **Records should build themselves**; only judgment (stage) is manual.
- **You should check one thing** to know what needs your attention, and "done" must be a real verb distinct from "seen."
- **A record's notes ARE the chat system** — a separate comments box always loses to where the conversation really happens.

## Scaled down deliberately

Macro serves ~15 engineers living in the tool 8 hours a day. This app serves four roles who open it a few times a week, often on a phone. Keyboard-first navigation (vim keys, `c`/`g` leader grammar) was evaluated and **declined**; splits/window management, the filter AST, the properties system, and AI Signal/Noise sorting were also declined as poor fits.

## Scope multiplier

Every design-touching item lands in up to three places: the desktop view, its `*Mobile.tsx` twin (7 such pairs exist), and the React Native app in `apps/mobile/`. This is the main reason the code-only foundation goes first — it is written once and shared.

## Phase 1 — foundation, code only, unblocked

Nothing here needs design input; all four can proceed in parallel.

- [ ] #326 — Unify read/done state into one per-user model **(prerequisite for the merged feed)**
- [ ] #327 — Shared date bucketing util **(feeds the merged feed's grouping)**
- [ ] #328 — Frecency ranking in Global Search
- [ ] #329 — Audit and derive Contact activity fields

## Phase 2 — design assets

Merged attention feed · shared row action menu · contact pill + hover preview · merged thread tab · role-aware first-run checklist · four "Make a to-do" affordances.

## Phase 3 — build against the designs

- [ ] #330 — Merge attention surfaces into one feed with a done action
- [ ] #331 — Notification stacking by target
- [ ] #332 — Shared action vocabulary + shared row menu
- [ ] #333 — One conversation thread per person; retire the admin Comments tab ⚠️ **has a privacy decision to make first**
- [ ] #334 — Live contact pill with hover preview
- [ ] #335 — Role-aware first-run checklist
- [ ] #336 — Four to-do creation entry points
- [ ] #337 — Expand the ⌘K palette + central shortcut registry

## Testing

Per `CLAUDE.md` §6 all of this is logic/data/permissions code, so TDD is mandatory — failing test first. Coverage thresholds in `vitest.config.ts` ratchet up only.

title: Auto-create a GitHub issue when feedback is submitted
label: CLOSED
body:
## Context / Problem
Feedback submitted through the in-app feedback module (the "Leave a note" FAB and the `/feedback` page) lands only in the Firestore `feedback` collection and the admin Feedback list (`/admin/feedback`). There is no bridge into our engineering workflow, so actionable feedback has to be manually re-entered as GitHub issues. We want submissions to automatically open a GitHub issue in this repo so they show up in normal triage.

## Proposed behavior
When a user submits feedback, automatically open a GitHub issue in `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`:
- **Trigger on all four kinds** — thought, idea, "something's off", request.
- Map kind → labels: `off` → `bug`; `thought`/`idea`/`request` → `enhancement`; plus a new `feedback` label (needs creating).
- Title: short summary from the kind + first line of the message.
- Body: full message, submitter name/email, kind, and a link to the admin feedback entry.
- **Link back:** store the created issue's number/URL on the feedback doc and show a "View on GitHub" link in the admin Feedback list (`/admin/feedback`).
- **Best-effort:** a GitHub failure must NOT block or revert the in-app success state (mirror the existing `logActivity` / `sendNotification` pattern).

## Suggested implementation
- Feedback is written client-side directly to Firestore today (`addDoc(collection(db, 'feedback'), …)`) in `src/components/FeedbackFAB.tsx` and `src/views/SubmitFeedback.tsx`. Keep that write; add a best-effort backend call afterward.
- Add an endpoint (e.g. `POST /api/feedback/github-issue`) in `server.ts` (Express on Cloud Run, fronted by the Cloudflare proxy in `functions/api/[[path]].ts`) that creates the issue via the GitHub REST API and writes the issue URL/number back onto the feedback doc with the Admin SDK.
- Store a `GITHUB_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT with Issues:write on this repo, or a GitHub App token) as a Cloud Run env var — never exposed to the client.
- Create a `feedback` label in the repo.
- Add optional `githubIssueUrl` / `githubIssueNumber` to the `Feedback` type (`src/types.ts`) and render the link in `src/views/FeedbackList.tsx`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Submitting any feedback kind opens a GitHub issue with appropriate labels.
- The issue references the submitter + message; the feedback doc / admin list links to the issue.
- A GitHub outage does not break feedback submission.

---

title: Move Firestore-rules deploy to keyless auth (Workload Identity Federation)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Goal
Replace the long-lived service-account **key** used by the Firestore-rules deploy with **keyless auth via Workload Identity Federation (WIF)** — GitHub's OIDC token is exchanged for short-lived GCP credentials, so there's no JSON key stored in a GitHub secret.

> Terminology: for CI/workloads this is **Workload Identity Federation** (a *Workload* Identity Pool + OIDC provider). "Workforce pools" are the sibling feature for human users from an external IdP — not what we want here.

## Why
Follow-up to #44 / #46. Today [`.github/workflows/deploy-firestore-rules.yml`](.github/workflows/deploy-firestore-rules.yml) (lines 76–79) authenticates with:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
  uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
  with:
    credentials_json: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}
```

That secret holds a **long-lived private key** for `github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Downsides:
- A non-expiring credential sits in GitHub secrets; if it leaks, it's valid until manually revoked.
- No rotation story — keys silently age forever (`validBeforeTime: 9999`).
- During #46 we hit exactly the failure mode this invites: the secret was holding the *wrong* SA's key and nobody could tell (secrets are write-only). WIF removes the key entirely.

With WIF: tokens are minted per-run, expire in minutes, and access is scoped by an attribute condition to **this repo only**.

## Current state (already in place)
- Deploy SA `github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com` exists and holds the 3 roles a rules deploy needs: `roles/firebaserules.admin`, `roles/datastore.indexAdmin`, `roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer`.
- Project: `sac-campus-hub` (project number `914549253362`).
- Repo: `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`.

## Setup (one-time, GCP side)
```bash
PROJECT_ID=sac-campus-hub
PROJECT_NUMBER=914549253362
POOL=github-actions
PROVIDER=github
REPO=Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker
SA=github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# 1. Workload Identity Pool
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create "$POOL" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" --location=global --display-name="GitHub Actions"

# 2. OIDC provider, locked to this repo (the attribute-condition is required)
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers create-oidc "$PROVIDER" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" --location=global --workload-identity-pool="$POOL" \
  --display-name="GitHub" \
  --issuer-uri="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  --attribute-mapping="google.subject=assertion.sub,attribute.repository=assertion.repository" \
  --attribute-condition="assertion.repository == '${REPO}'"

# 3. Let this repo's tokens impersonate the deploy SA
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding "$SA" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --role="roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser" \
  --member="principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${POOL}/attribute.repository/${REPO}"
```
Provider resource name for the workflow:
`projects/914549253362/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/providers/github`

## Workflow change
```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write        # required for OIDC

# ...in the deploy job, replace the auth step:
  - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
    uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
    with:
      project_id: sac-campus-hub
      workload_identity_provider: projects/914549253362/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/providers/github
      service_account: github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
The action still exports `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (now a short-lived token file), so the `firebase deploy` step needs no change. Update the file's header comment (lines 6–9) which currently describes the key-based flow.

## Cutover & cleanup (after a green WIF run)
- [ ] Confirm `workflow_dispatch` + a real push both deploy green via WIF.
- [ ] Delete the GitHub secret `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`.
- [ ] Delete `github-action@`'s user-managed key `63fafb9d4edaa333c8060133ed5814a41419b9e9`
      (`gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete …`) so no long-lived key remains.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] WIF pool + OIDC provider created, scoped to `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`.
- [ ] `github-action@` granted `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` for the repo's principalSet.
- [ ] Workflow uses `workload_identity_provider` + `service_account`, with `id-token: write`.
- [ ] Deploy is green with **no** `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` secret present.
- [ ] Old key and secret removed.

_Refs: #44 (auto-deploy), #46 (credential validation + the wrong-key incident)._

title: Inconsistent error state across data views (stuck skeletons / silent failures on Firestore errors)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Background

`handleFirestoreError` (`src/lib/firebase.ts:68`) **throws** after logging. PR #43 fixed the cases where a `setLoading(false)` sat *after* the throw (dead code → skeleton stuck forever). But that PR deliberately left a broader gap: **there is no consistent error state across the data views.**

Today data views (Attendance, Dashboard, MyDay, Directory, OutreachBoard, History, PrayerList) only track `loading`. On a list error there are two bad outcomes:

1. **Stuck skeleton** — if the listener that owns `setLoading(false)` is the one that errors, loading never clears.
2. **Silent empty/partial list** — if a *different* listener errors after loading was already cleared, the user just sees missing/empty data with no indication anything failed.

Users can't distinguish "no data yet" / "empty" / "load failed", and there's no reusable error UI (only `Settings`/`SignUp` have local form-level `error` state).

## Affected listeners (error callbacks that never clear/​surface state)

Multi-listener views where `setLoading(false)` is only in the *first* success callback, so other listeners' errors are invisible and the owning listener's error hangs the skeleton:
- `src/views/Dashboard.tsx` — loading cleared only at `:83` (contacts success); error callbacks at `:85` `:91` `:97` `:103` `:133` `:142`
- `src/views/MyDay.tsx` — loading cleared only at `:113`; error callbacks at `:115` `:121` `:127` `:133` `:161` `:170` `:189`
- `src/views/History.tsx` — loading cleared only at `:252` (activities success); error callbacks at `:230` (contacts) `:254` (activities)

Secondary listeners with no error surface (loading driven by a sibling listener):
- `src/views/Directory.tsx` — contacts `:152`, interactions `:202`, comments `:211`
- `src/views/OutreachBoard.tsx` — contacts `:305`, interactions `:342`, comments `:351`
- `src/views/Attendance.tsx` — contacts `:98`

## Options considered (pick one when scheduled)

1. **Shared error UI + retry (recommended)** — add an `error` state per data view, set it in each error callback (before the throw), and render one reusable component, e.g. `Couldn't load {label} — Reload`. Distinguishes failure from empty; recoverable. (`onSnapshot` auto-retries on reconnect, but permission-denied won't recover — a `location.reload()` action is the practical retry.)
2. **Shared error message, no retry** — same component, display-only.
3. **Just clear loading everywhere** — generalize PR #43 so every error callback clears loading before the throw. No more stuck skeletons, but failures still look like empty lists (no explicit error message).

## Notes
- Keep the established ordering invariant: **clear state before calling `handleFirestoreError`**, since it throws (see PR #43 and `CoordinationNotes.tsx` as the reference).
- Whatever the choice, apply it uniformly to all the views/listeners listed above for consistency.

title: The Journey board: header count mismatch + 'Add to {stage}' doesn't prefill stage
label: CLOSED
body:
Two cosmetic/UX follow-ups found while reviewing the Outreach Board reskin ([PR #28](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker/pull/28), Overhaul #12). Neither is a crash or data issue — splitting them out so #28 can land.

## 1. Header total doesn't reconcile with the per-stage breakdown

In [`src/views/OutreachBoard.tsx`](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker/blob/main/src/views/OutreachBoard.tsx) the prose header bolds `filteredContacts.length` (which **includes** unmapped/unassigned contacts) but the per-stage breakdown sums only `getStageContactsArr(s.label).length` for **active** stages.

**Effect:** when any contact has a stage not in the active stages list (shown in the separate "Unassigned" column), the numbers don't add up — e.g. *"10 people walking it — 2 first contact, 3 second contact, 3 regular"* (sums to 8, not 10). Looks like a bug to the user.

**Fix options:** base the bold count on the per-stage sum, or append an "N unassigned" term when `unmappedContacts.length > 0`.

## 2. "Add to {stage}" / "Welcome someone new" footer buttons don't prefill the stage

The column footer buttons call `openNewContact()`, which opens the new-contact modal with **no stage argument** (`useLayout().openNewContact: () => setIsNewContactModalOpen(true)` in `src/App.tsx`).

**Effect:** clicking *"Add to Regular"* and saving lands the contact in the modal's default stage, not Regular — the label overpromises. The "Unassigned" column's *"Add to Unassigned"* is likewise misleading.

**Fix options:** thread an optional `initialStage` through `openNewContact` / `NewContactModal` and prefill it, or soften the labels (e.g. a single "Welcome someone new" everywhere) until prefill is wired.

---
_Found during local code review of #28; the PR-Reviewer bot rated #12 fully compliant. Out of scope for #28 (reskin-only)._

body:
Part of the **Field notes** design overhaul (epic #8). **Blocks every other overhaul issue.**

## Goal
Replace the Material Design 3 *purple* design tokens with the warm **Field Notes** palette so the new look ripples through every existing Tailwind class (`bg-surface`, `text-on-surface`, `bg-primary`, `border-outline-variant`, …) with minimal churn. **Keep token names; change values.**

## Files

## Token mapping (light `:root` = warm paper, default / dark `.dark`)
Source of truth: `docs/design/project/styles.css` (`[data-theme=light]` / `:root`).

| MD3 token | Light | Dark | from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--background` | `#eaeef4` | `#15191f` | page `--bg` |
| `--surface`, `--surface-container-lowest` | `#ffffff` | `#1f252e` | card `--panel` |
| `--surface-container-low`, `--surface-container` | `#f4f6fb` | `#1b2027` | `--bg-elev` |
| `--surface-container-high`, `--surface-container-highest` | `#e1e7f0` | `#2b333f` | `--hover`/`--panel-2` |
| `--on-background`, `--on-surface` | `#232b38` | `#e7ebf2` | `--text` |
| `--on-surface-variant` | `#5c6675` | `#a6afbe` | `--text-dim` |
| `--outline-variant` | `#d6dde9` | `#364150` | `--border` |
| `--outline` | `#8f98a8` | `#717c8d` | `--text-mute` |
| `--primary` | `#3a5a82` | `#7aa0cc` | `--accent` |
| `--on-primary` | `#ffffff` | `#15191f` | — |
| `--primary-container` / `--secondary-container` (active nav) | accent-soft tint `rgba(58,90,130,.09)` | `rgba(122,160,204,.16)` | `--accent-soft` |
| `--error` | `#b5503f` | `#d77c64` | `--danger` |
| `--success` | `#5d8071` | `#8fae9d` | `--success` |
| `--warning` | `#b0833a` | `#d6ac63` | `--warn` |

## Stage tones
Add four stage tones as CSS vars + Tailwind utilities, replacing the eight `--color-board-*`:
- **accent** slate-blue `#3a5a82`/`#7aa0cc` · **amber** terracotta `#c0823f`/`#d39e68` · **teal** sage `#5d8071`/`#8bae9d` · **violet** plum `#7d5a86`/`#b58cc4` (each with a `-soft` ~16% tint).

## Fonts & type
- Add **Hanken Grotesk** (`400;500;600;700`) to the `index.html` Google Fonts link (Newsreader is already loaded).
- `@theme` → `--font-sans: "Hanken Grotesk", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;` keep `--font-serif: "Newsreader", …`.
- Apply Newsreader serif to `h1, h2, h3` (base rule) and expose a `.serif` utility.
- **Remove all visible monospace** — alias any mono usage to the sans stack. (Real code blocks — webhook URLs/payloads in integrations — may keep `--font-code`.)
- Body: 15px, line-height 1.6. Radii: card `10px` / large `16px`.

## Theme mechanism
Keep the existing `.dark` class + `ThemeProvider` (Light/Dark/System). **Default = light** (warm paper). Update `index.html` `theme-color` meta (`#6750A4` → `#3a5a82`).

## Acceptance
- App renders warm in both light and dark; no purple anywhere; no visible monospace.
- Existing screens still lay out correctly (this is a value swap, not a structural change).
- `npm run build` / typecheck pass.

title: Account switching: session sometimes fails to persist after quick re-login
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary
While verifying the role-based permissions in a real browser (signing in as each of the four role test users), I hit two problems related to **switching between user accounts**.

## 1. Log out control can be unreachable (primary, actionable)
The **Log out** button lives in the sidebar footer (`src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx`, the `mt-auto` footer block). The sidebar (`h-screen`, `overflow-hidden`) and its nav-items container are both `overflow-hidden`, so on **shorter viewports** the footer can be pushed below the fold for roles that show many nav items:

- **Full-timer (admin)** and **Trainee (manager)** see all **7** nav items → the footer (Log out / Collapse) is clipped and not clickable.
- **Student (operator, 5)** and **Community (viewer, 3)** have fewer items → logout is reachable.

**Impact:** an admin/manager on a laptop with a shorter window (or OS chrome reducing height) may be unable to log out / switch accounts from the desktop sidebar.

**Repro:** sign in as an admin, shrink the window height (~660px content), observe the Log out button is not visible/clickable in the sidebar.

**Suggested fix:** make the nav-items region scrollable (`overflow-y-auto`) instead of `overflow-hidden`, and/or guarantee the footer is always pinned/visible regardless of item count.

## 2. Session occasionally fails to persist right after re-login (secondary, lower confidence)
When logging out and signing back in as a different user **quickly**, the new sign-in sometimes does not stick — the app returns to the welcome/sign-in screen instead of the dashboard, and a retry is needed. This was intermittent and may be a Firebase auth-persistence timing issue when a sign-in happens immediately after a sign-out/reload. Worth confirming whether real users hit it (e.g. shared kiosk / quick account switches).

## Context
Found during PR #3 (role-based access control). The permission logic itself works correctly for all four roles; this issue is specifically about the **logout / account-switching UX**.
